title: Dujac Fils & Pere 2009  Morey-Saint-Denis

description: A bright, toasty wine, with the ripe fruits of the vintage and characteristics from the wood giving extra richness to this finely structured, mineral-textured wine.
title: Louis Latour 2009 La Garenne  (Puligny-Montrachet)

description: Still very closed up, this is a potentially rich wine with huge fruit flavors. It's sweet while still structured, with a dry core of spice and minerality. The future for this wine is good. Its richness will develop while always keeping structure. Drink from 2018.
title: Kuentz-Bas 2013 Pfersigberg Grand Cru Gewurztraminer (Alsace)

description: An off-dry character sets the scene for this concentrated, already balanced wine. The Hatschbourg vineyard in the southern Alsace village of Voegtlinshoffen is composed of clay and chalk soil on a southeast-facing slope. It gives exceptional ripeness, as here, a warm and full-bodied wine with great swathes of fruitiness. Drink from 2017.
title: Joseph Cattin 2013 Hatschbourg Grand Cru Pinot Gris (Alsace)

description: This single-vineyard wine is made from biodynamically grown grapes. It's rich while still stylish and fresh. Ripe apple fruit flavors are lifted by acidity and given a twist with spice, pepper and hints of tropical fruits. Drink from 2016.
title: Jean-Baptiste Adam 2013 Letzenberg Pinot Gris (Alsace)

description: This single-vineyard wine is made from biodynamically grown grapes. It's rich while still stylish and fresh. Ripe apple fruit flavors are lifted by acidity and given a twist with spice, pepper and hints of tropical fruits. Drink from 2016.
title: Jean-Baptiste Adam 2013 Letzenberg Pinot Gris (Alsace)

description: Farmed biodynamically, this wine has a pure fruit character, intense and mineral. It's on the sweet side, although the acidity allows good freshness into the mix. It needs to age, so drink from 2017.
title: Jean-Baptiste Adam 2013 Kaefferkopf Grand Cru Vieilles Vignes Gewurztraminer (Alsace)

description: Farmed biodynamically, this wine has a pure fruit character, intense and mineral. It's on the sweet side, although the acidity allows good freshness into the mix. It needs to age, so drink from 2017.
title: Jean-Baptiste Adam 2013 Kaefferkopf Grand Cru Vieilles Vignes Gewurztraminer (Alsace)

description: The biodynamic Letzenberg vineyard has produced an impressive wine that's rich and full in the mouth, packed with ripe white fruits, plums and lychees. A spicy texture gives a dry edge to what is otherwise a medium-sweet wine. Drink from 2016.
title: Jean-Baptiste Adam 2012 Letzenberg Pinot Gris (Alsace)

description: Plum, black cherry and fruit cake spice take center stage on the nose of this wine. Flavors of dried dates and crushed violets appear in the medium-weight mouth with a satiny texture, while the finish provides a touch of fudgy chocolate richness.
title: Hecht & Bannier 2007 Red (Minervois)

description: Plum, black cherry and fruit cake spice take center stage on the nose of this wine. Flavors of dried dates and crushed violets appear in the medium-weight mouth with a satiny texture, while the finish provides a touch of fudgy chocolate richness.
title: Hecht & Bannier 2007 Red (Minervois)

description: Tropical fruits and richly herbaceous flavors come together in this ripe, fruity wine. It has a citrus core along with a fine tang of orange zest and pineapple. Ready to drink.
title: Domaine Fouassier 2010 Les Grands Groux  (Sancerre)

description: Flavors of yellow fruit, peach and apricot are given a light burst of acidity and sent on their way with a mineral texture. This wine is all fruit at first, but with the apple skin edge, it needs a year of bottle age.
title: Domaine Fouassier 2010 Les Chasseignes  (Sancerre)

description: Firm and tannic, this balances its structural components with rich red-berry fruits. The wine is dense, the ripe fruit bursts in the mouth. It does need aging and would be worth keeping for 3–4 years.
title: Château Thieuley 2009 Réserve Francis Courselle  (Bordeaux)

description: From the southern slopes of Bordeaux's Entre-deux-Mers, this is rounded, fleshy and packed with plum and smoke flavors. It has the vintage's richness and the soft tannins, making it already drinkable.
title: Château Thieuley 2009 Clos Sainte-Anne  (Côtes de Bordeaux)

description: Packed with black plum and blackberry fruits, this is a firm yet ripe wine. It has wood, smoke and spice flavors that complement the fruit and tannins. Age for three years.
title: Château Mille-Roses 2009  Haut-Médoc

description: Very tannic and concentrated, this is a dry wine with a chunky structure and a dark, firm feel. Plum skin and black currant notes are behind the scenes; this wine needs at least three more years of aging.
title: Château Haut Gravet 2008  Saint-Émilion

description: Very tannic and concentrated, this is a dry wine with a chunky structure and a dark, firm feel. Plum skin and black currant notes are behind the scenes; this wine needs at least three more years of aging.
title: Château Haut Gravet 2008  Saint-Émilion

description: This shows the lean character that comes from the vintage. But it's balanced with juicy black-fruit flavors and soft tannins that are now maturing. This is attractrive for a light, ready-to-drink wine.
title: Château Béhèré Courtin 2007  Pauillac

description: French actor Gérard Depardieu, who has a vineyard in the Loire, has lent his name to this barrel-aged sparkling wine. It has great richness, and its fruits married with a more rounded, mature underlay and subtle acidity.
designation: Taille Princesse de Gérard Depardieu Rosé Brut
title: Bouvet-Ladubay 2008 Taille Princesse de Gérard Depardieu Rosé Brut  (Saumur)

description: This is showing some maturity with its ripe apple fruits and taut texture. Very dry, it is still rich and ripe enough to sustain the intense grapefruit and citrus finish.
title: Jeaunaux-Robin NV Extra Brut Grande Tradition  (Champagne)

description: This is showing some maturity with its ripe apple fruits and taut texture. Very dry, it is still rich and ripe enough to sustain the intense grapefruit and citrus finish.
title: Jeaunaux-Robin NV Extra Brut Grande Tradition  (Champagne)

description: Highly acidic Champagne, although also with some final sweetness. The wine is dominated by intense citric flavors, giving a mouth-puckering character. A year's bottle age might help.
title: G.H. Martel NV Brut Prestige  (Champagne)

description: With a typical cream and spice flavor, this rich Pinot Blanc is soft and flavored with ripe mirabelle and pear flavors. It is ready to drink, warm and accessible.
title: Domaine Léon Boesch 2009 Tradition Pinot Blanc (Alsace)

description: This is a smooth, yellow fruit-flavored wine that comes from a small area of the appellation. It has ripe apricot fruit and a toasty, creamy texture, giving it rich, full flavor. A light touch of textured minerality lifts the wine on the finish.
title: Domaine de la Denante 2015 Les Maillettes  (Saint-Véran)

description: This fine, perfumed wine is soft and stylish—a hallmark of the nonvintage Champagnes from this producer. It has plenty of red berry flavors and balanced acidity. Drink now.
title: Deutz NV Brut Rosé  (Champagne)

description: A dense wine, the wood just showing at this stage through its dark tannins and superb rich fruit. The wine is ripe, with a density of tannins that go right down deep. Big and powerful.
title: Clos du Marquis 2009  Saint-Julien

description: A dense wine, the wood just showing at this stage through its dark tannins and superb rich fruit. The wine is ripe, with a density of tannins that go right down deep. Big and powerful.
title: Clos du Marquis 2009  Saint-Julien

description: A superbly rich wine, with its acidity well integrated into the concentrated and rounded fruit. It has great texture and fruit that bursts from the glass. It is generous, warm and toasty, while also preserving the steeliness that is hallmark of the Les Clos vineyard. Age for at least five years.
designation: Clos des Hospices Les Clos Grand Cru
title: Domaine Christian Moreau Père et Fils 2009 Clos des Hospices Les Clos Grand Cru  (Chablis)
winery: Domaine Christian Moreau Père et Fils

description: With a structure that runs between acidity and dark smoky tannins, this is a wine with potential opulence. It's very rich in character, dense and dark. The black plum flavors are dominant, along with excellent acidity. For the long-term.
title: Château Pichon Longueville 2009  Pauillac

description: A hugely rich, powerful Chardonnay, layering ripe fruit with a core of tannic structure, acidity, wood and huge depth of flavor. The wine is concentrated, with layers of fruit and textured acidity. Of course, it needs aging—7 years at least.
title: Louis Jadot 2009  Corton-Charlemagne

description: A hugely rich, powerful Chardonnay, layering ripe fruit with a core of tannic structure, acidity, wood and huge depth of flavor. The wine is concentrated, with layers of fruit and textured acidity. Of course, it needs aging—7 years at least.
title: Louis Jadot 2009  Corton-Charlemagne

description: Enormous tannins, dominant black fruit and a solid, dense structure. The wine, packed with dark fruits, dry tannins, very firm in character. With its huge tannins as well as fruit, this is a wine that really needs many years of aging.
title: Château Montrose 2009  Saint-Estèphe

description: Enormous tannins, dominant black fruit and a solid, dense structure. The wine, packed with dark fruits, dry tannins, very firm in character. With its huge tannins as well as fruit, this is a wine that really needs many years of aging.
title: Château Montrose 2009  Saint-Estèphe

description: A beautifully structured wine, with its tannins layered between the ripest black plums, damsons and black currants. It is opulent while remaining dense, concentrated and very serious. Certainly a wine for long-term aging.
title: Château Léoville Las Cases 2009  Saint-Julien

description: Full in the mouth, this is a tight, caramel and red fruit flavored wine. It has tang and a textured character that suggests a light amount of tannin. With this nervy, mineral character, the wine could do with some aging. so wait a few months.
title: Domaines Ott 2012 Clos Mireille Rosé (Côtes de Provence)

description: A full, earthy, warm wine that has a strong herbal character as well as rich caramel and red fruits. It has a rare density for a rosé, textured and ripe. Try aging this wine for a  few months.
title: Domaine les Fouques 2012 Cuvée de l'Aubigue Rosé (Côtes de Provence)

description: Modern style of wine, with hints of polished wood, mint flavors and a strong sense of structure. Along with the blackberry fruit, still showing no signs of age, the wine has concentration and elegance. It's a wine for more aging over another 4–5 years.
title: Château Moulin de Grillet 2005 Les Ailes du Moulin  (Premieres Côtes de Blaye)

description: The top rosé cuvée from Léoube is full and rich. Find its generous red plum and berry fruits well encased in a complex structure. A touch of vanilla goes well with the final acidity.
title: Château Léoube 2012 Secret de Léoube Rosé (Côtes de Provence)

description: The top rosé cuvée from Léoube is full and rich. Find its generous red plum and berry fruits well encased in a complex structure. A touch of vanilla goes well with the final acidity.
title: Château Léoube 2012 Secret de Léoube Rosé (Côtes de Provence)

description: This wine, produced by the team of Château du Glana, is big, bold, solid and very firmly structured. With weight, richness, black plum skins and dark tannins, it's a fine wine for aging, so give it at least 6–7 years.
title: Château du Glana 2010 Terre du Lion  (Saint-Julien)

description: Satisfyingly ripe wine, now approaching maturity. It has just the right weight from the black currant fruits, the more mature leather texture and the firm tannins that give a dry core. The wine could age for several more years, but is ready to drink now.
title: Château Crusquet de Lagarcie 2008  Premieres Côtes de Blaye

description: This wine is still firm, only hinting at its potential. The weight is there as well as the rich fruitiness. Give this wine a few months to bring out the generous fruit and texture. Drink from 2017.
title: Yves Giroux 2014 Les Raidillons  (Pouilly-Fuissé)

description: Very recognisably Pinot Noir, even if not Burgundian, this is an earthy wine that is full of spice and secondary, mature flavors. It is rich and impressively full while keeping the perfumed Pinot character. The wine, from a portion of the Château Montus vineyard, is ready to drink.
title: Vignobles Brumont 2009 Le Pinot Noir d'Alain Brumont Pinot Noir (Vin de France)

description: Very recognisably Pinot Noir, even if not Burgundian, this is an earthy wine that is full of spice and secondary, mature flavors. It is rich and impressively full while keeping the perfumed Pinot character. The wine, from a portion of the Château Montus vineyard, is ready to drink.
title: Vignobles Brumont 2009 Le Pinot Noir d'Alain Brumont Pinot Noir (Vin de France)

description: Aged in wood, this wine is ripe, with a smoky character from the toastiness. Next to the spice, the red currant and berry fruits are intensely fresh and disclose a tight line of acidity. The wine is still young, although developing well as the acidity softens. It will be ready to drink from 2018.
title: Domaine Arnoux Père et Fils 2014 Les Beaumonts  (Chorey-lès-Beaune)

description: Lively and fresh, this wine offers apples, citrus and warmer pears. The juicy fruitiness is immediately attractive, perfumed and bright at the end. Drink now.
title: Pierre Vessigaud 2014 Vielles Vignes  (Pouilly-Fuissé)

description: Lively and fresh, this wine offers apples, citrus and warmer pears. The juicy fruitiness is immediately attractive, perfumed and bright at the end. Drink now.
title: Pierre Vessigaud 2014 Vielles Vignes  (Pouilly-Fuissé)

description: The cool character of this under-rated appellation is apparent in this red-currant-dominated wine. With a fresh streak of acidity, the wood and spice flavors are contained and balanced. The wine will be ready to drink from 2018.
title: Patriarche Père et Fils 2013 En Caradeux Premier Cru  (Pernand-Vergelesses)

description: The cool character of this under-rated appellation is apparent in this red-currant-dominated wine. With a fresh streak of acidity, the wood and spice flavors are contained and balanced. The wine will be ready to drink from 2018.
title: Patriarche Père et Fils 2013 En Caradeux Premier Cru  (Pernand-Vergelesses)

description: Full and structured, this has a spice note and a firm feel. Only on the finish does a more creamy character show. A few months bottle age would be a great benefit.
title: Bott Frères NV Cuvée Q.V. Paul Brut Sparkling (Crémant d'Alsace)

description: Rich and spicy wine, this has a smooth character. Just beginning to soften, it feels ripe and full, bearing a white currant flavor, with a pinch of nutmeg.
title: Bott Frères 2010 Cuvée Particulière Pinot Gris (Alsace)

description: Rich and spicy wine, this has a smooth character. Just beginning to soften, it feels ripe and full, bearing a white currant flavor, with a pinch of nutmeg.
title: Bott Frères 2010 Cuvée Particulière Pinot Gris (Alsace)

description: Warm and fruity, this has an open apricot flavor that's balanced by spice and vanilla from the wood aging. Citrus flavors give a fresh, more medicinal finish.
title: Domaine Ellevin 2009  Chablis

description: The palest pink in color, this wine is light and easy with the merest hint of fruitiness and acidity. Red currant and lime mark the finish.
title: Château Maupague 2015 Cabaret Rosé (Côtes de Provence)

description: With earthy, rustic aromas that translate onto the palate, this wine seems to miss out on some of the fruitiness normally associated with rosés. A few more months in bottle may help.
title: Château Coussin 2015 La Croix du Prieur Rosé (Côtes de Provence)

description: This blend of Sauvignon Blanc and Grenache Blanc is light and fresh. Gently fruity, hinting at herbs and citrus and with an easy, open texture, it is a soft quaffing wine. The aftertaste is lightly sweet.
title: Belle Made For You NV White (Vin de France)

description: This blend of Sauvignon Blanc and Grenache Blanc is light and fresh. Gently fruity, hinting at herbs and citrus and with an easy, open texture, it is a soft quaffing wine. The aftertaste is lightly sweet.
title: Belle Made For You NV White (Vin de France)

description: Lush scents of vanilla bean, raspberry sauce and cherry syrup show on the nose of this ripely fruited Pinot. The palate is light and direct, with virtually no tannic structure. A fleeting finish follows short flavors of juicy red plum and blueberry.
title: Café du Midi 2015 Pinot Noir (Vin de France)

description: Lush scents of vanilla bean, raspberry sauce and cherry syrup show on the nose of this ripely fruited Pinot. The palate is light and direct, with virtually no tannic structure. A fleeting finish follows short flavors of juicy red plum and blueberry.
title: Café du Midi 2015 Pinot Noir (Vin de France)

description: In its distinctive Provence skittle bottle, this wine conveys a warm seaside feel. It is soft with a touch of caramel and flavors of wild strawberries and cream. The acidity at the end is what makes this wine, giving it the refreshing character it needs.
title: Maison Belle Claire 2015 Rosé (Côtes de Provence)

description: This wine has soft flavors, fruity and bright, with a light, easygoing character that will sip down easily. Drink immediately, well chilled.
title: L'original French Kiss 2015 Sauvignon Blanc (Vin de France)

description: It seems strange to have such a heavy, expensive bottle for a wine at this price. The soft, off-dry Chardonnay inside has a lightly fruity character, showing white fruits and the softest texture. It is easy and ready to drink.
title: Le Pépin 2015 Chardonnay (Vin de France)

description: A selection of grapes from several hamlets (hameau in French), this light wine is soft and ready to drink. Lemon and green-herb flavors have a ripe, juicy character alongside flightly flat acidity.
title: Grandissime 2015 Le Hameau Sauvignon Blanc (Vin de France)

description: Black currant aromas lead on to a soft, off-dry wine with red-berry flavors and a stalky texture. With the softness, it is an immediate wine, easy to drink.
title: L'original French Kiss 2015 Malbec (Vin de France)

description: Black currant aromas lead on to a soft, off-dry wine with red-berry flavors and a stalky texture. With the softness, it is an immediate wine, easy to drink.
title: L'original French Kiss 2015 Malbec (Vin de France)

description: This delicate rosé offers a subtle bouquet of muddled cherry, carnation and mentholated berry. The light and slightly astringent palate boasts tangy, tart notes of currant and lime rind that linger through the medium-length finish.
title: La Vieille Ferme 2015 Rosé (Vin de France)

description: This delicate rosé offers a subtle bouquet of muddled cherry, carnation and mentholated berry. The light and slightly astringent palate boasts tangy, tart notes of currant and lime rind that linger through the medium-length finish.
title: La Vieille Ferme 2015 Rosé (Vin de France)

description: The nose has a yeasty, meaty character, while the palate is toasty. Rich flavors include ripe plum and vanilla followed by fragrant acidity at the end.
title: Frédéric Lornet 2011 Les Messagelins Chardonnay (Arbois)

description: There is a touch of earthiness typical of Menetou-Salon in this wine. It brings out gooseberry, catty flavors as well as swathes of citrus. Very crisp, this is a wine that could do with a year to round out.
title: Fournier Père et Fils 2012 Côtes des Morogues  (Menetou-Salon)

description: This big, ripe wine features red fruits, acidity and a touch of young tannins. It is structured, with chocolate and some licorice flavors that are balanced with the strawberry and ripe tannins. Drink from 2020.
title: Henri de Villamont 2014 Les Renardes  (Corton)

description: This is a ripe, rounded and aromatic wine, with just the right stretch of minerality and juicy citrus flavor. Crisp, tangy and refreshing in its fruitiness, the wine is rich and full, finishing with a final burst acidity.
title: Domaine Fourrey 2014 Mont de Milieu Premier Cru  (Chablis)

description: This is a ripe, rounded and aromatic wine, with just the right stretch of minerality and juicy citrus flavor. Crisp, tangy and refreshing in its fruitiness, the wine is rich and full, finishing with a final burst acidity.
title: Domaine Fourrey 2014 Mont de Milieu Premier Cru  (Chablis)

description: This ripe wine comes from vines from two parcels: one normally in the wine, with vines more than more than 60-years-old, the other a hilltop vineyard added in 2014. It is full of rich white fruits that skirt on the zesty side of citrus, giving a crisp edge to this otherwise full wine. It is balanced, juicy and ready to drink.
title: Bret Brothers 2014 Climat Les Clos Reyssié  (Pouilly-Fuissé)

description: This wine is structured, dark and dense, with great swathes of smoky tannins plus plenty of red-fruit flavors. With its concentration, structure and richness, the wine will develop well and powerfully. Drink from 2021.
title: Albert Morot 2014 Les Teurons Premier Cru  (Beaune)

description: This is a rich wine with a fine weight of ripe red apple and pink grapefruit flavors to go with the crisp finish. The wine is ripe and full in the mouth, with just the right final acidity.
title: Veuve Doussot NV Grand Cuvée Brut  (Champagne)

description: A ripe, balanced wine this is maturing well. It has a black plum note to go with the underlying tannins. Rich juicy flavors join notes of spice and wood, leading onto the firm finish. Age for another two years.
title: Domaine Pont de Guestres 2008  Lalande de Pomerol

description: This is a firmly textured wine, with tannins pushing through the black currant fruit. It is beginning to show a balanced structure and a smooth, smoky character that's leavened by acidity and juicy fruit.
title: Château Plaisance 2008  Bordeaux Supérieur

description: Firm and austere, this shows the structured side of the vintage. The wine has weight and rich fruit, giving it the promise of good aging. Give this at least two years to soften.
title: Horeau-Beylot 2010 Château la Fleur  (Montagne-Saint-Émilion)

description: An aromatic, full-bodied wine from a rich vintage, this has firm tannins and an approachable red-fruit flavor, with spice and toast notes from wood aging. Age this for at least two years.
title: Domaine Laporte 2009 Les Royaux  (Sancerre)

description: Ripe and fruity, this has sweet black-currant and plum fruits, a layer of rounded tannins and a juicy, full-in-the-mouth character. It will be ready to drink in a year.
title: Château Tour du Moulin 2009 Les Terres Rouges  (Fronsac)

description: Big, brooding and ripe, this is packed with a blackberry flavor that is laced through the bitter chocolate and mocha notes and dark tannins. It is powerful and concentrated, smooth and dark tasting.
title: Château Lamour 2009 Réserve  (Castillon Côtes de Bordeaux)

description: While youthful tannins play an important part in this dense wine, so does the black fruit character. It's balanced, with the wood toast adding extra complexity. Ripe, while structured, it will age over several years.
title: Château Bellevue Canterrane 2010  Haut-Médoc

description: While youthful tannins play an important part in this dense wine, so does the black fruit character. It's balanced, with the wood toast adding extra complexity. Ripe, while structured, it will age over several years.
title: Château Bellevue Canterrane 2010  Haut-Médoc

description: Big, rich and creamy, this has white and yellow fruits and a full-bodied mouthfeel. It is ripe and rounded, with its acidity showing through to the finish. It needs a year in the bottle.
title: Bouvet-Ladubay 2009 Saphir Brut  (Saumur)

description: This is a fully mature wine, soft and fruity with bitter cherry flavors. While it feels light, it also has tannins that support the smooth texture. It's not a wine for aging, so drink now and until 2017.
title: Fournier Père et Fils 2009 Les Belles Vignes  (Sancerre)

description: Pure apple aromas and flavors give this wine a refreshingly fruity feel. It has touches of almonds, a light and mineral texture and very crisp, fresh acidity. It tastes cool, collected and ready to go.
title: Domaine de Vaugondy 2012 Sec  (Vouvray)

description: Strange aromas emanate from this wine. They point to meat and gravy rather than fruit. So it's a shock to find that the wine is all fruitiness and crisp apple and pear acidity. It's a very textured and needs to age. Drink from 2016.
title: Rijckaert 2010 Les Sarres Savagnin (Côtes du Jura)

description: This soft, fruity wine is pretty much ready to drink. With its red-berry fruits and fresh acidity it has a crisp side, although its round, ripe texture is so attractive. Drink from the end of 2016.
title: Au Pied du Mont Chauve 2012 Le Charmois Premier Cru  (Saint-Aubin)

description: Still young, this is a dark wine with blueberry fruit and firm tannins both on display. It has concentration and the potential for juiciness and richness that will develop. A structured wine, it needs more time. Drink from 2018.
title: Alain Girard et Fils 2014 Domaine des Brosses  (Sancerre)

description: Still young, this is a dark wine with blueberry fruit and firm tannins both on display. It has concentration and the potential for juiciness and richness that will develop. A structured wine, it needs more time. Drink from 2018.
title: Alain Girard et Fils 2014 Domaine des Brosses  (Sancerre)

description: This is a silky, ready-to-drink red. Cherry and plum fruit mingle easily with earth, leather and mocha, finishing on a softly dusty note. Drink now–2023.
title: Barton & Guestier 2013 Passeport Red (Châteauneuf-du-Pape)

description: From La Moussière vineyard, this Pinot Noir-based wine is refreshingly crisp with red fruits and tight lemon and orange-zest acidity. It is lightly textured, with a minerality that comes from the chalk soil of the vineyard. Drink now.
title: Alphonse Mellot 2014 La Moussière Rosé (Sancerre)

description: Aging in big wood barrels has softened the intensity of this wine while leaving the fruitiness intact. It makes for a tangy, mineral-driven wine with a smoky, flinty aftertaste. Drink from 2017.
title: Gitton Père et Fils 2014 Les Romains  (Sancerre)

description: This wine is steely, with tight acidity and grapefruit and lime flavors. It is bright and lively, with a tense edge that needs to soften over the next few months. Drink from the end of 2016.
title: Gitton Père et Fils 2014 Les Montachins  (Sancerre)

description: Vines planted on gravel soil line a terrace above the Cher river. This wine with an intensely herbal character is fresh, crisp and packed with fruit. It has some weight, along with a great lift from the aromatic aftertaste. The wine can be drunk now, although it will be better from 2017.
title: Henri Bourgeois 2014 Haute Victoire  (Quincy)

description: A great value white, with fresh grapefruit and crisp acidity. In a few months, the current raw edge will have softened, as the 60% Sémillon in the blend calms down. But it's still a great summer drink.
title: Château Perron 2006  Graves

description: A great value white, with fresh grapefruit and crisp acidity. In a few months, the current raw edge will have softened, as the 60% Sémillon in the blend calms down. But it's still a great summer drink.
title: Château Perron 2006  Graves

description: From one of the rare organic vineyards of the Médoc, this is a firm wine whose tannins are a fine sheen over the ripe fruits. Balancing Cabernet and Merlot, the wine has structure and juicy blackberry flavors, laced with acidity. It's a wine to age for some years, so drink from 2018.
title: Château Meyre 2012  Haut-Médoc

description: Although wood aging in this superior cuvée is prominent, this wine has just enough juicy black fruits to allow it to develop well. Get past the wood, and the wine is rich enough and structured with fruit tannins. Allow the wine to integrate and drink from 2017.
title: Château Lamothe de Haux 2012 Première Cuvée  (Côtes de Bordeaux)

description: Although wood aging in this superior cuvée is prominent, this wine has just enough juicy black fruits to allow it to develop well. Get past the wood, and the wine is rich enough and structured with fruit tannins. Allow the wine to integrate and drink from 2017.
title: Château Lamothe de Haux 2012 Première Cuvée  (Côtes de Bordeaux)

description: This 19-acre property, in the same family since the 17th century, has produced a structured, Merlot-dominated wine that is as much about tannins as fruit. It's still young and all that juicy black currant fruitiness will blossom. Give it until 2017.
title: Château Guitignan 2012  Moulis-en-Médoc

description: Big, full-bodied and very much a product of the 2010 vintage, this structured, generous wine needs time. The dry tannins are still prominent, giving a tough edge to the more generous, concentrated fruits. Drink from 2018.
title: Château des Tourtes 2010 Cuvée Prestige  (Blaye Côtes de Bordeaux)

description: This wine has a rich core of black fruits, dense tannins and good acidity, offering testimony to the firm character of Saint-Estèphe. Concentrated. it will develop well. Wait until 2018.
title: Château de Côme 2012  Saint-Estèphe

description: Fresh and juicy, this balances well between fruit stalkiness and smooth wood aging. Dominated by Cabernet Sauvignon, it has black currant flavors that are given extra weight by ripe Petit Verdot. Drink from 2017.
title: Château Chantelys 2012  Médoc

description: Light in color, this has a warm jammy feel that's leavened by intense acidity. Just touched with tannins, it is attractive and ready to drink.
title: Roux Père et Fils 2010  Bourgogne

description: This is gentle and rounded, with creamed pear and citrus flavors. With hints of caramel and vanilla, it is soft, clean and very ready to drink.
title: Louis Max 2010  Mâcon-Villages

description: This is gentle and rounded, with creamed pear and citrus flavors. With hints of caramel and vanilla, it is soft, clean and very ready to drink.
title: Louis Max 2010  Mâcon-Villages

description: Apple and pear flavors dominate this attractive wine. It has a simple, fruit-forward character, and it's soft, rounded and developing well. On the finish, a more tangy, fresh character shows.
title: Domaine Viticole de la Ville de Colmar 2009 Florimont Grand Cru Riesling (Alsace)
winery: Domaine Viticole de la Ville de Colmar

description: A very tangy wine, this is full of lemon zest and crisp apple-skin flavors. It's attractive, fruity and delightfully laden with almond and pear notes. The finish is rounded and fresh; drink this year.
title: Domaine Schoffit 2010 Harth Tradition Riesling (Alsace)

description: Creamed pear- and apple-skin flavors give a wine that has warm acidity, with touches of vanilla and almond. This is warm, rounded and full bodied, with a tang of citrusy acidity that hints at its aging potential.
title: Domaine Michel Fonne 2010 Tradition Riesling (Alsace)

description: This is a ripe, rich wine, with an open yellow-fruit flavor. It has weight that lends a full-bodied character. While missing a more nervy character, it gives warm pleasure.
title: Cave de Kientzheim-Kaysersberg 2009 The Furst Riesling (Alsace)

description: This is a ripe, rich wine, with an open yellow-fruit flavor. It has weight that lends a full-bodied character. While missing a more nervy character, it gives warm pleasure.
title: Cave de Kientzheim-Kaysersberg 2009 The Furst Riesling (Alsace)

description: This wine shows so much rich fruit. It has a herbal edge, but the yellow and white fruits really define it. Wood-aging has left hints of spice, and the wine also has a tangy, mineral edge. It is ready to drink.
title: Château Mouton Rothschild 2013 Aile d'Argent  (Bordeaux Blanc)

description: With firm tannins and ripe, balanced fruit, this is a success for the vintage, profiting from the dry conditions during harvest in Saint-Estèphe. Blackberry fruits and rich tannins give the wine shape and aging potential. Keep the wine until 2019.
title: Château Lilian Ladouys 2013  Saint-Estèphe

description: The second wine of Léoville las Cases has structure and richness with plenty of concentration. At the same time, it has so much fresh, ripe fruit, laced with intense acidity that it is more fresh then structured. With this balance already established it will be ready to drink from 2019.
title: Château Léoville Las Cases 2013 Le Petit Lion  (Saint-Julien)

description: This wine comes from a vast 460-acre vineyard on the plateau just west of Pauillac. The wood-aging just shows in what is otherwise a ripe and fruity wine. A firm tannic core indicates the youth of the wine rather than masking the fruit. Generous and fruity, this wine will develop well. Drink from 2018.
title: Château Larose Trintaudon 2013  Haut-Médoc

description: While this wine is concentrated with firm tannins, the rich fruit dominates. It is dark, complex and rich, filled with black-plum flavors and a good structure. Intense juiciness character complements the tannins, giving a ripe wine that can age. Drink from 2018.
title: Château Mayne Vieil 2013 Cuvée Aliénor  (Fronsac)

description: While this wine is concentrated with firm tannins, the rich fruit dominates. It is dark, complex and rich, filled with black-plum flavors and a good structure. Intense juiciness character complements the tannins, giving a ripe wine that can age. Drink from 2018.
title: Château Mayne Vieil 2013 Cuvée Aliénor  (Fronsac)

description: This wine comes from a densely planted seven-acre estate, typical of many small properties in Pomerol. Strongly led by its wood aging, it's a structured, still very dry wine. It needs time to develop the black plum and juicy acidity that are there. Drink from 2019.
title: Château Lécuyer 2013  Pomerol

description: This is a well-made, ripe while structured wine. With its juicy black-currant fruits, edge of firm tannins and balanced character, it brings out the best of the year with fruit and not too much structure. Drink from 2019.
title: Château Grand-Puy Lacoste 2013  Pauillac

description: This is a well-made, ripe while structured wine. With its juicy black-currant fruits, edge of firm tannins and balanced character, it brings out the best of the year with fruit and not too much structure. Drink from 2019.
title: Château Grand-Puy Lacoste 2013  Pauillac

description: Offering some of the few relatively good-value wines from Pauillac, this 50-acre property has made an impressive wine in this tough year. It is structured and dense although the black-currant fruitiness shows that it will develop quickly to be drinkable from 2020.
title: Château Fonbadet 2013  Pauillac

description: Offering some of the few relatively good-value wines from Pauillac, this 50-acre property has made an impressive wine in this tough year. It is structured and dense although the black-currant fruitiness shows that it will develop quickly to be drinkable from 2020.
title: Château Fonbadet 2013  Pauillac

description: This wine is ripe, full of spice, toast and intense acidity. It has the herbal character of Sauvignon Blanc along with a fresh, tangy edge. Still tight and closed, it needs to develop; drink from 2018. After two centuries under various ownerships, the derelict Couhins estate was purchased by the French agricultural research institute (INRA) in 1968. After renovating the vineyards, the institute began selling wine in 2007.
title: Château Couhins 2013  Pessac-Léognan

description: With the high alcohol typical of 2010 vintage, this is a ripe, jammy and full wine. Black plums ooze richness against a background of firm tannins and acidity that will allow the wine to age. It is dense, concentrated and powerful, needing some time. Drink from 2018.
title: Château Beauséjour 2010  Puisseguin Saint-Émilion

description: Fine tannins give this wine density and structure. A high proportion (69%) of the two Cabernets has boosted the concentration and given the wine impressive weight for the vintage. It's an excellent success for the year. Drink from 2018.
title: Château Potensac 2013  Médoc

description: This wine is smoky with hints of wood. The red-plum fruits are a little suppressed at the moment although the acidity and freshness hint at a good future. It has a cool character with plenty of acidity under the tannins. It will develop, but slowly. Drink from 2020.
title: Domaine Faiveley 2014 Aux Chaignots Premier Cru  (Nuits-St.-Georges)

description: This wine has firm tannins and a dry, structured core. From vines that are close to Beaune, it is dense and concentrated, although with the pure fruit that marks out the vintage. It is going to develop well and with great style.
title: Domaine des Croix 2014 Les Peuillets Premier Cru  (Savigny-lès-Beaune)

description: This powerful wine has considerable structure and considerable acidity that will shine as the wine develops. The fruit is delicious, showing great potential. Drink from 2020.
title: Chanson Père et Fils 2013 Les Chenevottes Premier Cru  (Chassagne-Montrachet)

description: This big, bold and ripe wine has both structure and generous red fruits. It's already balanced with a touch of minerality from the limestone and clay soil. Wood aging has smoothed the tannins while retaining the fruit and bringing out balancing acidity. It is ready to drink but will be better from 2017.
title: Domaine du Théron 2012 Prestige Malbec (Cahors)

description: Rich and smoothly textured, this is rich with red berry fruits balanced by intense acidity. The structure is ripe, full of concentration from low-yield vines and ready for aging. Drink from 2017. This is from the Fer Servadou grape, similar to Cabernet Sauvignon, and known in Gaillac as Braucol. The estate, which spans both sides of the Tarn river, has been in the Hirissou family for six generations.
title: Domaine du Moulin 2013 Florentin Braucol (Gaillac)

description: A big and powerful wine considering the lighter style found in many 2011s. It's concentrated and dark, with black plums enveloping full and ripe fruit. Weight, richness and perfume combine to ensure long-term aging over six years and more.
title: Domaine du Comte Liger-Belair 2011  Echézeaux

description: Full bodied and savory, this is a dark, complex wine loaded with notes of cured meat, black olive, espresso and plum. The tannins are ripe to the point of imparting a creamy texture yet the wine never seems overripe or jammy, maintaining a fine sense of balance on the lingering finish.
title: Domaine de Nalys 2010 Réserve Red (Châteauneuf-du-Pape)

description: A taut, nervy, mineral-driven wine, this has intense citrus and grapefruit flavors, lemon grass spice and just the merest hint of wood. It's the structure that gives this impressive wine such power, and a steely edge that will need at least 6–10 years.
title: Domaine Leflaive 2010 Clavoillon Premier Cru  (Puligny-Montrachet)

description: Château Grenouilles is a parcel within the Grenouilles Grand Cru, a monopoly of the La Chablisienne cooperative. The wine is always impressive. It has weight, richness, concentration and considerable potential. Yellow fruits, wood-aging, spice and a firm structure indicate keeping this wine for six years.
title: La Chablisienne 2010 Château Grenouilles Grand Cru  (Chablis)

description: Château Grenouilles is a parcel within the Grenouilles Grand Cru, a monopoly of the La Chablisienne cooperative. The wine is always impressive. It has weight, richness, concentration and considerable potential. Yellow fruits, wood-aging, spice and a firm structure indicate keeping this wine for six years.
title: La Chablisienne 2010 Château Grenouilles Grand Cru  (Chablis)

description: From this powerful and structured vineyard comes a powerful and structured wine. It's very firm, dry and solidly concentrated at the heart. There is also a surge of rich, open fruitiness that complements the fine acidity. It's complex, perfumed and expressive. Age for seven years.
title: François Bertheau 2011  Bonnes-Mares

description: A rich wine, full and fruity up front, then opening up into a much more mineral, textured character. It is a great explosion of citrus, pear and green apple, the wood aging showing with subtlety. It's a wine for aging, complex and tight at the end.
title: Domaine Leflaive 2010 Les Pucelles Premier Cru  (Puligny-Montrachet)

description: With its structured, mineral character, this is a serious, ageworthy wine. It has a sense of coiled power and steel and a dense, complex texture that brings out both its ripe, pure fruit character and its intensity. Age this wine for at least 5–8 years.
title: Domaine Leflaive 2010 Les Combettes Premier Cru  (Puligny-Montrachet)

description: A dry, mineral wine, hiding its potential richness. Flavors of ripe pears and yellow fruits are matched by lime acidity. The wine has considerable power and a dense character, showing the immense density that comes from this vineyard. Age for 4–6 years and more.
title: Domaine des Croix 2011  Corton-Charlemagne

description: A monopoly of the domaine, La Romanée lies just up the slope from Romanée-Conti. It's already a beautiful wine, with its velvet tannins well integrated with the ripe berry fruits. Its core is dry and structured, with the fruits cushioning around it.
title: Domaine du Comte Liger-Belair 2011  La Romanée

description: A monopoly of the domaine, La Romanée lies just up the slope from Romanée-Conti. It's already a beautiful wine, with its velvet tannins well integrated with the ripe berry fruits. Its core is dry and structured, with the fruits cushioning around it.
title: Domaine du Comte Liger-Belair 2011  La Romanée

description: This is a succulent wine with its light tannins and juicy red-berry fruits. It is fresh with a mineral edge as well as spice and balanced acidity. The aftertaste is smooth and soft. It is ready to drink for the pleasure of its fruit.
title: Domaine Gérard Fiou 2013  Sancerre

description: This is a succulent wine with its light tannins and juicy red-berry fruits. It is fresh with a mineral edge as well as spice and balanced acidity. The aftertaste is smooth and soft. It is ready to drink for the pleasure of its fruit.
title: Domaine Gérard Fiou 2013  Sancerre

description: A rather high-toned note akin to resin appears at first but quickly turns into the sweet notion of fir honey. The palate is honeyed, too, with a rich, almost candied center of caramelised peach. There is concentration at the core and a convincing freshness.
title: Domaine Fernand Engel 2013 Altenberg de Bergheim Grand Cru Gewurztraminer (Alsace)

description: Mellow sweetness on nose and palate suggests peach compote perfumed with rose water. The result is heady and sweet, oriental and opulent, yet not without charm. Aromatic echoes of honeysuckle and dried orange peel temper the riches pleasantly.
title: Domaine Barmès-Buecher 2011 Pfersigberg Grand Cru Gewurztraminer (Alsace)

description: A hint of caramel hovers above the apple-driven nose. Creamy caramel notes give the palate a soft, cushioned aspect, harmonising with pliable, plump apple fruit. This is dry and unusually creamy for Riesling but full of charm.
title: Frédéric Mallo 2013 Rosacker Grand Cru Vieilles Vignes Riesling (Alsace)

description: A lifted, phenolic note of Bosc pear peel suggests both freshness and maturity. The soft, rounded palate sings with pear sweetness and finishes medium-dry. There is softness and pliability, but a guiding, focused freshness that provides excellent balance.
title: Domaine Moltès 2014 Steinert Grand Cru Pinot Gris (Alsace)

description: Tight, crisp and with herbal as well as citrus flavors, this wine comes from flinty soil. That creates all the intensity, the tautness, the mineral texture and the ability for the wine to age. True to style, this wine will need to be kept, so don't drink before 2017.
title: Domaine Gérard Fiou 2014  Sancerre

description: Tight, crisp and with herbal as well as citrus flavors, this wine comes from flinty soil. That creates all the intensity, the tautness, the mineral texture and the ability for the wine to age. True to style, this wine will need to be kept, so don't drink before 2017.
title: Domaine Gérard Fiou 2014  Sancerre

description: Rather dull, soapy wine, its fruit missing the right crispness. There are flavors of pear, yellow fruits, just not enough acidity.
designation: Perle d'Ivoire Blanc de Blancs Brut
title: Louis Bouillot NV Perle d'Ivoire Blanc de Blancs Brut  (Crémant de Bourgogne)

description: Rather dull, soapy wine, its fruit missing the right crispness. There are flavors of pear, yellow fruits, just not enough acidity.
designation: Perle d'Ivoire Blanc de Blancs Brut
title: Louis Bouillot NV Perle d'Ivoire Blanc de Blancs Brut  (Crémant de Bourgogne)

description: Typically semi-sweet style of rosé, crisp and clean, flavored with ripe strawberries. Good as an apéritif or with spicy dishes. Screwcap.
title: Les Vignerons des Terroirs de la Noëlle 2010 Les Ligeriens  (Rosé d'Anjou)
winery: Les Vignerons des Terroirs de la Noëlle

description: Typically semi-sweet style of rosé, crisp and clean, flavored with ripe strawberries. Good as an apéritif or with spicy dishes. Screwcap.
title: Les Vignerons des Terroirs de la Noëlle 2010 Les Ligeriens  (Rosé d'Anjou)
winery: Les Vignerons des Terroirs de la Noëlle

description: While it has some attractive apple fruits, the wine misses out on the real minerality and texture of Pouilly Fuissé. It's a wine hidden behind net drapes, indistinct.
title: Pierre André 2009  Pouilly-Fuissé

description: Pale gold in color, the wine is already hinting at maturity. It is deliciously ripe, perfumed with layers of green herbs and a finely textured character. Great acidity gives a tight, bright aftertaste.
title: Zusslin 2010 Bollenberg Riesling (Alsace)

description: Pale gold in color, the wine is already hinting at maturity. It is deliciously ripe, perfumed with layers of green herbs and a finely textured character. Great acidity gives a tight, bright aftertaste.
title: Zusslin 2010 Bollenberg Riesling (Alsace)

description: Yes, it is spicy, but this is also an elegant wine, balancing its honeyed sweetness and tropical fruits with a stylish acidity and sophisticated perfume. Warm and round at the end, it is ready to drink.
title: Domaine Zinck 2011 Terroir Gewurztraminer (Alsace)

description: Regarded almost as a Grand Cru in its own right, the Moutonne vineyard, wholly owned by Albert Bichot, is in a corner of the Vaudésir Grand Cru vineyard. In this sumptuous year, the wine is more generous, ripe yellow fruits than mineral texture. The acidity and the tangy aftertaste are a reminder that this is from cool-climate Chablis. Drink from 2023.
title: Albert Bichot 2015 Domaine Long-Depaquit Moutonne  (Chablis)

description: This is the Arnoux family's top wine coming from vines on the revered hill of Corton. It is a powerful wine, properly rich and structured from the vintage. Wood and spice come through although they will soon integrate with the dense black-plum fruits and mineral texture. Drink the wine from 2025.
title: Domaine Arnoux Père et Fils 2015 Le Rognet  (Corton)

description: From the largest Grand Cru in Vosne-Romanée, this wine has plenty of the structure as well as the fruit that shines in this vintage. It is rich and smoky with black fruits and red-berry flavors. The wine is still young, drink from 2026.
title: Louis Latour 2015  Echézeaux

description: A ripe, dense wine, this has powerful fruit and a serious long-term future. It is rich with yellow fruits with a generous, creamy texture, and tight with minerality. This gorgeous wine will certainly age well. Drink from 2024.
title: Louis Latour 2015 Les Demoiselles  (Chevalier-Montrachet)

description: Wood, ripe fruit and a tight texture give this wine a very complete feeling. It is structured, mineral-driven and packed with fresh apples and yellow fruit. The impressive structure and balance suggest the wine will age well; drink from 2024.
title: Louis Latour 2015  Bâtard-Montrachet

description: Wood, ripe fruit and a tight texture give this wine a very complete feeling. It is structured, mineral-driven and packed with fresh apples and yellow fruit. The impressive structure and balance suggest the wine will age well; drink from 2024.
title: Louis Latour 2015  Bâtard-Montrachet

description: This opulent, powerful wine has weight, richness and a beautiful creamy texture. It's built to age, from its wood aging to its minerality. Concentrated, it offers yellow fruits shot through with acidity. From the grandest Chardonnay vineyard in Burgundy, it will age well and be ready to drink from 2026.
title: Louis Latour 2015  Montrachet

description: Mordorée's Côtes du Rhône is a classic blend built around 40% Grenache and 30% Syrah, with smaller amounts of the other permitted varieties. The result combines scents of leather and roasted meat with cherries and dark overtones of cocoa and coffee. It's a nicely balanced, full-bodied wine, with just a touch of coarseness to its texture. Drink now-2016.
title: Domaine de la Mordorée 2010 La Dame Rousse Red (Côtes du Rhône)

description: Mordorée's Côtes du Rhône is a classic blend built around 40% Grenache and 30% Syrah, with smaller amounts of the other permitted varieties. The result combines scents of leather and roasted meat with cherries and dark overtones of cocoa and coffee. It's a nicely balanced, full-bodied wine, with just a touch of coarseness to its texture. Drink now-2016.
title: Domaine de la Mordorée 2010 La Dame Rousse Red (Côtes du Rhône)

description: This is a yeasty wine, with the fruit less evident. It has acidity and a touch of apple, although a bitter edge cuts into the rounded texture.
title: Domaine Luquet 2010  Bourgogne

description: This is bitter, with hints of sulfur, yeast and almond. It's soft in texture and lacking fruit.
title: Manuel Seguin 2010  Bourgogne

description: This is soft, with candy and raspbery flavors. Its acidity offers some freshness along with light sweetness on the finish. Drink now.
title: Quinson Fils 2010 Rosé (Côtes de Provence)

description: This is soft, with candy and raspbery flavors. Its acidity offers some freshness along with light sweetness on the finish. Drink now.
title: Quinson Fils 2010 Rosé (Côtes de Provence)

description: Delicate and rounded, this has soft vanilla and ripe strawberry flavos. It has touches of spice and orange peel, with gentle acidity on this finish.
title: Mas de Cadenet 2011 Arbaude Rosé (Côtes de Provence)

description: A bit lean and tannic, with an herbal tang to the tart cherry and cranberry fruit. This doesn't show much of the warmth of the vintage but remains a pleasant wine, best served alongside fatty foods like burgers.
title: Louis Bernard 2009 Domaine Le Garrigon Red (Côtes du Rhône)

description: Finding ripe Petit Verdot outside the Médoc in Bordeaux is unusual. And then to make an 100% varietal wine is very rare. It is a rich wine without being excessive. Its tannins and structure are firm, backed up by black fruits that will surely develop as the wine matures. Drink this success story from 2020.
title: Les Vignerons de Tutiac 2014 Lieu-Dit  (Blaye Côtes de Bordeaux)

description: Gerin's lieu-dit wines from 2013 are both successful. Les Grandes Places is muscular but not musclebound, combining finesse and elegance with elements of roasted meat and grilled fruit. After 20 months in new oak, the nose reveals hints of baking spices, but those are balanced by blueberry and pepper elements. Drink 2018–2028.
title: Domaine Jean-Michel Gerin 2013 Les Grandes Places  (Côte Rôtie)

description: This wine is firm with solid tannins. It has rich fruit and concentration with layers of blackberry and dark plums. It comes from a small seven-acre property and is aged for 15 months in wood. This impressive wine needs to age, so drink from 2022.
title: Château Lafleur du Roy 2015 Cuvée Excellence  (Pomerol)

description: The Gonet family's investment, which began in 1998, has begun to bear fruit. This wine comes from the second in a row of fine Bordeaux vintages. The style of the vintage is well represented in this richly endowed wine with its swathes of black fruits, its rich tannins and its warm full texture. This is just coming together after a quiet period for the vintage. Drink from 2018.
title: Château Haut-Bacalan 2009  Pessac-Léognan

description: The Gonet family's investment, which began in 1998, has begun to bear fruit. This wine comes from the second in a row of fine Bordeaux vintages. The style of the vintage is well represented in this richly endowed wine with its swathes of black fruits, its rich tannins and its warm full texture. This is just coming together after a quiet period for the vintage. Drink from 2018.
title: Château Haut-Bacalan 2009  Pessac-Léognan

description: Aromas seem blunted, but the palate shows both freshness and fruit. This is balanced and comes out with surprisingly friendly apple fruit, finishing on a fresh note.
title: Domaine Moltès 2014 Tradition Pinot Gris (Alsace)

description: Ripe aromas of peach, melon, apple and pineapple unfold on the nose of this wine, with additional hints of hay and flint that add an earthy streak. The light-weight palate shows a soft prickle of acidity that then fades quickly on the finish, feeling a touch flat. Drink now.
title: Château Ollieux Romanis 2013 Cuvée Classique White (Corbières)

description: Ripe aromas of peach, melon, apple and pineapple unfold on the nose of this wine, with additional hints of hay and flint that add an earthy streak. The light-weight palate shows a soft prickle of acidity that then fades quickly on the finish, feeling a touch flat. Drink now.
title: Château Ollieux Romanis 2013 Cuvée Classique White (Corbières)

description: This light and fruity wine has acidity sustaining the red-cherry flavors. It has a dry core along with really juicy flavors and soft tannins. Drink now, although the wine will be even fruitier from 2016.
title: Vignerons de Buxy 2013 Buissonnier  (Côte Chalonnaise)

description: This light and fruity wine has acidity sustaining the red-cherry flavors. It has a dry core along with really juicy flavors and soft tannins. Drink now, although the wine will be even fruitier from 2016.
title: Vignerons de Buxy 2013 Buissonnier  (Côte Chalonnaise)

description: The subtle scent of green and red apples makes for a refreshing opening. They also play on the rounded, clean palate and finish dry with a lovely, lemony briskness.
title: Paul Blanck 2014 Riesling (Alsace)

description: Bony and austere, the palate is marked by tart flavors and hints of underdeveloped stone fruit. It is crisp and clean, offering a distinctive, different take on white wine from the Southern Rhône.
title: Domaine du Pegau 2013 Château Pêgau Cuvée Lône White (Côtes du Rhône)

description: Bony and austere, the palate is marked by tart flavors and hints of underdeveloped stone fruit. It is crisp and clean, offering a distinctive, different take on white wine from the Southern Rhône.
title: Domaine du Pegau 2013 Château Pêgau Cuvée Lône White (Côtes du Rhône)

description: All black fruits, the wine is dominated by black currants and stalky tannins. It is fresh with lively acidity and berry flavors and a generous texture. Drink from 2016.
title: Pelvillain Frères 2013 Albatross Malbec (Cahors)

description: This is a softly ripe, blackberry-flavored wine, with its tannins lending a firm core. Along with the stalky fruit, the wine is dry with acidity. Drink now.
title: Les Portes de Bordeaux 2009  Bordeaux

description: This traditional method sparkling rosé is soft, rounded with strawberry fruit. There is a bitter almond edge to it that spoils its otherwise fruity character.
title: Grandin NV Rosé Dry Sparkling (Vin Mousseux)

description: Perfumed, light and fresh, this has acidity highlighting the white fruit and grapefruit flavors. It's a crisp wine, edged with an apple skin note.
title: Charles de Fère NV Reserve Nature Brut Sparkling (Vin Mousseux)

description: This structured wine is full of fruit and has a tight texture. It shows a creamy side from new wood, although this is well integrated into the fruity acidity and the mineral edge. The wine is likely to age well, ready to drink from 2020.
title: Louis Latour 2015 Château de Blagny Premier Cru  (Meursault)

description: From one of the top Beaune premier crus, this wine is structured and dense with tannins and with wood aging. At the same time, it has the rich fruitiness of the year, broad red berries and plums. They provide the delicious potential of this fine wine. Drink from 2022.
title: Jean-Luc and Paul Aegerter 2015 Les Grèves Premier Cru  (Beaune)

description: This wine is rich and spicy. At this stage, with its muted fruit, it is all potential, but one can sense the ripeness and generous texture that will make it excellent once it matures. Give this powerful wine until 2023.
title: Jean-Luc and Paul Aegerter 2015  Corton-Charlemagne

description: This is a ripe rounded wine, backed by the firm tannins that mark Pommard. It is bold, ripe with plenty of concentrated red fruits and finishing acidity. The wine has a crisp edge that lifts the tannins. Drink from 2023.
designation: Domaine Clos de la Chapelle Les Chanlins-Bas Premier Cru
title: Meurgey-Croses 2015 Domaine Clos de la Chapelle Les Chanlins-Bas Premier Cru  (Pommard)

description: The wine is tight with a strong mineral element over the acidity. It shows a sense of chalky terroir, full of red-currant fruits and a nervy aftertaste. It will take some time to fully develop, so wait until 2023.
designation: Clos de la Chapelle Premier Cru
title: Meurgey-Croses 2015 Clos de la Chapelle Premier Cru  (Volnay)

description: This small Premier Cru vineyard is wholly owned by the Devillard family. It is a rich wine, boasting layers of beautiful jammy red fruits and just the lightest touch of wood. Tannins are there, forming a core that will stand the wine in good stead as it ages. Drink from 2023.
designation: Château de Chamirey Clos des Ruelles Premier Cru
title: Domaines Devillard 2015 Château de Chamirey Clos des Ruelles Premier Cru  (Mercurey)

description: This small Premier Cru vineyard is wholly owned by the Devillard family. It is a rich wine, boasting layers of beautiful jammy red fruits and just the lightest touch of wood. Tannins are there, forming a core that will stand the wine in good stead as it ages. Drink from 2023.
designation: Château de Chamirey Clos des Ruelles Premier Cru
title: Domaines Devillard 2015 Château de Chamirey Clos des Ruelles Premier Cru  (Mercurey)

description: From perhaps the best known of Mercurey's premier crus, this is a firm solid wine, dense with tannins and concentrated berry fruits. It has a ripe character that is still embedded in the tannins. That means aging and this wine should not be drunk before 2023.
title: Domaine de Suremain 2015 Clos l'Evêque Premier Cru  (Mercurey)

description: Bruno Copéret has produced an impressive wine from this small vineyard on his property. It is still young, full of smoky wood and broad red-fruit flavors. The tannins and the concentration are considerable, although the wine also has a more stylish edge. Drink from 2019.
title: Domaine de Roche-Guillon 2015 Clos de la Tour  (Fleurie)

description: Bruno Copéret has produced an impressive wine from this small vineyard on his property. It is still young, full of smoky wood and broad red-fruit flavors. The tannins and the concentration are considerable, although the wine also has a more stylish edge. Drink from 2019.
title: Domaine de Roche-Guillon 2015 Clos de la Tour  (Fleurie)

description: This is a structured rich wine. It has great ripe fruit, generous with red berry and acidity in fine balance. It has a solid backbone of tannins although these are already well integrated into the opulent wine. Drink from 2021.
title: Château de Santenay 2015 Montée Rouge Premier Cru  (Beaune)

description: This is a firm wine that is structured with dense tannins. At the same time, its ripe black fruits and acidity promise a generous rich future. From a walled vineyard, once belonging to the local bishop, the wine is set for some long-term aging. Drink from 2023.
designation: Château de Chamirey Clos l'Evêque Premier Cru
title: Domaines Devillard 2015 Château de Chamirey Clos l'Evêque Premier Cru  (Mercurey)

description: Vanilla aromas indicate that wood aging has made an already ripe wine even richer. The tannins are still young, calling for aging, but bold cherry and red plum tones are ripe, full bodied and open. Drink this concentrated wine from 2019.
title: Domaine Fond Moiroux 2014  Moulin-à-Vent

description: Vanilla aromas indicate that wood aging has made an already ripe wine even richer. The tannins are still young, calling for aging, but bold cherry and red plum tones are ripe, full bodied and open. Drink this concentrated wine from 2019.
title: Domaine Fond Moiroux 2014  Moulin-à-Vent

description: A seven-acre vineyard on the eastern side of Mercurey gives a wine that is broad and ripe. Both its structure and its juicy red fruits are generous and with a firm core of tannins. The wine is likely to age well. Drink from 2022.
title: Domaine de Suremain 2015 La Bondue Premier Cru  (Mercurey)

description: This is a perfumed wine, opulent and with a fine smoky structure. With great ripe berry and red-currant fruit, the wine has a juicy character, bright and crisp with acidity while also solidly textured. Drink this wine from 2023.
title: Domaine de Suremain 2015 En Sazenay Premier Cru  (Mercurey)

description: This is a perfumed wine, opulent and with a fine smoky structure. With great ripe berry and red-currant fruit, the wine has a juicy character, bright and crisp with acidity while also solidly textured. Drink this wine from 2023.
title: Domaine de Suremain 2015 En Sazenay Premier Cru  (Mercurey)

description: Soft, ripe and rounded, this shows a gentle side of Bordeaux. The tannins are sweet, just hinting at wood, but this is more about blackberries and a finishing sweetness.
title: Château Teyssier 2005  Saint-Émilion

description: Soft, ripe and rounded, this shows a gentle side of Bordeaux. The tannins are sweet, just hinting at wood, but this is more about blackberries and a finishing sweetness.
title: Château Teyssier 2005  Saint-Émilion

description: A Merlot-dominated wine from the east bank of the Gironde estuary. It's big, possibly too powerful, with meaty, smoky flavors and spice. Solid, chunky, it gives freshness and liveliness right at the end, as the acidity comes through.
title: Bernard Magrez 2004 Château Pérenne  (Premieres Côtes de Blaye)

description: A fine, ripe wine, creamy toast coming through the red fruits and light tannins. It is already well developed, not a wine for aging, but it is delicious to drink now, very fresh, juicy.
title: Château d'Arcins 2005  Haut-Médoc

description: This smoky, ripe wine is attractively balanced, showing the freshness of the vintage. There is a pleasant touch of wood, along with black-currant fruitiness and the potential to age for 3–5 years.
title: Château Latour-Laguens 2011 Cuvée Bacchus  (Bordeaux Supérieur)

description: A spicy wine, with nutmeg and allspice as well as peppered plums. Against this exotic background, the tannins are solid and concentrated, suggesting good aging potential.
title: Château Laride 2011 L'Iris de Laride  Vieilles Vignes  (Haut-Médoc)

description: A very spicy Gewurztraminer that is soft, lychee flavored and full-bodied. It is all perfume, only just hinting at acidity, off dry in style, very ready to drink now.
title: Jean Becker 2012 Gewurztraminer (Alsace)

description: Designed as a fruity vision of Malbec, this is a ripe, lightly wood aged wine, laden with berry fruits, soft tannins and an open texture. It's ready to drink, a fine barbecue style, friendly wine.
title: Georges Vigouroux 2012 Pigmentum Rouge Malbec (Cahors)

description: Designed as a fruity vision of Malbec, this is a ripe, lightly wood aged wine, laden with berry fruits, soft tannins and an open texture. It's ready to drink, a fine barbecue style, friendly wine.
title: Georges Vigouroux 2012 Pigmentum Rouge Malbec (Cahors)

description: Light, herbaceous wine, very fruity, full of greengage and gooseberry flavors. It's tight, fresh and crisp, ready to drink.
title: Georges Vigouroux 2012 Pigmentum Blanc Ugni Blanc-Colombard (Côtes de Gascogne)

description: A blend of 50% Grenache Noir, 40% Mourvèdre and 10% Grenache Gris, this medium-weight rosé offers aromas and flavors of cherry, nectarine and watermelon rind. The acidity keeps the palate fresh and the finish slightly tart and biting.
title: Le Cirque 2012 Rosé (Côtes Catalanes)

description: A blend of 50% Grenache Noir, 40% Mourvèdre and 10% Grenache Gris, this medium-weight rosé offers aromas and flavors of cherry, nectarine and watermelon rind. The acidity keeps the palate fresh and the finish slightly tart and biting.
title: Le Cirque 2012 Rosé (Côtes Catalanes)

description: Simple, bright white and citrus fruits give this wine a great lift from the start. There is a smooth, vanilla texture as well as a touch of minerality giving texture. The wine finishes with bright acidity.
title: Vincent 2011 JJ Bourgogne Blanc  (Bourgogne)

description: Simple, bright white and citrus fruits give this wine a great lift from the start. There is a smooth, vanilla texture as well as a touch of minerality giving texture. The wine finishes with bright acidity.
title: Vincent 2011 JJ Bourgogne Blanc  (Bourgogne)

description: The typical Côtes de Gascogne blend of Colombard and Sauvignon Blanc, this is crisp, brightly herbaceous, hinting at peach as well as lime juice. It is fresh, clean and deliciously fruity.
title: Rieutort 2012 Colombard-Sauvignon Blanc (Côtes de Gascogne)

description: The blend of 90% Merlot and 10% Cabernet Franc gives this wine a rich character. It does have a firm edge of tannins still producing a dry character that needs to soften. The juicy black currants are developing well and should balance the tannins in a year or two. Drink this solid wine from 2018.
title: Château Roc de Boissac 2012  Puisseguin Saint-Émilion

description: With 20-year-old vines, this estate has the ability to produce open fruity wines like this. This wine, that is now almost mature, has black-currant fruit, juicy acidity and a layer of tannins to allow it to age further. Drink this attractive wine from 2017.
title: Château Renard 2012  Fronsac

description: A warm wine that shows rich flavors, ripe acidity and plenty of yellow fruits. It is rounded, smooth and likely to develop quickly. The acidity at the end is the crisp contrast to this full, forward wine. Drink from 2015.
designation: Les Murgers des Dents de Chien Premier Cru
title: Domaine Vincent Girardin 2011 Les Murgers des Dents de Chien Premier Cru  (Saint-Aubin)

description: From a small parcel in the Lamothe-Vincent vineyard, this rich, structured wine shows a strong relationship with terroir and minerality. It has power and intensity, while still preserving enough freshness. Drink from 2016.
designation: Le Grand Rossignol du Château Lamothe Vincent
title: Château Lamothe-Vincent 2010 Le Grand Rossignol du Château Lamothe Vincent  (Bordeaux Supérieur)

description: This impressive wood-aged wine has weight, rich black and red berry flavors and a smooth, unctuous texture. With its concentration, ripeness, acidity and tannins, it could age through 2016.
title: Château de Pierreux 2011 La Réserve du Château  (Brouilly)

description: Big, ripe and juicy, this solidly based wine also has great fruitiness. Black fruits, some bitter chocolate and licorice point to ripeness and wood aging. It has a rich texture, its spiciness bringing out the plum and damson fruits. For aging over the medium-term, drink from 2017.
title: Château Cormeil-Figeac 2011  Saint-Émilion

description: Big, ripe and juicy, this solidly based wine also has great fruitiness. Black fruits, some bitter chocolate and licorice point to ripeness and wood aging. It has a rich texture, its spiciness bringing out the plum and damson fruits. For aging over the medium-term, drink from 2017.
title: Château Cormeil-Figeac 2011  Saint-Émilion

description: Neither nose nor palate give much away in the way of aroma, but there is some fresh citrus. The palate is refreshing in a rather neutral but very clean way.
title: Domaine Rieflé-Landmann 2014 Pinot Blanc (Alsace)

description: Cherry fruits dominate this fresh wine. It has an attractive perfumed character with spice and acidity adding to the light texture and fruitiness. The wine is ready to drink.
title: Labouré-Roi 2014 Vieilli en Fût de Chêne  (Bourgogne)

description: Cherry fruits dominate this fresh wine. It has an attractive perfumed character with spice and acidity adding to the light texture and fruitiness. The wine is ready to drink.
title: Labouré-Roi 2014 Vieilli en Fût de Chêne  (Bourgogne)

description: A new wine for Aegerter, this is ripe and full-bodied. It has soft apple and crisp pear flavors that are round and lightly textured. The wine is easily ready to drink.
title: Jean-Luc and Paul Aegerter 2013 Chardonnay (Pays d'Oc)

description: A new wine for Aegerter, this is ripe and full-bodied. It has soft apple and crisp pear flavors that are round and lightly textured. The wine is easily ready to drink.
title: Jean-Luc and Paul Aegerter 2013 Chardonnay (Pays d'Oc)

description: This wine is all about acidity and citrus fruits. It is too tight and textured to give immediate pleasure and needs to soften. By late 2016, it should fill out and red-fruit flavors will dominate.
title: Château Pins des Dunes 2015 Rosé (Bordeaux Rosé)

description: This wine is all about acidity and citrus fruits. It is too tight and textured to give immediate pleasure and needs to soften. By late 2016, it should fill out and red-fruit flavors will dominate.
title: Château Pins des Dunes 2015 Rosé (Bordeaux Rosé)

description: With vineyards in the south of the Mâcon region, this estate has produced a simple, fruity and ripe Bourgogne that shows apricot and peach flavors. It is light, direct and immediately easy to drink. Drink now.
title: Château de Lavernette 2014  Bourgogne

description: While the blend ranges widely across Provence, the wine itself is a classic light, fruity rosé. With its tang of citrus, bright acidity and touch of spice, it is a delicious apéritif style wine.
title: Château de Berne 2015 Ludovic de Beauséjour Rosé (Mediterranée)

description: Pale in color, this rosé is soft and gentle. It has caramel and spice flavors that give a piquancy to the smooth, rounded red fruits. The aftertaste is just as soft.
title: Château Carignan 2015 L'Orangerie de Carignan Rosé (Vin de France)

description: With attractive yellow fruits and a soft texture, this wine is immediately drinkable. It has a touch of toastiness (although there is no wood aging) and almond flavors that balance fresh acidity and succulent fruitiness. Drink now.
title: Cave de Lugny 2014 Les Charmes  (Mâcon-Lugny)

description: This is a wine with good, dense and red fruit, a touch of wood and a firm structure. There is a sense of elegance backed up by some weight. The aftertaste brings in spice and balancing acidity.
title: Château des Combes 2008  Bordeaux

description: This is a wine with good, dense and red fruit, a touch of wood and a firm structure. There is a sense of elegance backed up by some weight. The aftertaste brings in spice and balancing acidity.
title: Château des Combes 2008  Bordeaux

description: A blend of Syrah and Carignan, this wine definitely has an unmistakable Languedoc herbaceousness to it amid the bright cherry and red plum flavors. Tightly structured with somewhat bracing acidity and a peppery finish. Drink now.
title: Château Cabezac 2007 La Garrigue Red (Minervois)

description: This wine is well balanced, ripe with apricot and white-peach flavors that contrast with the kiwi and grapefruit freshness. A more mineral edge gives texture. This delicious wine will be even better to drink from 2017.
title: Sylvaine et Alain Normand 2014  Pouilly-Fuissé

description: Packed with strawberry flavors, this ripe wine has plenty of the acidity typical of the vintage along with good fruitiness and structure. The wine is already developing well so drink from 2018.
title: Pierre Cornu Camus 2014 Les Charmières Premier Cru  (Savigny-lès-Beaune)

description: Packed with strawberry flavors, this ripe wine has plenty of the acidity typical of the vintage along with good fruitiness and structure. The wine is already developing well so drink from 2018.
title: Pierre Cornu Camus 2014 Les Charmières Premier Cru  (Savigny-lès-Beaune)

description: Red Chassagne-Montrachet used to be found more than white in the past. This wine has a ripe, earthy character that brings out structure and tannin as well as strawberry fruits. It has a juicy as well as smoky character with spice and solid tannins in the background. Drink from 2019.
title: Philippe Colin 2014 Les Chênes  (Chassagne-Montrachet)

description: Red Chassagne-Montrachet used to be found more than white in the past. This wine has a ripe, earthy character that brings out structure and tannin as well as strawberry fruits. It has a juicy as well as smoky character with spice and solid tannins in the background. Drink from 2019.
title: Philippe Colin 2014 Les Chênes  (Chassagne-Montrachet)

description: This négociant based in the Northern Rhône has turned out a meaty, savory Châteauneuf-du-Pape. It's full bodied and firmly structured, with plenty of clove, leather and peppered beef. Drink 2014–2020.
title: Les Vins de Vienne 2009 Les Otéliées Red (Châteauneuf-du-Pape)

description: The wine is tight with acidity and red-currant fruits. It has structure and tannins as well as the fruitiness. That means the cru needs to age a few months, so drink from mid-2017.
title: Henry Fessy 2015  Côte de Brouilly

description: Rich red cherry, plum and raspberry tones lead the nose of this fruit-forward wine, with hints of cocoa and cola spice dancing in the background. Those notes follow through to the satiny palate, framed by soft tannins that lead into a solid, medium-length finish.
title: La Forge Estate 2015 Pinot Noir (Pays d'Oc)

description: Rich red cherry, plum and raspberry tones lead the nose of this fruit-forward wine, with hints of cocoa and cola spice dancing in the background. Those notes follow through to the satiny palate, framed by soft tannins that lead into a solid, medium-length finish.
title: La Forge Estate 2015 Pinot Noir (Pays d'Oc)

description: A mix of granite and sandy soil give this wine its lightly spicy minerality and soft texture. It is a lively, fruity wine with tannins that are fully integrated into the red-currant fruit and acidity. Drink now.
designation: Domaine de la Madone des Loges
title: Georges Duboeuf 2015 Domaine de la Madone des Loges  (Beaujolais-Villages)

description: Coeur de Presse, the heart of the wine, is a ripe, juicy and fruity wine. It has friendly black-cherry fruit, a soft texture and a just-dry core to give it shape. Drink now.
title: Georges Duboeuf 2015 Coeur de Presse  (Beaujolais-Villages)

description: Aromatic notions of baked apple tart abound on the nose. The palate follows this with appetizing freshness, a mellow note suggesting ripe Red Delicious apples with a dash of kirsch. It's an unusual Gewurztraminer with a very warm finish.
title: Dopff & Irion 2015 Cuvée René Dopff Gewurztraminer (Alsace)

description: Subtitled Vin de Vinarchiste, this is a blended wine from organically grown grapes which include the local Fer and Périgord alongside Bordeaux varieties. It is a crisp wine showing some tight, almost green-pepper flavors as well as smoky acidity. It is young but will be ready to drink soon. Drink from early 2017.
title: Château Tour des Gendres 2015 La Vigne d'Albert Red (Bergerac)

description: Subtitled Vin de Vinarchiste, this is a blended wine from organically grown grapes which include the local Fer and Périgord alongside Bordeaux varieties. It is a crisp wine showing some tight, almost green-pepper flavors as well as smoky acidity. It is young but will be ready to drink soon. Drink from early 2017.
title: Château Tour des Gendres 2015 La Vigne d'Albert Red (Bergerac)

description: This Syrah-Grenache rosé is intensely herbal, with strong notes of thyme, sage, parsley, laurel and lavender, all grounded by a tart cherry character. The palate is pleasantly zippy in acidity and a touch astringent through the close, with notes of orange pith and melon rind that linger nicely. Drink now.
title: Château la Grave 2015 Expression Rosé (Minervois)

description: This crisp wine, flavored with black fruit is lightly tannic and deliciously full of lively fruit. It is full of juicy black-currant fruit and acidity with a soft texture that means it can be drunk now.
title: Château du Cèdre 2014 Chatons du Cèdre Malbec (Cahors)

description: Still with its tannins firmly in place, this is a structured wine. It has a dry core surrounded by bold black fruits and kept in place with acidity. The wine, mainly Malbec with some Merlot added to soften will be ready to drink from 2017.
title: Château de Gaudou 2015 Tradition Malbec-Merlot (Cahors)

description: Generous, juicy and ripe yellow pears are boosted by some residual sweetness that is well balanced by the midpalate texture. Drink soon for maximum fruit.
title: Allimant-Laugner 2015 Pinot Gris (Alsace)

description: A rossignol is a nightingale, an increasingly rare bird but one found in Cahors. The wine certainly sings with its attractive red fruits, soft tannins and bright acidity. With its fruit character, it is ready to drink.
title: Domaine du Prince 2008 Rossignol Malbec-Merlot (Cahors)

description: A rossignol is a nightingale, an increasingly rare bird but one found in Cahors. The wine certainly sings with its attractive red fruits, soft tannins and bright acidity. With its fruit character, it is ready to drink.
title: Domaine du Prince 2008 Rossignol Malbec-Merlot (Cahors)

description: Vibrant and espressive notes of tart red currant, blueberry jam and charred meat compose the bouquet. The palate reveals some developed notes of dried leaves and beef jerky. It's full bodied, with moderate extraction, firm and structured tannins and bright acidity. It has a fairly short finish; drink now until 2014.
title: Domaine la Croix Chaptal 2009 Cuvée Charles Red (Terrasses du Larzac)

description: A full, ripe wine, with delicious white plum, sweet grapefruit and a tense mineral edge. There is a great texture from fruit tannins, boosted by intense shots of acidity. Age for another year or two.
title: Guy Saget 2008 Le Domaine Saget  (Pouilly-Fumé)

description: A concentrated, rich wine, packed with peach and pear flavors, the freshness coming from ripe apples and green plums. While the fruit dominates, there is always a good edge of minerality, tightening the wine, giving it a taut, crisp aftertaste.
title: Domaine Thomas & Fils 2008 Grand'Chaille  (Sancerre)
