description: Silex is the French name for the flint over limestone soil that occurs in the Sancerre and Pouilly regions. There is a definite character of tight texture in this wine, very mineral while it also has ripe fruit. This is a new wine from Fournier, an impressive addition to the range.
title: Fournier Père et Fils 2008 Cuvée Silex  (Sancerre)

description: Still very crisp and fruity with only a hint of maturity, this is a bright, apple- and citrus-driven wine. Light and stylish, it gets its generous minerality from the Chardonnay in the blend. While it's great now, it will be even better from 2018.
title: Deutz 2006 Amour de Deutz Brut  (Champagne)

description: Still very crisp and fruity with only a hint of maturity, this is a bright, apple- and citrus-driven wine. Light and stylish, it gets its generous minerality from the Chardonnay in the blend. While it's great now, it will be even better from 2018.
title: Deutz 2006 Amour de Deutz Brut  (Champagne)

description: Produced from vines high up the Grand Cru slope, this wine is finely textured and stylish while also full-bodied. It has weight, spice from wood aging, precise acidity and a strongly mineral, salty edge. Drink from 2021.
title: La Chablisienne 2014 Les Preuses Grand Cru  (Chablis)

description: Produced from old vines in the Grand Cru vineyards of Chouilly in the Côte des Blancs, this is a beautifully crisp, ripe wine, showing taut fruit and fine, stylish acidity. As a Special Club bottling, it adheres to stringent qualitative guidelines set out by an elite group of growers. Still young, it will be best from 2019.
designation: Special Club Blanc de Blancs Chouilly Grand Cru Brut
title: Roland Champion 2011 Special Club Blanc de Blancs Chouilly Grand Cru Brut Chardonnay (Champagne)

description: What this mature, ripe wine has lost in fruit, it has gained in richness and complexity. Its toasty, nutty character attracts, along with its tight acidity and taut, nervy texture. Nicely evolved and well-balanced, it is ready to drink now.
title: H. Blin 2008 Millésime Brut  (Champagne)

description: This wine, though still young, reveals much about the Deutz style as well as the vintage. It strikes a balance between softness and crispness that fits the ethos of the house. At the same time, it's an attractive medium-term bottling, in line with what many producers acheived in 2010. It should be kept until 2019.
title: Deutz 2010 Brut  (Champagne)

description: Always a popular vineyard, Beaune Grèves has produces a full, ripe, intense wine. It shows some signs of wood aging as well as rich strawberry and red plum. It's delicious already, but this full and complex wine deserves aging. Drink now –2025.
title: Jean-Claude Boisset 2011 Les Grèves Premier Cru  (Beaune)

description: This is a smooth, rich wine with a dosage that adds enough sweetness to balance creamy apple flavors marked with sharp acidity. Ripe yet elegantly balanced, it's maturing well. It can be drunk now, but a year or two of waiting will serve it well. Drink now–2016.
title: Jacquart 2005 Cuvée Vintage Brut  (Champagne)

description: This rich and creamy vintage wine boasts soft apples, fresh acidity and a fine, tight texture. There's just a hint of toast to round out the palate and add complexity. It could improve with age further, so drink through 2020.
title: Piper-Heidsieck 2006 Vintage Brut  (Champagne)

description: Bright and fruity, this is a crisp, herbal wine. From the Bougrier family estate it is perfumed, creamy and offers refreshing acidity, citrus and hints of apricots. The wine is ready to drink.
title: Bougrier 2015 Domaine Guenault Sauvignon Blanc (Touraine)

description: This rare intrusion of Sauvignon Blanc into Burgundy is in the small northern vineyard of Saint-Bris, close to Chablis. This wine is fruity with a herbal character that is balanced by the crisp citrus and melon flavors. Drink the wine now.
title: Bailly-Lapierre 2015  Saint-Bris

description: This is an attractively ripe wine that shows the richness of the vintage well. It has yellow fruits along with touches of sultana and sliced apple. The wine is fruity, soft and ready to drink.
title: Maison Stéphane Brocard 2015 Closerie des Alisiers  (Bourgogne)

description: Warm, rounded and open style of wine with attractive fruits, hints of raisins and a smoky character. Not for aging.
title: Henry Fessy 2009  Côte de Brouilly

description: Warm, rounded and open style of wine with attractive fruits, hints of raisins and a smoky character. Not for aging.
title: Henry Fessy 2009  Côte de Brouilly

description: La Nerthe's white is a blend of Clairette, Bourboulenc, Roussanne and Grenache Blanc. The result is a slightly floral wine that's full bodied yet lacking flesh on the midpalate. The apricot and citrus flavors finish with surprising freshness.
title: Château La Nerthe 2009 White (Châteauneuf-du-Pape)

description: This is a medium-bodied, fruit-driven Syrah that seems built for immediate consumption. Black cherry fruit is in the lead, with hints of chocolate and lavender to spice things up. Eminently quaffable, with bright fruit and a lingering finish.
title: Vignobles La Coterie 2009  Saint-Joseph

description: This is a plump, medium-bodied rosé, vibrant with confected berry fruit and undertones of mossy stones and peppery spice. Should be versatile at the table, as it's fresh enough to handle fish yet intense enough to partner grilled meats.
title: Les Vignes des Prêcheurs 2010  Tavel

description: By contrast with some of the other powerful reds from Triguedina, this is a relatively soft, velvet-textured wine. But don't be deceived: beneath the smooth surface, there is a dark and mineral wine, all solid fruits and rich black berries.
designation: Clos Triguedina La Chapelle du Clos
title: Jean-Luc Baldès 2008 Clos Triguedina La Chapelle du Clos Malbec (Cahors)

description: By contrast with some of the other powerful reds from Triguedina, this is a relatively soft, velvet-textured wine. But don't be deceived: beneath the smooth surface, there is a dark and mineral wine, all solid fruits and rich black berries.
designation: Clos Triguedina La Chapelle du Clos
title: Jean-Luc Baldès 2008 Clos Triguedina La Chapelle du Clos Malbec (Cahors)

description: A richly textured wine, showing some attractive fresh fruits and soft berries mingling with a layer of firmer tannins. The wine has weight, an attractive edge of spice and a final sweet juicy character.
title: Château Plaisance 2006  Montagne-Saint-Émilion

description: A high toast wine, the fruit and fresh acidity submerged beneath the wood. At the present, it is hard to enjoy, but in 2–3 years the fruit will kick in. It would be good if the producer had been less enthusiastic about the wood.
title: Château de Candale 2007  Saint-Émilion

description: Cherry fruits and firm tannins band well together in this rich wine. It offers spice from light wood aging, a touch of banana, and full forward fruitiness. The structure suggests it needs to age for a year.
title: Jean-Claude Debeaune 2011 Domaine Mont Chavy  (Morgon)

description: A deliciously creamy wine, shining with apple and grapefruit flavors. The wine is light, bright, softly textured and hinting at wood aging, while displaying a more steely line of tight acidity at the end.
title: Manuel Olivier 2010  Bourgogne Hautes Côtes de Nuits

description: The red-fruit flavors on the nose almost have a candied edge, akin to red-berry candy. The palate adds lots of freshness and a finely fizzing mousse on its light fruit-driven body. The finish is refreshing, dry and echoes with fruit.
title: Lucien Albrecht NV Brut Rosé Sparkling (Crémant d'Alsace)

description: The red-fruit flavors on the nose almost have a candied edge, akin to red-berry candy. The palate adds lots of freshness and a finely fizzing mousse on its light fruit-driven body. The finish is refreshing, dry and echoes with fruit.
title: Lucien Albrecht NV Brut Rosé Sparkling (Crémant d'Alsace)

description: Appetizing notes of strawberry and Red Delicious apple create an inviting opening. These same flavors play on the very frothy, totally fruit-driven but dry palate. This is fresh and refreshing and with its fruit-forward style, it's an ideal pale-pink drink for summer parties.
title: Jean-Baptiste Adam NV Brut Rosé Sparkling (Crémant d'Alsace)

description: Brisk lemon freshness sets the tone on the nose. The very frothy mousse on the palate continues in this fruity, exuberant and fresh vein. The finish is superclean, brisk and dry, creating an ideal and invigorating apéritif-style for summer days.
title: André Kientzler 2013 Cuvée MIllésimée Non Dosée Sparkling (Crémant d'Alsace)

description: Fine, elegant wine, packed with delicious strawberry flavors, sweetness and richness. At the core are firm tannins, but these are almost crowded out by the ripe fruit.
title: Henri de Villamont 2008 Les Feusselottes Premier Cru  (Chambolle-Musigny)

description: A big, bold and fruity wine that is full of ripe berry fruits, rich and generous. This is Beaujolais at its most exuberant, a celebration of delicious fruit. It could age, but is ready to drink.
title: Georges Duboeuf 2009 Domaine des Rosiers  (Moulin-à-Vent)

description: A smoky, intensely flavored wine that is ripe and opulent. The tannins are beautifully integrated into the powerful texture of sweet berry fruits, intense acidity and sumptuous aftertaste. Age for 3–4 years.
title: Maison Champy 2008 Les Taillepieds Premier Cru  (Volnay)

description: The 2015s from the Tavel cooperative universally impressed. This cuvée, drawn from terroirs dominated by galets roulés, combines notes of crushed stones and ripe cherries. It's still tight and primary; like many good Tavels, it should drink better two years from the harvest than it does now.
title: Les Vignerons de Tavel 2015 Cuvée Royale  (Tavel)

description: A ripe, still very young wine that has a rich, almost honeyed character while remaining bone dry and tightly textured. There is a mineral character to this wine that should disappear as it ages leaving the ripe pear and apple flavors and the elusive touch of honey. Drink from 2020.
title: Domaine du Petit Métris 2014 Clos de la Marche  (Savennières)

description: A ripe, still very young wine that has a rich, almost honeyed character while remaining bone dry and tightly textured. There is a mineral character to this wine that should disappear as it ages leaving the ripe pear and apple flavors and the elusive touch of honey. Drink from 2020.
title: Domaine du Petit Métris 2014 Clos de la Marche  (Savennières)

description: This is part of a series of wines named after the subsoil in which the vines are planted. The soil in this case is formed from igneous rocks. It gives a fine, pure wine that has great richness as well as fresh apple and pear flavors. The wine with just that extra few months aging is ready to drink.
title: Domaine de l'Ecu 2014 Orthogneiss  (Muscadet Sèvre et Maine)

description: This small production wine is the equivalent of a second wine for Count Leo de Malet-Roquefort's Premier Grand Cru Classé estate. The wine is smooth, elegant and ripe. Black plums and perfumed acidity are accompanied by some wood aging flavors and fresher black-currant fruitiness. It is a sophisticated wine that still needs to age. Drink from 2019.
title: Château la Gaffelière 2012 Clos Gaffelière  (Saint-Émilion)

description: There are attractive floral and garrigue tones to the subtle fruit core of this wine, with hints of white cherry, melon rind and strawberry hull. The lively palate offers brisk acidity and lively tart-fruit flavors. A touch of white chocolate echos on the medium-length finish.
title: Domaine Montrose 2013 Rosé (Côtes de Thongue)

description: There are attractive floral and garrigue tones to the subtle fruit core of this wine, with hints of white cherry, melon rind and strawberry hull. The lively palate offers brisk acidity and lively tart-fruit flavors. A touch of white chocolate echos on the medium-length finish.
title: Domaine Montrose 2013 Rosé (Côtes de Thongue)

description: A crushed carnation aroma accents the ripe fruit core of strawberry, raspberry and mango on this selection. The palate is juicy and fruit forward, with red berry flavors, medium acidity and a subtle earthy spice that unfolds on the finish.
title: Domaine Cabirau 2013 Rosé (Côtes du Roussillon)

description: A crushed carnation aroma accents the ripe fruit core of strawberry, raspberry and mango on this selection. The palate is juicy and fruit forward, with red berry flavors, medium acidity and a subtle earthy spice that unfolds on the finish.
title: Domaine Cabirau 2013 Rosé (Côtes du Roussillon)

description: Here's a friendly, accessible and value-priced rosé that's perfect for warm-weather entertaining. Ripe cherry, plum and raspberry flood the nose and mouth, with a soft dusting of cocoa that adds interest and decadence. The ripe flavors are full and jammy, but balanced by medium acidity that keeps the palate fresh and the finish clean.
title: Château Cabezac 2012 La Tradition Rosé (Minervois)

description: This is brilliantly fruity, very crisp and fragrant, with delicious spice, perfumed red fruits and lively acidity. It's very dry, with a fresh aftertaste.
title: Vignoble de la Jarnoterie 2013 Quintessence  (Saint-Nicolas-de-Bourgueil)

description: The lightly intense bouquet is laced with nuances of hard, underripe peach, yellow flower and a soft mineral streak. Medium weight but fresh and lively, with a clean, slightly tart finish reminiscent of lemon and green plum flavors.
title: Jean-Luc Colombo 2010 La Violette Viognier (Vin de Pays d'Oc)

description: Jammy strawberry and raspberry notes fill the nose and mouth, and a soft accent of chocolate-covered cherry adds just the right amount of decadence. A slight peppery lift keeps things vibrant on the finish.
title: The Frenchhouse 2010 Pinot Noir (Vin de Pays d'Oc)

description: A lovely floral streak adds interest to the bright red-berry and ripe rhubarb aromas. Cherry-skin and rich strawberry flavors fill the palate and remain through the clean finish. Light weight with soft tannins and an easy demeanor.
title: Les Vignerons de la Méditerranée 2010 Réserve St. Martin Pinot Noir (Pays d'Oc)

description: With superripe fruit, fat and glossy, with rich white fruits, round, dense and concentrated, this is a wine to ooze into the glass. It is perhaps not very Chablis, but delicious as a fine Chardonnay.
title: Simonnet-Febvre 2005 Vaillons Premier Cru  (Chablis)

description: This wine has spice, concentrated yellow fruits and a delicious backbone of acidity. With its acidity firmly in place, the wine is beginning to reveal the richer yellow fruit and tangy lemon. Already delicious, it will be better from 2017.
title: Domaine de la Croix Senaillet 2014  Saint-Véran

description: This wine has spice, concentrated yellow fruits and a delicious backbone of acidity. With its acidity firmly in place, the wine is beginning to reveal the richer yellow fruit and tangy lemon. Already delicious, it will be better from 2017.
title: Domaine de la Croix Senaillet 2014  Saint-Véran

description: This family domaine has produced a rich, structured wine from its holding in Vosne-Romanée. It is firm, dark and concentrated with rich tannins and red-berry fruit. Spice, acidity and a dense aftertaste promise aging. Drink from 2018.
title: Domaine Coquard Loisson-Fleurot 2014  Vosne-Romanée

description: This ripe and full wine has hints of toast and baked bread along with rich apricot and peach flavors. The texture is warm while the aromatic aftertaste is immediately attractive.
title: Marcel Couturier 2014 Le Clos Reyssie  (Pouilly-Fuissé)

description: This wine has both structure and ripe red-plum fruits. It is dark and dense, solid and with good acidity. A clear line of freshness promises a good future. This needs time, so don't drink before 2020.
title: Louis Latour 2014 Epenots Premier Cru  (Pommard)

description: This tangy, perfumed single-vineyard wine also has some ripe fruit. A zesty character dominates at this early stage, leaving room for richer yellow fruits to come through in time. The wine has good potential, so wait until 2017 to drink.
title: Jean Rijckaert 2014 Les Bouthières  (Pouilly-Fuissé)

description: Old vines planted in a small parcel at the base of the Corton hill give this ripe and rich wine. Full of jammy fruit, it has structure as well as strawberry and red-cherry flavors, packed with juiciness that comes from the acidity. This wine has a good future. Drink from 2020.
title: Château de Santenay 2014 Les Brunettes et Planchots  (Aloxe-Corton)

description: This is a juicy wine, packed with red fruits. It has acidity along with an edge of tannins. The attractive fruitiness suggests the wine will develop quickly. Drink from 2019.
title: Bouchard Aîné et Fils 2014 Clos du Roi Premier Cru  (Beaune)

description: A normal five-barrel production was cut to two because of hail. This wine is firm, with hints of the generosity of the appellation waiting behind the dry texture. It's structured, with acidity and plum skins that will take some time. Drink from 2019.
title: Alex Gambal 2014  Volnay

description: Fresh strawberry flavors, followed by some vanilla and sweet acidity characterize this wine from the Lagrezette winery. With its blend of Malbec, Syrah and white Viognier, this has softness, ripeness and, despite its acidity, a definite sweet finish.
title: Château Lagrézette 2007 Zette Rosé Malbec (Vin de Pays du Lot)

description: A simple, unoaked Malbec that shows the earthy character, black fruit and high acidity of the grape. It's a straightforward wine, its acidity masking ripe fruits and a layer of dry tannin.
title: Château la Caminade 2006 Malbec (Vin de Pays du Lot)

description: Crisp and elegant in feel, this has apricot and peach flavors that are balanced by the tight structure and the green-fruit-like acidity. The layers of toast have integrated with the ebullient fruit character and the taut, minerally finish. For aging 3–4 years.
title: Olivier Leflaive 2010 Dents du Chien Premier Cru  (Saint-Aubin)

description: Crisp and elegant in feel, this has apricot and peach flavors that are balanced by the tight structure and the green-fruit-like acidity. The layers of toast have integrated with the ebullient fruit character and the taut, minerally finish. For aging 3–4 years.
title: Olivier Leflaive 2010 Dents du Chien Premier Cru  (Saint-Aubin)

description: This is a rich, rounded wine, yet it also expresses a tight texture and nervy acidity. The toast influence is still dominating, although the fruitiness of this ripe selection is also showing. With its weight and structure, this is a prime candidate to age for several years.
title: Olivier Leflaive 2010 Charmes Premier Cru  (Meursault)

description: This is a rich, rounded wine, yet it also expresses a tight texture and nervy acidity. The toast influence is still dominating, although the fruitiness of this ripe selection is also showing. With its weight and structure, this is a prime candidate to age for several years.
title: Olivier Leflaive 2010 Charmes Premier Cru  (Meursault)

description: This wine shows the structured side of Gevrey-Chambertin. The vineyard is situated at the opening of a small side valley, a location that allows the grapes to ripen slowly. This is elegant and structured, and it's full of solid tannins as well as cherry and red berry flavors. Age this for 7–8 years.
title: Albert Bichot 2010 Lavaux Saint-Jacques Premier Cru  (Gevrey-Chambertin)

description: Currently dominated by tannins, this wine is rich and structured, and it demonstrates the potential of its huge fruit and weight. The final note of this age-worthy wine is smokiness from wood aging.
title: Domaine Champy 2010  Corton-Rognet

description: Round, opulent and generous, this wine has yellow-fruit flavors that are paired with lime-like acidity, creating a balanced feel. The toast note is still showing strongly, and it needs a few years to settle.
title: Olivier Leflaive 2010 Referts Premier Cru  (Puligny-Montrachet)

description: Round, opulent and generous, this wine has yellow-fruit flavors that are paired with lime-like acidity, creating a balanced feel. The toast note is still showing strongly, and it needs a few years to settle.
title: Olivier Leflaive 2010 Referts Premier Cru  (Puligny-Montrachet)

description: This is a closed, smoke-filled wine, and its tannins and toasty wood character currently dominate, which gives it a bitter edge. It has richness, with hints of juicy fruit that sit under the structure. Give it at least six years.
title: L. Tramier & Fils 2009 Collection  (Corton)

description: Big, bold and cuddly, this wine's tannins are cushioned by the red berry fruit and attractive acidity. It has weight and a rich feeling, and the dry edge offers the possibility of aging. This small clos is exclusive to Jaffelin.
designation: Sur les Grèves Clos Saint-Anne Premier Cru
title: Jaffelin 2009 Sur les Grèves Clos Saint-Anne Premier Cru  (Beaune)

description: Big, bold and cuddly, this wine's tannins are cushioned by the red berry fruit and attractive acidity. It has weight and a rich feeling, and the dry edge offers the possibility of aging. This small clos is exclusive to Jaffelin.
designation: Sur les Grèves Clos Saint-Anne Premier Cru
title: Jaffelin 2009 Sur les Grèves Clos Saint-Anne Premier Cru  (Beaune)

description: This is as serious as Provence rosé can get. It is a limited production wine, selected from the best Grenache (75%) and Syrah (25%) parcels. Structured and impressively dense, its red fruits are concentrated, bone-dry and with a textured character. It is ready to drink although it will become richer from early 2016. The Sumeire family arrived in the Sainte Victoire mountain range in the 13th century.
title: Château Coussin 2014 Cuvée César à Sumeire Rosé (Côtes de Provence Sainte-Victoire)

description: With its wonderful poise between dark structure and intensely fragrant fruit, this is firm, dry and packed with ripe blackberry fruits. It has great potential, as befits a concentrated wine from Vosne-Romanée, and is certainly not ready to drink before 2020.
title: Roche de Bellene 2012 Vieilles Vignes  (Vosne-Romanée)

description: With its wonderful poise between dark structure and intensely fragrant fruit, this is firm, dry and packed with ripe blackberry fruits. It has great potential, as befits a concentrated wine from Vosne-Romanée, and is certainly not ready to drink before 2020.
title: Roche de Bellene 2012 Vieilles Vignes  (Vosne-Romanée)

description: Closed up and just hinting at its great potential, this wine is showing tannins and a dry, solid core. Slowly it reveals delicious, opulent red berry fruits and concentrated texture. It needs a lot of time before drinking; wait until 2019.
title: Roche de Bellene 2012 Vieilles Vignes  (Morey-Saint-Denis)

description: This beautifully perfumed wine has rounded tannins finely integrated into the opulent red cherry fruit. It's already a delicious wine, juicy and fragrant, although still with a long future. If you can wait, drink it from 2018.
title: Roche de Bellene 2012 Pitures Premier Cru  (Volnay)

description: The Marconnets vineyard on the slopes above Savigny-lès-Beaune produces some of the most perfumed wines in the appellation. This is typical, a wonderful medley of juicy, fruity aromas. It is still young, although temptingly attractive now. Drink ideally from 2018.
title: Roche de Bellene 2012 Les Marconnets Premier Cru  (Savigny-lès-Beaune)

description: Made from 60-year-old vines from a property next door to Vosne-Romanée, this wine is both structured and rich. It has dark tannins, with juicy and jammy plum fruits that are layered with acidity. It is still firm, dense and needs time. Drink from 2020.
title: Roche de Bellene 2012 Aux Boudots Premier Cru  (Nuits-St.-Georges)

description: Onion-skin pink in color, this wood-aged wine is opulent and ripe. It is textured, with generous red fruits that are given a great lift by the spice and pepper that fill the mouth and give the wine power and richness. The acidity is well integrated, finishing the wine with freshness. A far cry from so many fruity rosés, this is a serious wine.
title: Château d'Esclans 2013 Garrus Rosé (Côtes de Provence)

description: The fruit here is pure, fresh with the merest hints of its future richness. The green fruits, citrus and acidity are prominent, with a hint of toast and a finishing line of minerality. It needs to age, so drink from 2017.
title: Domaine Vrignaud 2013 Les Vaupulans Fourchaume Premier Cru  (Chablis)

description: The fruit here is pure, fresh with the merest hints of its future richness. The green fruits, citrus and acidity are prominent, with a hint of toast and a finishing line of minerality. It needs to age, so drink from 2017.
title: Domaine Vrignaud 2013 Les Vaupulans Fourchaume Premier Cru  (Chablis)

description: Light and fresh, this is a crisp, red berry flavored wine with lively acidity and a dry, bright aftertaste. Ready to drink.
title: Domaine Houchart 2013 Rosé (Côtes de Provence)

description: An herbal, very crisp wine, it is unoaked and very bright. It's fresh, fruity, light in color and with citrus fruits running right through. Drink now.
title: Commanderie de la Bargemone 2013 White (Coteaux d'Aix-en-Provence)

description: Tight, zingy and crisp, this wine has fresh, citrus character that comes right up front. It is light and fruity, with raspberries and red currants. With its very dry aftertaste, it is for food.
title: Ravoire et Fils 2013 Domaine la Rabiotte Rosé (Coteaux d'Aix-en-Provence)

description: An extremely lively mousse gives this wine an instant festive character. It also brightens the already fresh, crisp red berry fruits and acidity. It's totally ready to drink.
title: Pierre Sparr NV Brut Rosé Sparkling (Crémant d'Alsace)

description: A very fruity, floral wine, it's lightly spicy while showing white fruits and citrus right up front. It is dry but the fruitiness gives the wine a lively feel and a soft aftertaste. Drink now.
title: Pierre Sparr 2012 Pinot Blanc (Alsace)

description: This is only Brut in name, because it is actually a medium-sweet wine that maintains pear freshness. It's ripe, full in the mouth and ready to drink.
designation: Comte de Rinken Blanc de Blancs Brut
title: Pierre and Charles Sparr NV Comte de Rinken Blanc de Blancs Brut Pinot Blanc (Crémant d'Alsace)

description: This is an unusually toasty Pinot Blanc. Wood flavors add another dimension but cover the natural spice and fruit of the grape.
title: Pierre and Charles Sparr 2011 Cuvée Tradition Pinot Blanc (Alsace)

description: Crisp fruit is broadened by caramel flavors and soft acidity. Ripe red cherries dominate along with a smooth texture. This is a fine apéritif style, ready to drink.
title: Domaine Sainte-Marie 2013 Vie Vité Rosé (Côtes de Provence)

description: Crisp fruit is broadened by caramel flavors and soft acidity. Ripe red cherries dominate along with a smooth texture. This is a fine apéritif style, ready to drink.
title: Domaine Sainte-Marie 2013 Vie Vité Rosé (Côtes de Provence)

description: A fresh wine with juicy red fruits, but weighed down by harsh tannins. The mouthfeel is dry, just bitter. It's only in the finish that good fruit acidity shows through.
title: Château d'Arnaussan 2004  Bordeaux

description: This wine is all fruit, with bright acidity and refreshing apple and Rocha pear flavors. It is juicy, light and crisp, a fine apéritif style with its perfumed final acidity. Drink now.
title: Michel Vattan 2014 Tradition  (Sancerre)

description: With its origins in the 17th century, this estate has 50 acres. This red with its ripe tannins and juicy red-berry fruits has the weight to give richness as well as fruit. A good structure supports the fruit while remaining discretely in the background. Drink now.
title: Domaine Roger Champault 2014 Les Pierris  (Sancerre)

description: Soft Pinot Noir gives this warm, rounded wine. Red-berry fruits are freshly cut with acidity while keeping the fruitiness to the fore. This bright, juicy wine is ready to drink.
title: Domaine Pellé 2014 Morogues Rosé (Menetou-Salon)

description: Based in Bué, one of the top villages of Sancerre, this producer has made a ripe, crisp and nervy wine that comes from chalk soil. Tangy with a mineral texture, it offers rich currant and lime flavors and full-throated final acidity. Drink now.
title: Domaine Franck Millet 2014  Sancerre

description: Based in Bué, one of the top villages of Sancerre, this producer has made a ripe, crisp and nervy wine that comes from chalk soil. Tangy with a mineral texture, it offers rich currant and lime flavors and full-throated final acidity. Drink now.
title: Domaine Franck Millet 2014  Sancerre

description: Ripe, soft and full bodied, this wine has fresh citrus and gooseberry flavors along with zesty lemon and a bright aftertaste. It needs a few more months to fill out, so drink from 2017.
title: Domaine Cédrick Bardin 2014  Pouilly-Fumé

description: This is a fruity wine, full of herbal and apple flavors. The vines are planted on slopes across the Loire from Sancerre, giving minerality as well as juicy acidity. Young and fresh, the wine will benefit from waiting a few months more. Drink from early 2017.
title: Clement et Florian Berthier 2014 Sauvignon Blanc (Coteaux du Giennois)

description: This wine is unusually taut and crisp for a Châteauneuf-du-Pape, with cherry and cranberry fruit framed by hints of earth and leather. Drink now–2020.
title: Les Trois Couronnes 2013 Red (Châteauneuf-du-Pape)

description: This wine is unusually taut and crisp for a Châteauneuf-du-Pape, with cherry and cranberry fruit framed by hints of earth and leather. Drink now–2020.
title: Les Trois Couronnes 2013 Red (Châteauneuf-du-Pape)

description: This is a very feline wine with tight citrus and gooseberry fruits that are almost too intense for its own good.
title: Château des Gravières 2012  Bordeaux Blanc

description: This is a very feline wine with tight citrus and gooseberry fruits that are almost too intense for its own good.
title: Château des Gravières 2012  Bordeaux Blanc

description: Juicy and fruity, this wine has strong layers of acidity and extracted tannins. It has a hard, austere character that doesn't promise for the future.
title: Château du Lort 2011  Bordeaux Supérieur

description: Dry, firmly structured and tough, this is an austere wine that doesn't hold out much hope for improvement. Drink it soon with rich food to balance out its dense tannins and wood flavors.
title: Château du Cros 2011  Bordeaux

description: This wine seems rather unfocused with indistinct tannins and fruit. There is a soapy texture, and the red berry fruits seem awash with acidity.
title: Château Bernés 2011  Bordeaux

description: There is way too much acidity here, and it's exagerrated by the wine's soft, unfocused texture. Notes of bitter toast and dark tannins are rather unbalanced.
title: Château Ballan-Larquette 2011  Bordeaux

description: This warm fruity wine is rounded and ripe with flavors of vanilla as well as red-berry fruits. It is soft with just a light tang of orange zest and finishing acidity. Drink this attractive wine now.
title: Jérôme Gueneau 2016 Domaine des Grandes Perrières Rosé (Sancerre)

description: This deliciously perfumed wine originates from a small appellation west of Sancerre. With its crisp texture and aromatic Sauvignon Blanc grapes, it is a wine to appreciate as an apéritif rather than drink with food.
title: Jean-Michel Sorbe 2015  Quincy

description: A deliciously ripe and soft wine, this is also fruity and with a fine tang of clementine. There is a refreshing side to the red-currant fruitiness and intense acidity. It is lightly perfumed and finished with a touch of pepper. Drink now.
title: Mirabeau 2016 Pure Rosé (Côtes de Provence)

description: This soft wine has attractive red-berry flavors. They are given a lift by the bright acidity. It is a gentle wine, ideal for an apéritif with just the lightest tang at the end.
title: Mas de Cadenet 2016 Arbaude Rosé (Côtes de Provence)

description: This is a delicious and fruity wine with attractive acidity and bright, ebullient character—it's just waiting for summer. The up-front red fruits and acidity are well in balance. This is ready to drink.
title: Les Vignobles Gueissard 2016 Les Papilles Rosé (Côtes de Provence)

description: Sweet pear perfumes announce a ripe style of white wine. It is on the soft side, its acidity well under the pear and melon flavors, aided by nutmeg and tangerines. The finish is juicy, ripe, always soft.
title: Château le Bonnat 2006  Graves

description: A blend of Loin de l'Oeil, Mauzac and Sauvignon Blanc, this needs the shot of acidity from the Sauvignon—it gives a real lift to the ripe apricot fruits. The wine is structured, quite tight with apple skin flavors, creating an appetizing, juicy finish.
title: Domaine des Terrisses 2007 Grand Tradition White (Gaillac)

description: A spicy, perfumed, soft wine. The hint of wood opens the wine and provides vanilla, lychee, ginger and artichoke flavors. The downside is a lack of freshness in a wine that feels quite fat.
title: Domaine des Terrisses 2006 Blanc Sec Terre Originelle White (Gaillac)

description: This wine is quiet at first, with tight scents of dark berries, black currant leaf and German chocolate cake. A pleasant tartness enlivens the slightly round palate, expressed in hints of cassis and underripe black cherry. Ample tannins provide some structure, with a medium-length finish.
title: Marius 2016 Grenache-Syrah (Pays d'Oc)

description: This wine is smooth, mature and rich with yellow fruits and a rounded texture. A hint of wood and spice has plenty of crisp acidity to balance. Drink now.
title: Marcel Couturier 2015 Les Longues Terres  (Mâcon-Loché)

description: This is a tight, textured wine, with plenty of acidity to balance the ripe fruit. It has the generous texture typical of the vintage and ripe yellow fruits, with an attractive crisp aftertaste. Drink now.
title: Marcel Couturier 2015 Le Clos Reyssie  (Pouilly-Fuissé)

description: This is a tight, textured wine, with plenty of acidity to balance the ripe fruit. It has the generous texture typical of the vintage and ripe yellow fruits, with an attractive crisp aftertaste. Drink now.
title: Marcel Couturier 2015 Le Clos Reyssie  (Pouilly-Fuissé)

description: This tangy, ripe and fruity wine is crisp with acidity. It's attractively brimming with fruit and ready to drink.
title: Louis Max 2016  Mâcon-Villages

description: This large appellation in the Côte Chalonnaise can produce fruity wines like this. With red-berry fruits and light tannins, the wine has spice and crisp edge of acidity that comes from fruit that was just ripe, surprising in the rich 2015 vintage. The wine will be ready to drink from 2018.
title: L. Tramier & Fils 2015 Laurent Dufouleur Château Mi-Pont  (Mercurey)

description: Touches of crushed purple violets add depth and interest to the brambly black berry and raspberry core of this lush wine. Hints of menthol and charred oak dance in the background, with flavors of cherry skin and blackberry taking centerstage on the solidly structured palate.
title: Fortant 2016 Coast Select Cabernet Sauvignon (Pays d'Oc)

description: Showcasing the rich vintage, this is a generous fruit-driven wine. With red-berry flavors and plenty of acidity to balance, the wine is soft and juicy. Drink it from 2018.
title: Domaines Devillard 2015 Le Renard  (Bourgogne)

description: Wood aromas and spice show strongly in this wine. On the palate, there is a toasty character that gives a bitter edge to the ripe red fruits. That needs to go, so wait to drink this wine from 2019.
title: Domaines Devillard 2015 Domaine de la Ferté  (Givry)

description: This Chardonnay-based wine, with 10% Chenin Blanc, opens with aromas of pressed yellow flowers, peach blossom and just-ripe tropical fruit. There's good zip to the bright fruit flavors, finishing fresh and clean. Drink now.
title: Domaine Rives-Blanques 2016 White (Pays d'Oc)

description: A crisp, tangy and mineral-driven wine, this is also ripe with generous citrus and apple flavors. The texture is still tight. which will allow it to age. Drink from 2018.
title: Domaine de l'Echelette 2016 La Belouse  (Mâcon-Cruzille)

description: Crisp apple aromas lead to a spicy, yellow and melon-flavored wine. With its touches of vanilla and warm, ripe character, the wine is full and generous. Drink now.
title: Domaine Bernard Moreau 2016  Bourgogne

description: This is a crisp, lightly wooded wine. Tangy texture and mineral acidity are part of the lively character of this still young, zesty bottling. Drink from 2018.
title: Clos des Rocs 2016 En Près Forêt  (Mâcon-Loché)

description: This is a wine that tastes of the wild herbs and pines that surround the vineyard. It is spicy, perfumed with the contrast of the crisp green fruit. Low-yielding vines have produced a wine with concentration and plenty of tangy citrus and lime zest. Drink now.
title: Château Rimauresq 2016 Cru Classé White (Côtes de Provence)

description: This is a rounded and rich wine, packed with citrus fruits and delicious acidity. Lemon and orange-zest flavors balance well with the mineral texture. Drink from 2018.
title: Cave de Lugny 2016 Les Charmes  (Mâcon-Lugny)

description: Attractive and fruity, this warm wine is crisp and fresh at the same time. Yellow fruits and tangy orange zest are complemented by minerality and a refreshing aftertaste. It is ready to drink.
title: Louis Chevallier 2014  Saint-Véran

description: In this wine, herbal, green flavors bring out a bright, fruity character. It's fresh and crisp, while also having ripe green fruits and a light touch of spice. Drink now.
title: Roland Tissier et Fils 2014 Tradition  (Sancerre)

description: This wine is soft, lightly fruity and refreshing. Apple and ripe pear flavors contrast with the textured acidity. It's a balanced wine, full of fruitiness and ready to drink now.
title: Domaine Sautereau 2014 Côte de Reigny  (Sancerre)

description: This wine is soft, lightly fruity and refreshing. Apple and ripe pear flavors contrast with the textured acidity. It's a balanced wine, full of fruitiness and ready to drink now.
title: Domaine Sautereau 2014 Côte de Reigny  (Sancerre)

description: Chorey vineyards, on the plain close to Beaune, often produce good-value wines. This attractive wine is a good example from an uneven vintage. It has structure and fruit, maybe not enough, along with a fresh, tangy character. It is developing fast, so drink from 2017.
title: Domaine Maillard 2013  Chorey-lès-Beaune

description: This fruity, light wine is full of red berries. The tannins are there, playing a supporting role to the intense fruitiness and acidity that's typical of the vintage. This wine will develop quickly, so drink from 2017.
title: Domaine Belland 2013 Charmes  (Santenay)

description: This wine is dry and smoky, with tannins that will allow it to age. The fruit, though, only hints at red berry fruits and should be more developed for a simple appellation wine such as this. Drink from 2017.
title: Château de Santenay 2012 Vieille Vignes  (Bourgogne)

description: This wine is dry and smoky, with tannins that will allow it to age. The fruit, though, only hints at red berry fruits and should be more developed for a simple appellation wine such as this. Drink from 2017.
title: Château de Santenay 2012 Vieille Vignes  (Bourgogne)

description: Laudun is considered one of the top communes for white varieties in the Southern Rhône. This cuvée, from the region's cooperative cellar, is a vibrant, refreshing wine that combines modest pineapple fruit, with hints of wet stone and honey. Drink now.
title: Laudun Chusclan 2013 Cinq Cépages White (Côtes du Rhône)

description: A smooth, deliciously drinkable blend of Mauzac and Loin de l'Oeil gives crisp acidity, green fruits and tangy acidity. It's a wine that's fresh and ripe at the same time, a very dry wine that will certainly be best with food. Drink from late 2016.
title: Domaine des Terrisses 2015 Grande Tradition White (Gaillac)

description: This is a fruity, juicy wine that Heifara Swartvagher made to be drunk young. With black currant freshness over firm, dry tannins, it's ripe, packed with attractive fruitiness and ready to drink.
title: Château Saint-Sernin 2012 Malbec-Merlot (Cahors)

description: The 17-acre vineyard is situated right at the western end of the Cahors appellation, giving a fresh feel to the ripe blackberry fruit flavors. There is an attractive, juicy feel to this wine. Soft, dusty tannins and bright acidity contribute to a wine that is now ready to drink.
title: Château les Hauts d'Aglan 2010 Malbec-Merlot (Cahors)

description: This is a soft, off-dry Champagne that has preserved plenty of apple and pear fruitiness with some softness on top. There is a yeasty character to the wine that is less attractive, although the aftertaste is all about crisp fruitiness.
title: H. Blin NV Demi-Sec  (Champagne)

description: Oak-aged Sauvignon Blanc and Muscadelle give a full, rounded wine that may have lost some of its herbaceous character while gaining richness and full fruitiness. A hint of toast is just an adjunct to this mineral and fruit flavored wine. Drink now or until 2018.
title: Château K 2013 White (Bergerac Sec)

description: The Xavier Flouret brand covers the world, but its Sancerre is always among its most consistent. It is balanced, fruity and only lightly herbaceous. Touches of white currants add to the fruitiness of this ready-to-drink wine.
title: Xavier Flouret 2013 Domaine la Gemière French Blonde  (Sancerre)

description: A ripe, fruity wine that is bone-dry but so full of red fruits that it seems soft. It's a delicious, lightly textured wine with a good touch of minerality at the end. Drink now.
title: Vignobles Berthier 2013 Domaine des Clairneaux Rosé (Sancerre)

description: A pure, clean mineral-driven Champagne. It's very crisp, with a chalky texture, flavors of green apples and tight acidity. It's one of those Champagnes that needs time in the glass, because as it opens the flavors become more complex, bringing out yellow fruits as well as the underlying citrus.
title: Jean-Noël Haton 2005 Extra Blanc de Blancs Brut Chardonnay (Champagne)

description: A pure, clean mineral-driven Champagne. It's very crisp, with a chalky texture, flavors of green apples and tight acidity. It's one of those Champagnes that needs time in the glass, because as it opens the flavors become more complex, bringing out yellow fruits as well as the underlying citrus.
title: Jean-Noël Haton 2005 Extra Blanc de Blancs Brut Chardonnay (Champagne)

description: A tough, dark wine, needing considerable aging to bring out its balanced fruits. It has the feel of a serious, impressive wine, dominated by powerful tannins. Underneath, the fruit is dark, brooding and firm. Give this wine at least five years.
title: Domaine de l'A 2010  Castillon Côtes de Bordeaux

description: This wine is structured with red fruits. It has a thin texture, a metallic character that is less pleasant. It needs more weight and richness.
title: Domaine Pierre Guillemot 2014 Aux Gravains Premier Cru  (Savigny-lès-Beaune)

description: Produced from organic grapes from the plateau above the prestigious slopes of Chablis, this is a cool and fresh wine with plenty of citrus as well as acidity. Drink now.
title: Domaine Philippe Goulley 2014  Petit Chablis

description: Fresh, fruity and with a tight texture, this attractive wine has crisp acidity, lemon and lime flavors, and a juicy aftertaste. Drink now.
title: Nadine et Maurice Guerrin 2014  Pouilly-Fuissé

description: This tangy wine with spice and acidity has kiwi and lime flavors that give a fresh character. The aftertaste is lightly perfumed. Drink now.
title: Jean-Christophe Perraud 2014  Mâcon La Roche Vineuse

description: This tangy wine with spice and acidity has kiwi and lime flavors that give a fresh character. The aftertaste is lightly perfumed. Drink now.
title: Jean-Christophe Perraud 2014  Mâcon La Roche Vineuse

description: The Layon valley vineyards produce deliciously honeyed wines like this one. There is botrytis here that gives a light texture to the wine, along with apricot fruit. With this richness, there is also refreshing crisp acidity. Worth aging 4–5 years but already delicious.
title: Château la Varière 2011 Le Savetier Chenin Blanc (Coteaux du Layon)

description: The second of two sweet wines produced by Marc Labat at Rousse, this certainly has a honey character, with flavors of dry fruits, a dancing acidity and a fruity aftertaste. Great as an aperitif.
title: Château de Rousse 2011 Cuvée Sélection  (Jurançon)

description: The second of two sweet wines produced by Marc Labat at Rousse, this certainly has a honey character, with flavors of dry fruits, a dancing acidity and a fruity aftertaste. Great as an aperitif.
title: Château de Rousse 2011 Cuvée Sélection  (Jurançon)

description: An extra year in bottle may cut down on the crispness of a Muscadet, but it does bring out so many attractive flavors. This wine boasts nuttiness and floral acidity that complements notes of white fruits and red apples. Screwcap.
title: Château de la Ragotiere 2010 Vieilles Vignes Sur Lie  (Muscadet Sèvre et Maine)

description: A selection from the best parcels gives a rich, full-bodied and wood-aged white wine. With tropical fruit flavors laced with lemon zest, it's both concentrated and fresh. Impressive wine for aging over 2–3 years and definitely to be drunk with food.
title: Château de la Jaubertie 2011 Mirabelle White (Bergerac Sec)

description: A very firm wine, layering acidity, black currant fruits and dense tannins. It currently is dominated by its acidity and structure, needing several years to open out. But it's all there, a powerful, perfumed and textured wine.
title: Charles Joguet 2010 Les Charmes  (Chinon)

description: A wood-aged Chenin Blanc from the Chinon region, this is a new departure for Charles Joguet. The wine is opulent and concentrated from lees stirring, giving power from the quince fruit and elegance from the smooth texture. It could age for several years.
title: Charles Joguet 2010 Clos de la Plante Martin Chenin Blanc (Touraine)

description: A wood-aged Chenin Blanc from the Chinon region, this is a new departure for Charles Joguet. The wine is opulent and concentrated from lees stirring, giving power from the quince fruit and elegance from the smooth texture. It could age for several years.
title: Charles Joguet 2010 Clos de la Plante Martin Chenin Blanc (Touraine)

description: This is a deliciously ripe wine, aged in wood to give roundness to the blend of Chenin Blanc and Chardonnay. It is full bodied and rich in the mouth with orange and pineapple flavors giving a great lift to the mineral texture.
title: Bouvet-Ladubay 2009 Trésor  (Saumur)

description: This is a deliciously ripe wine, aged in wood to give roundness to the blend of Chenin Blanc and Chardonnay. It is full bodied and rich in the mouth with orange and pineapple flavors giving a great lift to the mineral texture.
title: Bouvet-Ladubay 2009 Trésor  (Saumur)

description: There's a freshness to this wine, a product of the cool 2013 vintage. It plays down the rich spice and pushes up the crisp apple flavors, giving a dry character that's refreshing. It can be drunk now.
title: Jean-Baptiste Adam 2013 Réserve Gewurztraminer (Alsace)

description: There's a freshness to this wine, a product of the cool 2013 vintage. It plays down the rich spice and pushes up the crisp apple flavors, giving a dry character that's refreshing. It can be drunk now.
title: Jean-Baptiste Adam 2013 Réserve Gewurztraminer (Alsace)

description: Very sweet and honeyed, this dense wine almost has a botrytis character, sweet and dry together. Spice and yellow fruits are balanced with a touch of fresher lemon. This could age; drink from 2017.
title: Wunsch & Mann 2012 Hengst Grand Cru Gewurztraminer (Alsace)

description: This is a dry Pinot Gris, very mineral in character, with crisp acidity balanced by fragrant pear and quince topped with spice. It's a crisp wine, lighter than usual for this cuvée and fresher at the end.
title: Domaine Zinck 2012 Terroir Pinot Gris (Alsace)

description: A blend from different Grand Cru vineyards has resulted in this fresh and still-young wine. It has perfumed acidity, crisp acidity and a bone-dry character. Needing to age, it is packed with white fruits and flavored with summer flowers. Drink from 2016.
title: La Cave des Vignerons de Pfaffenheim 2012 Steingold Riesling (Alsace)
winery: La Cave des Vignerons de Pfaffenheim

description: This complex wine has a touch of sweetness allowing the fruit to be ready to drink sooner. At the same time, it has structure, strong minerality and a floral, fragrant character. Drink from 2015 or wait for the full effect until 2018.
title: Biecher & Schaal 2013 Schlossberg Grand Cru Riesling (Alsace)

description: This is a ripe, attractively fruity wine. With its red cherries, touch of spice and earthy, juicy character, it is all ready to drink, smooth and with a light touch of tannin.
title: Boeckel 2012 Les Terres Rouges Pinot Noir (Alsace)

description: The wine balances the sweet spiciness of Gewurztraminer with a good level of acidity. That gives the wine a light touch while allowing the rose and bergamot character of the grape to shine through. The wine is ready to drink.
title: Michel Léon 2013 Gewurztraminer (Alsace)

description: An impressive quality of Cahors is that you can find a wine as concentrated and dense as this without excessive alcohol. This 2006, wood aged, with touches of eucalyptus, is a big hearted, black fruit dominated wine, smooth and powerful, and just so well balanced for food. Can drink now, but better age for 3–5 years.
title: Château Lagrézette 2006 Malbec (Cahors)

description: An impressive quality of Cahors is that you can find a wine as concentrated and dense as this without excessive alcohol. This 2006, wood aged, with touches of eucalyptus, is a big hearted, black fruit dominated wine, smooth and powerful, and just so well balanced for food. Can drink now, but better age for 3–5 years.
title: Château Lagrézette 2006 Malbec (Cahors)

description: With a small amount of Tannat in the blend, this is a severe, tannic wine that will age. It has plum skin fruits, great weight and concentration, a dark, brooding structure, firm and solid. Age for 4–5 years.
title: Château Eugénie 2008 Cuvée Réservée de l'Aïeul Malbec (Cahors)

description: Less successful than the red Jacques Sans Souci, this nevertheless has some attractive fresh citrus and green plum flavors and bright fresh acidity. Simple fruits and a light green apple structure give it a good, crisp finish.
title: Barrière Frères 2006 Jacques Sans Souci  (Bordeaux Blanc)

description: A smooth and soft wine this is fruity, fresh and forward in style. Red-cherry flavor and gentle acidity dominate on the palate. It's rounded and ready to drink now. Finshes with a hint of sweetness.
title: Vollereaux NV Rosé de Saignée Brut Pinot Noir (Champagne)

description: A Merlot-dominated wine, structured with stalky black currant fruits, solid tannins and attractive spiciness. With its firm, serious character, it does need to age a few years. Drink from 2015.
title: Château de Terrefort-Quancard 2010  Bordeaux Supérieur

description: fruits touched with caramel and soft tannin. It's well balanced, with fruit and acidity integrating richly on the finish. It's a fine summer wine but also good for Thanksgiving turkey.
title: Château Castel des Maures 2012 Cuvée Jeanne Rosé (Côtes de Provence)

description: This full, ripe wine is rich with strawberry and red plum fruit. It's weighty on the palate with flavors of orange zest and a touch of spice. Brisk acidity cuts through the palate adding freshness on the finish.
title: Bernard Magrez 2012 Les Muraires Douce Vie Rosé (Côtes de Provence)

description: This is a soft, gently fruity wine that has pure peach and apple flavors cut with crisp, fresh acidity. Intended to be consumed while young, it is bright and fresh with a caramel and spice element that lingers on the finish.
title: Nicolas Potel 2012  Mâcon-Villages

description: This is the most extravagant version of three wines in a range in which grower Didier Pelvillain uses the figure seven for its mystic qualities. Here, the wine is ripe, brimming with fresh black fruits and acidity. The structure is firm in the background, allowing the wine to age. Drink from 2019.
title: Pelvillain Frères 2014 Inspiration 7.9 Malbec (Cahors)

description: This is a full, spicy and rich wine from the foothills of the Pyrénées mountains, ripe with apricot and plum fruits. There is freshness as well, along with a toasty character that adds complexity. This full-bodied wine can be aged for several years, so drink from 2019.
title: Lionel Osmin & Cie 2014 Cami Salié  (Jurançon Sec)

description: I know Bordeaux isn't known for being fruit-driven, but this paucity of fruit in a wine that's 50% Merlot (from a vintage that favored this variety's development) is hard to fathom. Leather and old wood combine with earth and mushrooms. There's decent weight and intensity here, so if these are flavors you look for this is an example to seek out.
title: Château Ducla 1998  Bordeaux

description: A light, toffee-and-caramel-tinged red that seems to be fading. Some earth and cherry flavors provide for acceptable drinking now, but this wine is headed south. Get to it soon.
title: Castel Roubine 1996 Cru Classe Red (Côtes de Provence)

description: Shows its Right Bank roots in Merlot and Cab Franc-derived red fruit and herb flavors: strawberry, tomato and rhubarb. Turns leathery and earthy, with some hints of toast on the finish.
title: Vieux Château Négrit 1997  Montagne-Saint-Émilion

description: Pretty strawberries and cherries are paired with softly minty nuances in this lightweight charmer. No, there's not a lot of intensity, but you could even serve it slightly chilled as a picnic wine.
title: Seigneurs de Bergerac 1999 Red (Bergerac)

description: This well-known Burgundy négociant has branched out into the Rhône, like so many others have before. The good news is that the wine is bursting with bright cherry flavors—tart and juicy. Would make a nice burger or sandwich accompaniment.
title: Mommessin 1999 Château De Domazan Red (Côtes du Rhône)

description: This well-known Burgundy négociant has branched out into the Rhône, like so many others have before. The good news is that the wine is bursting with bright cherry flavors—tart and juicy. Would make a nice burger or sandwich accompaniment.
title: Mommessin 1999 Château De Domazan Red (Côtes du Rhône)

description: With a nose of spicy green herbs—notably tarragon—and flavors of lemon and pink grapefruit, this no-nonsense blend of 50% Sauvignon Blanc and 50% Sémillon goes down easy and clean. The crisp finish is a good palate-cleanser.
title: Marquis de Chasse 1999 Reserve  (Bordeaux Blanc)

description: Bears a striking resemblance to blueberry pie in its aromas. Lighter than expected on the palate, before fading on the finish. A pleasant lunch mate to pâté or charcouterie.
title: Château d'Or et de Gueules 1998 Red (Costières de Nîmes)

description: Bears a striking resemblance to blueberry pie in its aromas. Lighter than expected on the palate, before fading on the finish. A pleasant lunch mate to pâté or charcouterie.
title: Château d'Or et de Gueules 1998 Red (Costières de Nîmes)

description: From a vintage known for its readily-approachable wines, this grand cru Saint-Emilion shows surprising structure. Some toasty oak frames delicate black-cherry fruit. Black tea notes on the finish carry more tannins than the fruit can handle in the long run, so catch this one soon before it heads south.
title: Château Lapelletrie 1997  Saint-Émilion

description: From a vintage known for its readily-approachable wines, this grand cru Saint-Emilion shows surprising structure. Some toasty oak frames delicate black-cherry fruit. Black tea notes on the finish carry more tannins than the fruit can handle in the long run, so catch this one soon before it heads south.
title: Château Lapelletrie 1997  Saint-Émilion

description: Features attractive aromas of chocolate, prunes, leather and soy sauce that are fairly complex and mature. The flavors are similar, with touches of earth and black cherries. Drink now.
title: Château des Sarrins 1997 Red (Côtes de Provence)

description: Another Cahors from the stable of Alain-Dominque Perrin, this one is the entry-level wine, made to be more accessible than his flagship wine from Château Lagrezette or the luxury cuvée. There's still plenty of toasty oak, but also some raspberry-cherry fruit and green tobacco on the finish.
title: Castel Montplaisir 1997 Red (Cahors)

description: This soft, gentle wine is defined by its notes of pepper and spice. The light acidity is just a hint in the full, rounded palate.
title: Domaine François Schmitt 2011 Bollenberg Auxerrois (Alsace)

description: This soft, gentle wine is defined by its notes of pepper and spice. The light acidity is just a hint in the full, rounded palate.
title: Domaine François Schmitt 2011 Bollenberg Auxerrois (Alsace)

description: Clean and fresh with lively citrus rind and red apple flesh aromas and flavors. It's not overdone and quite drinkable, with a soft toastiness that lingers through the finish. The texture is creamy and the swallow crisp.
designation: Méthode Traditionnelle Brut Chardonnay-Pinot Noir Sparkling Wine
title: Les Jamelles NV Méthode Traditionnelle Brut Chardonnay-Pinot Noir Sparkling Wine  (France)

description: This branded wine produced by the Cazes family of Château Lynch-Bages is ripe and rounded with dense tannins and sweet fruit. It has weight, spice from wood and a fine ready-to-drink balance.
title: Jean-Michel Cazes 2009 Michel Lynch  (Bordeaux)

description: A field blend of the Enclos vineyard has given a superrich wine, densely packed with juicy black plum fruits and sweet tannins. Ripe, full-bodied with a slight alcohol burn.
title: Château l'Enclos 2009 Triple A  (Sainte-Foy Bordeaux)

description: With stalky fruit and black currant acidity, the wine starts out lean. Then a richer, smoky wood character gives weight and sweeter flavors. Give the wine a year.
title: Château le Gardera 2009  Bordeaux Supérieur

description: Wood-dominated wine, very structured. It is spicy, firmly dry, with juicy black currant fruit behind the wood. Give a year or two for the wood to soften out and the fruit to come forward.
title: Château Lacombe Noaillac 2009 Les Traverses la Franque  (Médoc)

description: Wood-dominated wine, very structured. It is spicy, firmly dry, with juicy black currant fruit behind the wood. Give a year or two for the wood to soften out and the fruit to come forward.
title: Château Lacombe Noaillac 2009 Les Traverses la Franque  (Médoc)

description: This wine starts off a bit closed, but with time opens up to express attractive notes of small red berries, herbal twigs and whole baking spice. Medium weight with soft tannins and balanced acidity, this is a food-friendly wine that's sure to pair with most red meat or game dishes without overpopwering them.
title: Château Cabezac 2008 Le Petit Arthur Red (Minervois)

description: A slightly herbal edge and floral notes mingle with the dark berry and cherry aromas. Hints of tobacco and soft sweet spice add depth to the mouth, which is otherwise bright and vibrant but also straightforward. Drink now.
title: Château Cabezac 2007 Cuvée Arthur Red (Minervois)

description: With its rich texture from aging on the lees, this is a Sauvignon Blanc that goes more to the tropical and pineapple fruit direction. It has refreshing acidity along with weight and concentration. The lemon acidity kicks in in the aftertaste.
title: Château Bertinerie 2010  Blaye Côtes de Bordeaux

description: With its rich texture from aging on the lees, this is a Sauvignon Blanc that goes more to the tropical and pineapple fruit direction. It has refreshing acidity along with weight and concentration. The lemon acidity kicks in in the aftertaste.
title: Château Bertinerie 2010  Blaye Côtes de Bordeaux

description: A wine that shows firm tannins, fruit and wood acidity. It is now ready to drink, a wine that will remain firm and dry.
title: Château Bellerose Figeac 2007 Prestige  (Saint-Émilion)

description: Light aromas of red cherry and raspberry can be discovered upon deep nosing, but the fresh garrigue, tree bark and raw cocoa nib notes steal the show. A hint of vanilla-strawberry sweetens up the close. Drink now.
title: La Forge Estate 2010 Unfiltered Pinot Noir (Pays d'Oc)

description: This blend of Grenache Blanc, Grenache Gris, Roussanne and Maca­beau is a tad closed and shy now, but should develop more intensity with time. Peach skin, white melon and orange notes are present on the nose and mouth, and are dusted with a lovely sweet-spice accent on the finish, but the mouthfeel comes across as slightly flabby.
title: Domaine de l'Edre 2010 Carrément Blanc White (Côtes du Roussillon)

description: This ripe, fruity wine has attractive acidity that's balanced with yellow fruit and apple notes. It shows a bright character, with some good intensity of flavor and a crisp, refreshing finish.
title: Moingeon NV Brut  (Crémant de Bourgogne)

description: This smooth, soft wine is light and fruity. It has some tannins although fresh berry fruit and perfumed acidity are what characterize this wine. Immediately attractive, it's a light wine from a light year, and is ready to drink now.
title: Maurice Ecard 2013  Bourgogne

description: Soft and creamy, this gentle sparkling wine has some ripe apple fruits and attractive acidity. A yeasty aftertaste is less attractive.
title: Marquis de la Tour NV Brut Sparkling (Vin Mousseux)

description: The Grenache and Cinsault in this rosé are from the Jura and other vineyards. The result is a soft, smooth and creamy wine. Fresh red-berry fruits give it a round, almost off-dry character. It's fresh at the end, and definitely in an apéritif style.
title: François Montand NV Brut Rosé Sparkling (Vin Mousseux)

description: From the Cognac region, this ripe, totally fruity wine has no suggestion of wood aging. Attractive apple and light citrus flavors are ripe and right up front. Acidity adds freshness to the end. Drink now.
title: Maison des 3 Ponts 2014 Maison des 3 Ponts Chardonnay (Charentais)

description: This is soft, rounded and light. Baked apples and a creamy texture come with a refreshing burst of acidity tempered by a lightly toasty character. The wine is ready to drink.
title: Louis Chevallier 2013  Bourgogne

description: A balanced, ripe wine, this offers a good contrast between the dusty tannins and bright red-berry fruits. It's ready to drink with its fruitiness, although it will develop a richer, fuller character as it ages over the next year. Drink from 2017.
title: Joseph Mellot 2014 Le Rabault  (Sancerre)

description: All tangy fruit, this wine was fermented in stainless steel to keep the freshness of the fruit. It is crisp and lively, full of apple and pink-grapefruit flavors with a clean, bright aftertaste. Drink from mid-2016.
title: Henry Fessy 2014 Sous la Roche  (Pouilly-Fuissé)

description: Based in the Jura, this producer blends grapes from other regions to make this fresh, crisp and apple-flavored wine. It's light, bright and just off dry, with attractive acidity. Like it's rosé partner, it is really for apéritifs.
title: François Montand NV Brut Blanc de Blancs Sparkling (Vin Mousseux)

description: A caramel aroma sets the scene for a ripe, smooth wine. It has ripe red fruits that have a nutty, toasty character that balances with the crisp acidity and tight texture. Drink now.
title: Domaine Roger Champault 2014 Les Pierris Rosé (Sancerre)

description: With some weight behind it, this is a rounded wine, lightly flavored with apricot and lemon and a tang of bitter orange zest. The acidity is soft, an easy element in the texture.
title: Château Guirauton 2007  Graves

description: Light, light and light. This is such a soft, easy wine, already drinkable, the fruit fresh but missing concentration. The hint of smoke and wood are the only suggestion of complexity.
title: Chateau Dauzac 2007  Margaux

description: This wine is a bit on the lean side compared to most southern Rhône whites, but the plus side to that is its freshnesss and vivacity. Pear fruit is underlined by hints of spice, finishing clean and crisp. Drink now.
title: Louis Bernard 2007 White (Côtes du Luberon)

description: Decant this wine to help lessen the burnt match aroma that mars the nose initially. Once past that annoyance, this is a broad, very drinkable wine that blends pineapple notes with touches of honey, spice and alcoholic warmth. Drink now.
title: Domaine du Grand Tinel 2007 White (Châteauneuf-du-Pape)

description: Decant this wine to help lessen the burnt match aroma that mars the nose initially. Once past that annoyance, this is a broad, very drinkable wine that blends pineapple notes with touches of honey, spice and alcoholic warmth. Drink now.
title: Domaine du Grand Tinel 2007 White (Châteauneuf-du-Pape)

description: Light in color, this shows red cherry and strawberry flavors. The tannins are soft, creating an easy wine that is ready to drink.
title: Barton & Guestier 2011  Beaujolais

description: This firmly tannic wine has all the structure of 2010 without the fruit. It's a skeleton without flesh, and it will be unlikely to soften in the coming years.
title: Château la Gorre 2010  Médoc

description: Full bodied and rich, this has flavors of spice, red plum and caramel. It's quite heavy and dense, so drink it with food.
title: Georges Vigouroux 2011 Pigmentum Rosé Malbec (Lot)

description: Full bodied and rich, this has flavors of spice, red plum and caramel. It's quite heavy and dense, so drink it with food.
title: Georges Vigouroux 2011 Pigmentum Rosé Malbec (Lot)

description: An obviously wood-aged wine, this shows a bitter toast character. The fruit is lean, struggling to show through the dark chocolate flavor. It has an austere finish, which is mitigated by its final acidity.
title: Château Le Bourdieu 2010  Médoc

description: An obviously wood-aged wine, this shows a bitter toast character. The fruit is lean, struggling to show through the dark chocolate flavor. It has an austere finish, which is mitigated by its final acidity.
title: Château Le Bourdieu 2010  Médoc

description: Soft and so easy to drink, this is a fresh and fruity wine with gentle red fruits and light acidity. Attractive, it's crisply ready to enjoy.
title: Les Maîtres Vignerons de la Presqu'île de Saint-Tropez 2014 Cep d'Or Rosé (Côtes de Provence)
winery: Les Maîtres Vignerons de la Presqu'île de Saint-Tropez

description: Soft and light just off dry, this is an attractive and fruity wine. Strawberry flavors give a crispness to the background of the wine, finishing with a light, dancing aftertaste.
title: Le Charmel 2014 Rosé (Côtes de Provence)

description: This lightly fruity wine brings in layers of the freshest acidity before broadening out with citrus and green fruits. The wine is all about crisp, light fruitiness. A blend of Grenache, Syrah and Cinsault, it benefits from warm days and cool nights from vineyards at nearly 1,200 feet.
title: Pure Provence 2014 L'Opaline Rosé (Coteaux Varois en Provence)

description: Poised, stylish and very fruity, this wine is fresh with acidity, showing lemon and red currant, with a touch of pepper on the finish. It's just right as an apéritif.
title: Domaines Bunan 2014 Bunan Selection Rosé (Var)

description: From organically grown fruit, this is a soft, lemon- and pear-flavored wine. It has plenty of fresh acidity as well as a warm, full-in-the-mouth character. The aftertaste brings out touches of vanilla as well as the acidity.
title: Domaine Philippe Goulley 2012  Petit Chablis

description: The flavors of this wine follow the same light character as its pale, almost-white color. It does have some fresh juiciness, light acidity and a cut of lemon at the end. Crisp and clean, it's ready to drink.
title: Château Réal d'Or 2014 Rosé (Côtes de Provence)

description: Straightforward and fruity, this is fresh and light in character. It has plenty of acidity along with red cherry fruit flavors and a slight amount of tannin. It's drinkable now.
title: Domaine Poulleau Père et Fils 2013  Bourgogne

description: Straightforward and fruity, this is fresh and light in character. It has plenty of acidity along with red cherry fruit flavors and a slight amount of tannin. It's drinkable now.
title: Domaine Poulleau Père et Fils 2013  Bourgogne

description: Lemon and orange peel are right at the front of this wine. It's fruity, tangy and completely ready to drink.
title: Domaine d'Astros 2014 Cuvée Prestige Rosé (Vin de Pays des Maures)

description: This simple, soft and fruity wine has attractive acidity as well as red currant fruit flavors. With its final tang of acidity, it's well placed as an apéritif.
title: Château du Rouët 2014 Cuvée Réserve Tradition Rosé (Côtes de Provence)

description: This wine is structured, packed with tannins and acidity. Blackberry flavors come from behind to give some flesh to the structure. For a difficult vintage, this is attractive and will be drinkable after 2016.
title: Château Rousset-Caillau 2013  Bordeaux Supérieur

description: This wine is well balanced between its juicy black-currant fruits and dry tannins. The high percentage of Petit Verdot (20%) gives both the color and the firmer tannic background. It is beginning to age well, so drink from 2017.
title: Château Reverdi 2013  Listrac-Médoc

description: This five-acre property has produced a ripe wine that is more about fruit than structure. Although there are tannins, the bold, black fruits and fresh acidity show best. The aftertaste is fruit with a generous texture. Drink from 2018.
title: Château les Hautes Graves 2012  Montagne-Saint-Émilion

description: This Fontana family wine is concentrated and ripe. Blackberry and red fruits go with balanced acidity to give a wine that's already drinkable. Tannins support the ripe, full foreground. Drink now, or, better, from late 2016.
title: Château Le Clou du Pin 2014  Bordeaux

description: With Sauvignon Gris and Muscadelle as part of the blend, this is an attractively perfumed wine. Apricot, pear and quince flavors are already well integrated. The texture is light, with just a touch of orange zest. Drink now.
title: Château Landereau 2014  Entre-Deux-Mers

description: With Sauvignon Gris and Muscadelle as part of the blend, this is an attractively perfumed wine. Apricot, pear and quince flavors are already well integrated. The texture is light, with just a touch of orange zest. Drink now.
title: Château Landereau 2014  Entre-Deux-Mers

description: There is a good structure here, plenty to support the fresh fruits and red-berry flavors. This wine is full of fresh acidity with fruit and tannins in balance. It's going to develop well, always full of fruit and attractive acidity. Drink from 2018.
title: Château du Domaine de l'Eglise 2013  Pomerol

description: There is a good structure here, plenty to support the fresh fruits and red-berry flavors. This wine is full of fresh acidity with fruit and tannins in balance. It's going to develop well, always full of fruit and attractive acidity. Drink from 2018.
title: Château du Domaine de l'Eglise 2013  Pomerol

description: A full, fruity and textured wine, this is ripe with quince and apple flavors that are freshened by the citrus acidity. The ripe and fruity character, with a light toastiness, allow the wine to be drunk now.
title: Château d'Alix 2013  Pessac-Léognan

description: A full, fruity and textured wine, this is ripe with quince and apple flavors that are freshened by the citrus acidity. The ripe and fruity character, with a light toastiness, allow the wine to be drunk now.
title: Château d'Alix 2013  Pessac-Léognan

description: This ripe wine has light tannins to go with its red currant and blackberry fruits. The blend is 70% Merlot, 27% Cabernet Sauvignon and 3% Cabernet Franc. It is developing fast. With its acidity and gentle tannins it will be ready from 2017.
title: Château Chantemerle 2014  Blaye Côtes de Bordeaux

description: This ripe wine has light tannins to go with its red currant and blackberry fruits. The blend is 70% Merlot, 27% Cabernet Sauvignon and 3% Cabernet Franc. It is developing fast. With its acidity and gentle tannins it will be ready from 2017.
title: Château Chantemerle 2014  Blaye Côtes de Bordeaux

description: This wine has some richness, with ripe black currants and balanced acidity. The wood-aging just shows but, again, is balanced. With its fresh fruitiness, the wine will age quickly, so drink from 2017.
title: Château Balac 2013  Haut-Médoc

description: A blend from different Premier Cru vineyards across Chablis, this wine is the product of the wide choice of grapes available to this cooperative. It's soft and ripe yet shows the crisper edge typical of the vintage. Drink from 2018.
title: La Chablisienne 2014 Grande Cuvée Premier Cru  (Chablis)

description: Ripe and bold, it balances acidity and texture. Very mineral in character, it is textured and tight at this young stage. Green fruits, citrus and red apples show the fruity side. Age until 2016.
title: Dominique Cornin 2012 Les Chevrières  (Pouilly-Fuissé)

description: Made from 80-year-old vines from several parcels, this is a concentrated and dense wine. Red berry fruits give freshness, but it is the structure that counts. Drink from 2018.
title: Domaine René Bouvier 2011 Racines du Temps  (Gevrey-Chambertin)

description: This finely made wine has weight and firm tannins, along with intense acidity. Faiveley owns 12 acres of this premier cru which produces structured wines with fruit tannins and smoky fruit. At the end, the wood aging gives a burnt edge that needs to soften. Drink from 2017.
title: Domaine Faiveley 2011 Les Cazetiers Premier Cru  (Gevrey-Chambertin)

description: Round and full-bodied, the wine is dominated by wood-aging flavors. That masks the fruit at this stage, leaving the impression of a wine that is still to focus and bring out the impressive ripe fruits and mineral structure. Give it until 2017 to pull itself together.
title: Château de Fuissé 2012 Vieilles Vignes  (Pouilly-Fuissé)

description: To me, this luxury cuvée loses a bit of its identity to oak and ripeness while remaining an excellent red wine. Delicious? You bet. It's dark and intense, marked by the vanilla and cedar notes that overlay cherry and cracked pepper. The tannins are supple to the point of creaminess, creating a lush, soft mouthfeel.
title: Cave de Tain 2010 Epsilon  (Hermitage)

description: The wine comes from a single vineyard in the large 90-acre Château de Chamirey estate. It is beautifully balanced, rich and generous. Great red-plum fruits are there along with acidity and finely textured tannins. This is going to be a warm wine with a fine future. Drink from 2022.
designation: Château de Chamirey Clos du Roi Premier Cru
title: Domaines Devillard 2015 Château de Chamirey Clos du Roi Premier Cru  (Mercurey)

description: The wine comes from a single vineyard in the large 90-acre Château de Chamirey estate. It is beautifully balanced, rich and generous. Great red-plum fruits are there along with acidity and finely textured tannins. This is going to be a warm wine with a fine future. Drink from 2022.
designation: Château de Chamirey Clos du Roi Premier Cru
title: Domaines Devillard 2015 Château de Chamirey Clos du Roi Premier Cru  (Mercurey)

description: With ripe fruits and solid tannins, this is going to be a rich wine. It has plenty of acidity to balance this richness. At the same time, the tannins are going to allow it to age well. Drink from 2023.
designation: Carelle sous la Chapelle Premier Cru
title: Domaine Rossignol-Février Père et Fils 2015 Carelle sous la Chapelle Premier Cru  (Volnay)

description: This rich wine is dense and concentrated, with beautiful apple and spice flavors lifted by acidity. The fruit and the minerality typical of the appellation give this wine both its fine texture and its tangy fruitiness. Drink from 2018.
title: Domaine Pascal et Mireille Renaud 2016 Cuvée Vieilles Vignes  (Pouilly-Fuissé)

description: This east-facing vineyard is in the village of Fuissé. With the wood-aging giving spice and toast flavors, it is a ripe wine. The wood marches well with the apple and green-plum fruits. Still young, this rich wine has a mineral texture that comes from chalky soil. Drink from 2019.
title: Domaine Pascal et Mireille Renaud 2015 Aux Insarts  (Pouilly-Fuissé)

description: A blend from different vineyards of the Fleurie appellation, this wine is deliciously elegant and floral. Crisp red fruits are sustained by acidity and a juicy character. As often with this appellation, it is a wine to age and will be better from 2018.
title: Domaines Dominique Piron 2015  Fleurie

description: The juiciness of this wine, made by a producer based in Savigny, is what makes it so good. It is so fruity, with the tannins really only in a supporting role. That means it will develop quickly with the typical Savigny generosity. There is an attractive sprinkling of spice at the end. Drink from 2020.
title: Domaine Antonin Guyon 2015 Les Goudelettes  (Savigny-lès-Beaune)

description: The juiciness of this wine, made by a producer based in Savigny, is what makes it so good. It is so fruity, with the tannins really only in a supporting role. That means it will develop quickly with the typical Savigny generosity. There is an attractive sprinkling of spice at the end. Drink from 2020.
title: Domaine Antonin Guyon 2015 Les Goudelettes  (Savigny-lès-Beaune)

description: This wine is structured and concentrated with solid tannins. It has great ripe red fruits and plenty of berry flavors. It is going to be a fine wine, full of both fruit and structure as it develops. Drink from 2022.
title: Jaffelin 2015 Les Vergelesses Premier Cru  (Savigny-lès-Beaune)

description: This wine is ripe, generous with the opulence of the vintage. It has tropical fruits, rich acidity and a light touch of spice. Rounded and smooth, it has aging potential. Drink from 2019.
title: Henri de Villamont 2015 Clos des Guettes Premier Cru  (Savigny-lès-Beaune)

description: The wine has density and a good structure. It also has the acidity that marks the vintage. Red-cherry fruits and a crisp texture are balanced by the firmer tannins and solid character at the end. Drink from 2020.
title: Louis Latour 2015  Morey-Saint-Denis

description: Both ripe mirabelle and yellow juicy pear appear on the nose. The palate brims with the same fruit. The body is precise and fresh with a lip-smacking citrus finish.
title: Domaine Jean Sipp 2015 Les Trois Terroirs Pinot Blanc (Alsace)

description: The nose of juicy plum promises ripe fruit. The palate follows with a generous softness. There is ease on this light body and lots of freshness. Enjoy while aromas are at their peak.
title: Domaine Barmès-Buecher 2015 Rosenberg Pinot Blanc (Alsace)
