description: 93-95. Barrel sample. The wine shows depth and richness while also being very structured, almost severe. Weight and density is followed by extreme juiciness and blackberry fruits.
title: Clos du Marquis 2011 Barrel Sample  (Saint-Julien)

description: 93-95. Barrel sample. Ripe, fruity and powerful, this wine has intense Cabernet black-currant flavors, with plenty of richness and concentration. It shows the acidity and the bright fruit of the year.
title: Château Léoville Poyferré 2011 Barrel Sample  (Saint-Julien)

description: 93-95. Barrel sample. This is a crisp-textured wine, with a complex structure of rich, dense fruits, spice and wood. The wine is only just coming together, promising many years of aging ahead.
title: Château la Tour Blanche 2011 Barrel Sample  (Sauternes)

description: 93-95. Barrel sample. This is a crisp-textured wine, with a complex structure of rich, dense fruits, spice and wood. The wine is only just coming together, promising many years of aging ahead.
title: Château la Tour Blanche 2011 Barrel Sample  (Sauternes)

description: 93-95. Barrel sample. Dense and ripe, this wine boasts sweet tannins and flavors of ripe plums. With the vintage's tight, taut acidity, the aging potential is there.
title: Château Kirwan 2011 Barrel Sample  (Margaux)

description: Fresh and fruity, this wine has a crisp, mineral character that gives an intense texture. It is balanced, ripe while still taut and crisp. The background to this is riper yellow fruits and a full, generous aftertaste. Drink from 2016.
title: Domaine Vincent Girardin 2013 Les Vieilles Vignes  (Pouilly-Fuissé)

description: While it is structured and solid, the wine also has rich black fruits that are surrounded by the firm, dry tannins. There is a base of dark chocolate, wood spice and a brooding final quality to the weighty finish.
title: Château de Corbiac 2008  Pécharmant

description: A dense wine whose tannins initially overwhelm, but then blend more easily into its ripe black-plum core, which is laced with intense acidity. The wine is concentrated and very compact; a wine to age over the next 3–4 years.
title: Domaine Laougué 2009 L'Excellence de Marty Tannat-Cabernet (Madiran)

description: A dense wine whose tannins initially overwhelm, but then blend more easily into its ripe black-plum core, which is laced with intense acidity. The wine is concentrated and very compact; a wine to age over the next 3–4 years.
title: Domaine Laougué 2009 L'Excellence de Marty Tannat-Cabernet (Madiran)

description: Apricot and lemon marmalade aromas open up on this smooth, unctuous wine. It has concentrated honey and rich botrytis flavors, with an intense texture and fruit quality. Ready to drink now.
title: Domaine l'Ancienne Cure 2007 L'Abbaye  (Monbazillac)

description: This is a balanced and stylish wine, with a solid base of solid tannins and a dry core that gives strength to the blackberry fruit and acidity. There is minerality as well as a firm, austere finish. Age for 4–5 years.
title: Château Coste Peyrouse 2007 Malbec-Merlot (Cahors)

description: The top wine from Château Chambert is huge and densely concentrated. It has a solid, black fruited feel to it along its immense tannins. It's richness has given its structure a sweeter almost jammy finish. The wine will certainly age many years.
title: Château de Chambert 2009 Grand Vin Malbec (Cahors)

description: The top wine from Château Chambert is huge and densely concentrated. It has a solid, black fruited feel to it along its immense tannins. It's richness has given its structure a sweeter almost jammy finish. The wine will certainly age many years.
title: Château de Chambert 2009 Grand Vin Malbec (Cahors)

description: Big but murky; there just isn't much focus to this leathery, full-fruit bruiser that seems to draw its energy from a powerful beam of acidity that runs through the center of things. Short on balance and charm, but big on extract and tannins.
title: Michel Picard 2001 Cabernet Sauvignon (Languedoc)

description: Big but murky; there just isn't much focus to this leathery, full-fruit bruiser that seems to draw its energy from a powerful beam of acidity that runs through the center of things. Short on balance and charm, but big on extract and tannins.
title: Michel Picard 2001 Cabernet Sauvignon (Languedoc)

description: Peppery and green in the nose, with black olive aromas and little ripe fruit. That green quality carries onto the palate, where things are thin and vegetal, with just a hint of sour raspberry to keep it afloat.
title: Ferraton Pere et Fils 2000 Le Matiniere Blanc Marsanne (Crozes-Hermitage)

description: Light in color, in fact almost transparent. The nose is full of tomato, brier and dried herbs. In a word: it's weak. The palate is equally lean and spicy, while the finish seems starched out and on its final legs. On the plus side is a leathery feel and some dried-herb nuances that mingle below the surface.
title: Ferraton Pere et Fils 1998 Le Parvis Grenache (Châteauneuf-du-Pape)

description: Almost tan in color, with neutral aromas and a dull, almondy flavor profile. Round and smooth. but all in all it's boring and fading fast.
title: Domaine de la Courtade 2001 L'Alycastre Rosé (Côtes de Provence)

description: Melon and peach aromas start out fine but lose clarity. Citrus flavors that aren't quite full precede mild lemon and banana on the tail end. Nondescript and turns hot at the end. Kosher.
title: Abarbanel 2001 Estate Bottled Chardonnay (Vin de Pays de L'Aude)

description: Light and oaky at first, with earth notes. But then it goes awkward, showing imbalanced berry and plum fruit and overt oak. The wine shows some complexity and style, but at the same time it's all over the place, with hard tannins that subtract from the final tally.
title: Château Camplazens 1999 La Garrigue - La Clape Controlle Red (Coteaux du Languedoc)

description: Rubbery and spicy in the nose, with a hint of orange peel. In the mouth, a heavy flatness sets in fast. The wine seems old, and for a rosé, it is. It just sits on your palate, tasting o.k. but needing a poke in the ribs.
title: Château Ferry Lacombe 2000 Cuvee Lou Cascai Rosé (Côtes de Provence)

description: Sweet, light and floral, but not fruity. Lemon and orange flavors yield to a zesty finish. Simple and very high in acidity.
title: Mommessin 2002 Nid D'Abeille Chardonnay (Vin de Pays d'Oc)

description: Sweet, light and floral, but not fruity. Lemon and orange flavors yield to a zesty finish. Simple and very high in acidity.
title: Mommessin 2002 Nid D'Abeille Chardonnay (Vin de Pays d'Oc)

description: Green pepper and tobacco aromas signal some of the sour fruit that appears on the palate. Tastes of beets and pie cherries and an oaky, disparate finish doesn't do much to shape things up. Too sour and scattered.
title: M. Chapoutier 2001 Petite Ruche  (Crozes-Hermitage)

description: Green pepper and tobacco aromas signal some of the sour fruit that appears on the palate. Tastes of beets and pie cherries and an oaky, disparate finish doesn't do much to shape things up. Too sour and scattered.
title: M. Chapoutier 2001 Petite Ruche  (Crozes-Hermitage)

description: Sweet aromas of leather and caramel seem murky and tired. The palate comes without snap, and that's despite some plum and raspberry flavors. The finish is lean and basic, and overall it's a simple wine that doesn't really taste much like Syrah.
title: Val d'Orbieu 2001 Reserve St. Martin Syrah (Languedoc)

description: Sweet aromas of leather and caramel seem murky and tired. The palate comes without snap, and that's despite some plum and raspberry flavors. The finish is lean and basic, and overall it's a simple wine that doesn't really taste much like Syrah.
title: Val d'Orbieu 2001 Reserve St. Martin Syrah (Languedoc)

description: Cherry, plum and earth aromas lead into a tart, lean palate that struggles to offer more than a modicum of cherry and cassis flavors. The finish is sweet and spicy, which makes for an odd, not terribly appealing combination.
title: Val d'Orbieu 2001 Reserve St. Martin Cabernet Sauvignon (Languedoc)

description: Michel Laroche has been branching out of Chablis in recent years and his southern French effort has some chlorine notes along with aromas of mint and sweet wood. The power is up there, but there isn't suppleness to match. The palate pulsates while the finish is dark and sharp, with a burnt flavor.
title: Michel Laroche 2001 Merlot (Vin de Pays d'Oc)

description: Michel Laroche has been branching out of Chablis in recent years and his southern French effort has some chlorine notes along with aromas of mint and sweet wood. The power is up there, but there isn't suppleness to match. The palate pulsates while the finish is dark and sharp, with a burnt flavor.
title: Michel Laroche 2001 Merlot (Vin de Pays d'Oc)

description: Berry aromas come in front of a tart pie cherry and rhubarb palate. The feel is tight and acidic, so it lacks for mouthfeel and cries out for food. As a bistro or supermarket buy it offers the most potential.
title: Heron 2000 Merlot (Vin de Pays d'Oc)

description: This blend of Syrah and Grenache has minty, wet-plaster aromas, but also some pure Grenache notes. The palate runs tart, with cranberry and cherry. And the finish is tight and bitter, with more acids than tannin. A viable bistro wine but go no further.
title: Château de Jau 2002 Jaja Red (Vin de Pays d'Oc)

description: This blend of Syrah and Grenache has minty, wet-plaster aromas, but also some pure Grenache notes. The palate runs tart, with cranberry and cherry. And the finish is tight and bitter, with more acids than tannin. A viable bistro wine but go no further.
title: Château de Jau 2002 Jaja Red (Vin de Pays d'Oc)

description: An attractive, ripe wine with acidity and black currant fruits. This is a medium-bodied Bordeaux, the dry core ripened with a rounded, soft texture.
title: Château les Reuilles 2005  Bordeaux

description: An attractive, ripe wine with acidity and black currant fruits. This is a medium-bodied Bordeaux, the dry core ripened with a rounded, soft texture.
title: Château les Reuilles 2005  Bordeaux

description: A dry, firm wine, with light fruits and a perfumed smoky character. It is developing in a dry, black currant, stalky style.
title: Château Grand-Maison 2008  Côtes de Bourg

description: A wine that is firmly tannic, solid, chunky and dry with red fruits buried behind the foursquare facade. Fruit flavors and acidity come through more strongly at the end.
title: Château Bertinerie 2008 Merlot-Cabernet  (Côtes de Bordeaux)

description: Ripe botrytis, honey and peaches make for an attractive, open, ready-to-drink sweet wine. The acidity keeps the richness in check.
title: Barton & Guestier 2008  Sauternes

description: A somewhat austere, lean wine, with dry tannins and tobacco aromas. The berry fruits are full of spice and fresh currants, giving a wine that is stalky, firm and finishes dry.
title: Manoir de la Tête Rouge 2007 Bagatelle  (Saumur)

description: This hugely ripe Merlot has created a monster of a wine, heavily laden with bitter coffee extraction as well as very ripe black plum fruits. Big and concentrated, this is a wine to be enjoyed for its profusion and excess.
title: Château Siaurac 2010  Lalande de Pomerol

description: This wine has weight and concentration, heavy on the tannins at this stage. Wild strawberry and dark plum fruits are taking their time to show through the structure. Dark tannins from firm wood aging and extracted fruit can also be found here. Drink from 2015.
title: Château la Favière 2010 Muse  (Bordeaux Supérieur)

description: This is a fully mature wine showcasing toast, ripe fruit and citrus acidity at their best. It is not a dry wine, with signs of a relatively high dosage, but that gives the wine softness as well as richness. Ready to drink now, but it will also keep until 2020.
title: Chanoine 2008 Tsarine Millésime Brut  (Champagne)

description: Named after Léonie Duchêne, one of the founders of the company, this is a toasty bottling. It has an onion-skin pink color and delicate aromas of red fruits which show on the palate, along with a crisp and dry acidity. Ready to drink.
title: Canard-Duchêne NV Cuvée Léonie Brut Rosé  (Champagne)

description: In keeping with the dry style that marks Jeaunaux-Robin Champagne, this is a taut, crisply fruity wine. It has light, bright fruits with a touch of more mature toast and cookie flavors. It's just ready to drink.
title: Jeaunaux-Robin NV Sélection Extra Brut  (Champagne)

description: While certainly ripe and fruity, this wine is also structured—its generosity tempered by intense acidity, crisp apple-skin notes and a mineral texture. The result is a full wine that needs a little time to soften. Drink from 2014.
title: Henri de Villamont 2010 Premier Cru  (Montagny)

description: The nose is rather closed and just hints at crunchy cherries. The palate has ample red-cherry fruit but lacks a little definition and sports a slightly bitter edge. The body is dry and juicy. Drink soon.
title: Domaine Fernand Engel 2015 Meyerhof Pinot Noir (Alsace)

description: The wine is smooth and ripe. Generous and already balanced between tannins and black fruits, it is a rich wine that will develop quickly. Drink from 2019.
title: Château Victoria 2014  Haut-Médoc

description: Situated to the north of the village of Listrac, this estate is one of several that carries the name Dupré. The wine is dominated by Merlot (60%). That explains the wine's high alcohol and lush character. It also shows signs of firm extraction that has left a tough dry core. It will soften, but it will not lose its overwhelming richness.
title: Château Saransot-Dupré 2014  Listrac-Médoc

description: From a small estate of only 10 acres, this wine with its 60% Merlot is fruity with just the right amount of tannins. It has red fruit and crisp acidity along with a dry edge. The wine is likely to age quickly, so drink from 2019.
title: Château Peyredon Lagravette 2014  Haut-Médoc

description: Very easy, slightly confected cherry fruit comes immediately to the fore. The palate has the same candy-ish notion countered with lots of freshness. The body is light, translucent and off dry. Drink soon while berryish aromas are at their peak.
title: Domaine Robert Klingenfus 2015 Pinot Noir (Alsace)

description: The nose seems to be dampened by notes of earth. The palate, however, is fresh and sprightly with friendly pear notes but with slightly bitter edges. Drink soon.
title: Maurice Schoech & Fils 2015 Côtes d'Ammerschwihr White (Alsace)

description: The nose is subdued and gives little away. The palate seems slightly dilute and neutral, showing very little of Sylvaner's subtly perfumed quality. It's a very light bodied, clean but almost neutral white.
title: Domaine Charles Baur 2014 Sylvaner (Alsace)

description: The nose is subdued and gives little away. The palate seems slightly dilute and neutral, showing very little of Sylvaner's subtly perfumed quality. It's a very light bodied, clean but almost neutral white.
title: Domaine Charles Baur 2014 Sylvaner (Alsace)

description: This is a light wine with bright acidity and red fruit flavors. It has a mere touch of tannin to give structure to the crisp aftertaste. Drink now.
title: Château Vieux Porier 2014  Bordeaux

description: This is tight, juicy wine produced by the local cooperative. It has intense black-currant acidity and spice and toast from the wood aging. With its tannins it will age. Drink from 2019.
title: Château Ladignac 2014  Médoc

description: A blend with 67% Cabernet Sauvignon produces this black currant and crisply fruity wine. The wood aging and the fruit tannins are integrating well, giving a wine that is bright, packed with fruit and likely to age well over the medium term. Drink from 2020.
title: Château Haut Grignon 2014  Médoc

description: This is firm with dry tannins and a concentrated dense texture. It is more about structure than fruit and it is likely to remain dry. The acidity at the end does give a final lift.
title: Château du Moulin Rouge 2014  Haut-Médoc

description: Soft, fresh, just off dry, a fruity wine that is light and fragrant. Crisp acidity cuts through the wine, giving a tight, nervy edge along with bright fruitiness.
title: Cave de Cleebourg 2011 Riesling (Alsace)

description: Soft, fresh, just off dry, a fruity wine that is light and fragrant. Crisp acidity cuts through the wine, giving a tight, nervy edge along with bright fruitiness.
title: Cave de Cleebourg 2011 Riesling (Alsace)

description: A soft, pure fruited wine, this is rounded, full of pear and white peach flavors. The wine is soft, fruity, ready to drink, finishing with light, easy acidity.
title: Jean Becker 2011 Pinot Blanc (Alsace)

description: A fruity wine, just touched by some wood aging with attractive strawberry fruit flavors and acidity. It's not a wine for aging, its light minerality enhancing the fruitiness.
title: Domaines Devillard 2011 Le Renard  (Bourgogne)

description: A full and rounded wine, touched by caramel as well as red plum and ripe strawberries. It is generous, with a soft, open aftertaste. There is a light texture from the acidity that creeps in at the end.
title: Château Saint-Sernin 2012 Domaine Saint-Sernin Fare Saint-Sernin Rosé (Côtes du Lot)

description: This blend of 30% Carignan, 40% Grenache and 30% Syrah is easygoing and approachable, with medium-intense aromas and flavors of wild strawberry, black cherry, raspberry and fresh herbs. The palate is ripe and fruity, with dusty tannins and a clean, bright finish.
title: Les Vignerons des Côtes d'Agly 2009 Les Arcades Red (Côtes du Roussillon Villages)

description: Rounded wine, softly fruity. Its attractiveness comes from ripe white fruits, soft structure and a generous feel. It's not for aging and can be drunk now.
title: Vignerons de Buxy 2011 Buissonnier  (Montagny)

description: Rounded wine, softly fruity. Its attractiveness comes from ripe white fruits, soft structure and a generous feel. It's not for aging and can be drunk now.
title: Vignerons de Buxy 2011 Buissonnier  (Montagny)

description: Big, bold and fruity wine, boasting deliciously ripe black fruits and a smooth, just tannic texture. All fruit, this is the perfect barbecue wine: rich, open and generous. Drink now and until 2016.
title: Georges Vigouroux 2012 Gouleyant Malbec (Cahors)

description: A forward, fruity wine, full of apple and creamed pear flavors. The acidity is light, bright and attractive giving a wine that is fresh and ready to drink.
title: Domaines Devillard 2011 Le Renard  (Bourgogne)

description: Made by the Tari family who used to own Château Giscours in Margaux, Bordeaux, this wine with its 18 months wood aging shows a great understanding of red-wine making. Firm and tannic, almost totally from Mourvèdre, this dark and brooding wine is nowhere near ready to drink. The organically grown grapes give a purity of fruit that cuts through the tannins. Don't drink before 2018.
title: Domaine de la Bégude 2012 La Brûlade Red (Bandol)

description: Made by the Tari family who used to own Château Giscours in Margaux, Bordeaux, this wine with its 18 months wood aging shows a great understanding of red-wine making. Firm and tannic, almost totally from Mourvèdre, this dark and brooding wine is nowhere near ready to drink. The organically grown grapes give a purity of fruit that cuts through the tannins. Don't drink before 2018.
title: Domaine de la Bégude 2012 La Brûlade Red (Bandol)

description: The nose is subdued while the palate shows some apple and yellow-plum fruit. This is simple and fresh but shows a bitter edge and some dilution.
title: Kuentz-Bas 2014 Tradition Pinot Blanc (Alsace)

description: The nose is subdued while the palate shows some apple and yellow-plum fruit. This is simple and fresh but shows a bitter edge and some dilution.
title: Kuentz-Bas 2014 Tradition Pinot Blanc (Alsace)

description: Flavors of apple are spoiled by notes of mud and pondwater on the nose. The palate is bitter and undefined.
title: Frédéric Mallo 2014 Special Delivery Pinot Blanc (Alsace)

description: A very neutral wine, this has some earthy spice on the palate, but is almost bare of fruit. It's clean and neutral but not refreshing.
title: Domaine de la Tour Blanche 2014 Pinot Blanc (Alsace)

description: This otherwise fruity wine has a rustic edge. It gives an unattractive herbal character that may come from underripe grapes.
title: Château Haut Mouleyre 2015 Rosé (Bordeaux Rosé)

description: From the sweet white appellation of the Bergerac region, this is a full, botrytis-dominated wine, opulent, layered with dryness to balance the citrus and honey flavors. Maybe without complexity, but certainly with all the right botrytis wine characters.
title: Clarendelle 2003 Amberwine  (Monbazillac)

description: A crisp, fresh, intensely dry wine that is balanced by some ripe caramel and red currant flavors. This is a rosé in the Provence tradition, dry, designed for food.
title: Moulin de Gassac 2006 Le Mazet Rosé Red (Vin de Pays de L'Herault)

description: Fresh and lively with flavors of strawberry, cherry, raspberry and red plum pulp. The acidity subdues the stronger fruit flavors on the palate, balancing everything out nicely. Moderate weight with a full texture and a zingy, lingering finish.
title: Les Jamelles 2007 Rosé Cinsault (Vin de Pays d'Oc)

description: Offers heady aromas of mashed peaches, banana, blueberry and walnut. The palate matches the nose in flavors and intensity, but is lifted by the vibrant acidity and somewhat prickly texture. Finishes clean with moderate length.
designation: Famille Grassa Rosé de Pressée Merlot-Syrah-Tannat
region: Vin de Pays des Côtes de Gascogne
title: Domaine du Tariquet 2007 Famille Grassa Rosé de Pressée Merlot-Syrah-Tannat Rosé (Vin de Pays des Côtes de Gascogne)

description: The nose offers minor essences of apple core and more pronounced notes of wet minerality. On the palate, more refreshingly acidic characteristics shine with flavors of ripe rhubarb and red cherry. A rosé perfectly designed for enjoying with food.
title: Domaine de Nizas 2007 Rosé (Coteaux du Languedoc)

description: This had quite an evolved nose, suggesting bitter almond and vanilla, as much as pear and dried orange rind. The palate is dry and expressive, fluid but precisely drawn showing great depth of flavor and concentration. An intriguing nuttiness makes for a long dry finish.
title: Domaine Pfister 2014 Silbergerb Pinot Gris (Alsace)

description: This blend dominated by Cabernet Sauvignon comes from schist soil on the plateau above the Loire river. It benefits from a warm vintage to give a rich character as well as some firm tannins. The balance between fruit and structure is just right. Although the wine is young, it will mature quickly, so drink from 2019.
title: Domaine du Petit Clocher 2015 Cabernet Franc-Cabernet Sauvignon (Anjou Villages)

description: Enticing notes of ripe juicy yellow pear mix with tangy notes of fresh citrus zest on the nose. The fluid palate has the same interplay of ripe generosity—think yellow plum and ripe pear, and fresh lemony zestiness. This is off dry, full flavored and fresh.
title: Domaine de la Tour Blanche 2015 Pinot Gris (Alsace)

description: Frédéric Borderie brings his winemaking experience from Australia and Napa Valley back to the family property and this crisp and perfumed wine. It has great spiciness balanced by crisp green and white stone fruits. The wine could do with a few more months, so drink from late 2017.
title: Château Les Combes 2016  Bordeaux Blanc

description: Frédéric Borderie brings his winemaking experience from Australia and Napa Valley back to the family property and this crisp and perfumed wine. It has great spiciness balanced by crisp green and white stone fruits. The wine could do with a few more months, so drink from late 2017.
title: Château Les Combes 2016  Bordeaux Blanc

description: This is a wine that, unlike many Muscadets, can age well. Although only three years old, it will likely go for several more. That comes from the depth of the fruit, the ripe spice and acidity and the rounded white fruits. So drink now and until 2022.
title: Chateau de l'Oiselinière 2014 Les Grands Gâts Sur Lie  (Muscadet Sèvre et Maine)

description: Open and ripely fruity, this has fresh acidity, with tight and tangy flavors of lemon zest. A warm, rounded character to the wine puts it firmly as an apéritif.
title: Château Roubine 2014 R de Roubine Rosé (Côtes de Provence)

description: This has a delicious tang of citrus and acidity to go with the crisp red currant fruitiness. It is bright and ready to drink, with refreshing acidity at the end.
title: Domaine de la Sanglière 2014 Breezette Rosé (Côtes de Provence)

description: This wine is packed with red fruits, crisp apples and oranges. It is so fresh and bright, with good acidity that gives everything a total lift.
title: Domaine de la Croix 2014 iirrrésistible Rosé (Côtes de Provence)

description: From an estate in the hills above Saint-Tropez, this wine is soft, aromatic and gently fruity. It is as light as a breath of wind, but crisp at the end, with hints of red berry fruitiness.
title: Les Maîtres Vignerons de la Presqu'île de Saint-Tropez 2014 Château des Launes Rosé (Côtes de Provence)
winery: Les Maîtres Vignerons de la Presqu'île de Saint-Tropez

description: This open and generous wine is attractive and ready to drink. White peach and pear flavors give it great fruitiness without losing sight of acidity. It's fruity, softly textured and just right now.
title: Joseph Drouhin 2012  Mâcon-Lugny

description: Bonheur—happiness—is an appropriate name for this fresh and crisp wine that comes in a flute à corset bottle. It is fruity, lively with orange and apricot over raspberries. Bright acidity finishes it all in good humor.
title: Thomas Carteron 2014 Le Bonheur Rosé (Côtes de Provence)

description: Made from 50% Grenache, 30% Cinsault and 20% Syrah, this is a vibrant, floral rosé, offering upfront aromas of iris, lavender and laurel that complement the raspberry and strawberry-hull core. The fruity palate is bright and refreshing, with ample acidity and just a hint of orange blossom on the finish.
title: Côté Mas 2012 Rosé Aurore Rosé (Pays d'Oc)

description: Meat and bacon aromas introduce a wine that is taut, structured and high on the acidity. It has a lean, slightly dirty taste, which is not attractive.
title: Château Tire Pé 2009  Bordeaux

description: Round and lacking form, this shows only tannins. It features some attractive acidity, but it is finally spoiled by a rustic character.
title: Château Mazeyres 2009  Pomerol

description: This has loads of wood that seems to hide the fruit. It has a bitter wood flavor of burnt toast, plus extracted tannins.
title: Château de la Cour d'Argent 2010  Bordeaux Supérieur

description: This has loads of wood that seems to hide the fruit. It has a bitter wood flavor of burnt toast, plus extracted tannins.
title: Château de la Cour d'Argent 2010  Bordeaux Supérieur

description: This wine is all wood, with no promise of fruit.
title: Château la Verrière 2010  Bordeaux Supérieur

description: A flavor of black currant drop gives this wine a sweet-tasting, overripe sensation. There is little structure and no great aging potential.
title: Château l'Isle Fort 2009  Bordeaux Supérieur

description: A bitter yeast flavor doesn't do this 100% Sémillon wine any favors. It is heavy and fat, and the citrus fruits are lost along the way.
title: Château Fonchereau 2010  Bordeaux Blanc

description: This smells and tastes like cherry Powerade—soft and merely fruity. Not for aging.
title: Château du Pin 2009  Bordeaux

description: There is an awkwardness to this wine, coming from the overripe fruit and juicy character. It lacks structure and will likely age quickly.
title: Trocard 2009  Bordeaux Supérieur

description: The wine is ripe, dense and with fine layers of green fruits, grapefruit and acidity. The flinty texture is still strong in this young wine which bursts with youthful fruitiness. It is going to develop well into an impressive wine. Drink from late 2018.
title: Château Favray 2015  Pouilly-Fumé

description: The song of the elm is the poetic name of this wine. It is a rich wine, dense with fruit and with some toast from the wood aging. It is impressive with its ripe swathes of fruit and its spicy aftertaste. The wine is just ready to drink although it will be better from 2018.
title: Pierre Morin 2015 Le Chant de l'Orme  (Sancerre)

description: This classy wine is rich, with its firm structure still intact. It has bold tannins, ripe blackberry fruit and bright acidity. Its concentration, together with its dry, tannic core, confirms that it will age further. Drink from 2020.
title: Château la Croizille 2012  Saint-Émilion

description: This rich wine is full of intense botrytis. It has fine poise, balancing its concentrated apricot and lemon flavors with botrytis notes. Drink from 2022.
title: Château de Rayne Vigneau 2014 Madame de Rayne  (Sauternes)

description: Yeasty in character, this wine seems to have missed out both on fruit and texture.
title: Doudet Naudin 2013  Pouilly-Fuissé

description: Yeasty in character, this wine seems to have missed out both on fruit and texture.
title: Doudet Naudin 2013  Pouilly-Fuissé

description: This is a wine with harshness, sharp walnut and bitter orange flavors. It gives off a hard feeling that probably won't soften much.
title: Domaine des Deux Roches 2013 Plants Carré  (Mâcon-Villages)

description: This wine is perfumed, soft and with a light character. An oddly floral character doesn't jell with the fruitiness that is behind it.
title: Domaine Carrette 2013 Les Crays  (Pouilly-Fuissé)

description: This wine is perfumed, soft and with a light character. An oddly floral character doesn't jell with the fruitiness that is behind it.
title: Domaine Carrette 2013 Les Crays  (Pouilly-Fuissé)

description: Soft with a yeasty character, this wine has not gotten its act together. It has some bitterness, walnut and spice flavors although nothing hangs together.
title: Domaine Ferret 2013  Pouilly-Fuissé

description: Produced by Château Larose Trintaudon for historic Bordeaux merchant Schröder & Schÿler, this is a rounded, black-fruit flavored wine. Now soft and ready to drink, it still has attractive juicy flavors as well as ripe blackberry. Soft tannins form the background and sustain the structure. Drink now.
title: Schröder & Schÿler 2011 Private Selection  (Haut-Médoc)

description: Produced by Château Larose Trintaudon for historic Bordeaux merchant Schröder & Schÿler, this is a rounded, black-fruit flavored wine. Now soft and ready to drink, it still has attractive juicy flavors as well as ripe blackberry. Soft tannins form the background and sustain the structure. Drink now.
title: Schröder & Schÿler 2011 Private Selection  (Haut-Médoc)

description: A full, ripe wine that has melon, crisp pear and hints of yellow fruits. Amidst this fruit salad of flavors, there are tight acidity and minerality. The wine is crisp and tangy at the end.
title: Ollivier Frères 2015 Domaine des Amoureux Sur Lie  (Muscadet Sèvre et Maine)

description: Bright and tangy, this is a crisp, tight and mineral wine. It is fruity with pear and lime fruits that are caught up in the tangy texture and tense acidity. This is a wine that could age a while more, so drink from 2017.
title: Domaine du Haut Bourg 2015 Pavillon Sur Lie  (Muscadet Côtes de Grandlieu)

description: Bright and tangy, this is a crisp, tight and mineral wine. It is fruity with pear and lime fruits that are caught up in the tangy texture and tense acidity. This is a wine that could age a while more, so drink from 2017.
title: Domaine du Haut Bourg 2015 Pavillon Sur Lie  (Muscadet Côtes de Grandlieu)

description: Situated on the ridge in the center of Entre-deux-Mers that produces fine white wines, this vineyard has produced a wine that is rich and full. Apricot and ripe pear fruits have a perfumed touch along with almond and spice flavors. It could do with a few more months and will be best from 2017.
title: Château Landereau 2015  Entre-Deux-Mers

description: This smoky wood-aged wine shows tannins as well as black fruits. It has a fine structure that balances with the fruitiness. Produced in the Entre-deux-Mers, the wine has a spicy, fresh aftertaste.
title: Château la Calvaire 2012  Bordeaux Supérieur

description: The second wine of Château de Lamarque is named after the medieval tower of the castle. It is a densely tannic wine, firm and dense although also with plenty of black-plum fruits. The wood aging is still showing prominently, giving a tough, dry edge to the wine that needs to soften. Give this tight wine until 2018.
title: Château de Lamarque 2012 Donjon de Lamarque  (Haut-Médoc)

description: Produced from 60-acres of vines on the plateau east of Saint-Émilion village, this is a fresh and fruity wine. It has layers of tannin surmounted with red cherry and black-currant fruits. The wine, with its dominance of Merlot, is developing well and will be ready to drink from 2018.
title: Château Boutisse 2013  Saint-Émilion

description: A 24-acre vineyard at the southern end of the Graves region has produced a 2010 that is rich while still retaining an attractive light touch. There are firm tannins that are the background to the blackberry fruits and bold structure. Drink this wine from 2017.
title: Château Andréa 2010  Graves

description: A 24-acre vineyard at the southern end of the Graves region has produced a 2010 that is rich while still retaining an attractive light touch. There are firm tannins that are the background to the blackberry fruits and bold structure. Drink this wine from 2017.
title: Château Andréa 2010  Graves

description: There is an attractive 15% Cabernet Franc in this wine. That gives a strongly perfumed character and brings out firm tannins from both the fruit and the wood aging. The wine's blackberry fruits are ripe and juicy with a smooth, rounded aftertaste. Drink from 2019.
title: Château Alta Gaïa 2012  Bordeaux Supérieur

description: Classic northern Rhône aromas of smoke, espresso and black olive set the stage, followed by layers of dark fruit and spice. The finish is softly dusty, brimming with plum and licorice notes. Full-bodied, concentrated and supple, this is ready to drink now, yet should age well through 2025 or so.
title: Gilles Flacher 2013 Les Reines  (Saint-Joseph)

description: This is refreshingly bright for a white Châteauneuf-du-Pape. Pineapple and bergamot notes mark the palate, while the finish is tight, citrusy and even a bit chalky in texture. Drink now–2020.
title: Famille Perrin 2014 Les Sinards White (Châteauneuf-du-Pape)

description: The 2012 vintage was reasonably warm, and this wine is ripe and creamy in texture, with ground clove and cracked pepper notes accenting plummy fruit. Vanilla and bacon notes chime in on the slightly dusty finish. Drink now–2025.
title: E. Guigal 2012 Brune et Blonde de Guigal  (Côte Rôtie)

description: Light, fresh, soft and already very drinkable. The initial taste is dominated by citrus, and then it rounds out, adding toast, green fruits and a definite sophistication for a simple white Burgundy.
title: Pierre Morey 2005  Bourgogne

description: Crisp, green and steely, this is classic Chablis, all about pure green fruits and minerality, only lightly layered with wood. It is vibrant and fresh, with the acidity adding a mouthwatering lightness.
title: Pascal Bouchard 2006 Mont-de-Milieu Premier Cru  (Chablis)

description: A toasty, oaky wine, with smoky aromas and flavors that mask the white fruit flavors and acidity. Hopefully all this high toast will burn off. Hold for 2–3 years.
title: Faiveley 2005 Clos Rochette  (Mercurey)

description: An elegant rendering of the appellation, this is only medium bodied, yet packs in plenty of complex flavors. Cracked pepper, cured meat, blueberry and plum notes finish with a soft dusting of silky tannins. Drink now–2020.
title: Vidal-Fleury 2010 Brune et Blonde de Vidal-Fleury  (Côte Rôtie)

description: This is strongly marked by toasty, cedary oak, but enough fruit comes through on the midpalate and finish to suggest this is more than just another oaky red. It's rich and creamy through the midpalate, then finishes long, with mixed berry notes emerging at the end.
title: Tardieu-Laurent 2011 Guy Louis Red (Côtes du Rhône)

description: Fermented in oak (50% new), this is a broad, toast-accented wine that delivers hints of honey and marmalade yet remains reasonably long and focused on the finish. Best enjoyed before the end of 2015.
title: Famille Perrin 2012 Les Sinards White (Châteauneuf-du-Pape)

description: This is Mordorée's top cuvée of Tavel, and it earns that distinction by virtue of its length and stoniness on the finish. There's a hint of garrigue to the cherry aromas and a plump, complex midpalate as well. Drink it over the next year or two.
title: Domaine de la Mordorée 2013 La Reine Des Bois  (Tavel)

description: The nose shows restrained citrus and a slightly lifted, very slightly aromatic touch of conifer. The palate is taut and slender, presenting sober, clean citrus flavors. This stands upright and has a wonderful backbone of freshness. I feel it will have more to give in the future. It's refreshing now and promising in the future. The finish is so subtly fruited that this will be worth the wait. Drink now through 2030.
title: Trimbach 2014 Riesling (Alsace)

description: The nose shows restrained citrus and a slightly lifted, very slightly aromatic touch of conifer. The palate is taut and slender, presenting sober, clean citrus flavors. This stands upright and has a wonderful backbone of freshness. I feel it will have more to give in the future. It's refreshing now and promising in the future. The finish is so subtly fruited that this will be worth the wait. Drink now through 2030.
title: Trimbach 2014 Riesling (Alsace)

description: Tangerine and mirabelle plum aromas combine on a very inviting nose. The palate is slender and fresh, framing the ripe mirabelle fruit in zesty refreshing brightness. This is dry and lemony, ripe and whistle clean. The tangy lemon flavors create a long and bracingly clean, utterly refreshing finish.
title: Ruhlmann 2015 Cuvée Jean-Charles Riesling (Alsace)

description: This is the top wine from this producer. Produced, as its name indicates, from old vines, it is ripe with mango and pineapple fruits as well as fine streak of tangerine. There is good mineral texture and tight acidity to give this wine its crisp side. Drink this rich wine from 2018.
title: Roger et Didier Raimbault 2014 Vieilles Vignes  (Sancerre)

description: A wonderfully aromatic note of tangerine and orange peel appears first. The palate continues with the purity of ripe aromatic citrus flavors: there is zest and freshness on a slender, lively and bundled body that delivers a blast of tangy ripe citrus. The finish is clean, just off dry and almost addictive—you just have to take another sip.
title: Henri Schoenheitz 2015 Linsenberg Riesling (Alsace)

description: The aromatic tang of ripe lemon peel plays on the nose. The palate is pervaded by the same refreshing zestiness, shimmering with cheerful citrus brightness amidst riper notions of pear and peach. This is mouth-watering stuff, almost addictive with its dry zesty finish.
title: Domaines Schlumberger 2015 Les Princes Abbés Riesling (Alsace)

description: The aromatic tang of ripe lemon peel plays on the nose. The palate is pervaded by the same refreshing zestiness, shimmering with cheerful citrus brightness amidst riper notions of pear and peach. This is mouth-watering stuff, almost addictive with its dry zesty finish.
title: Domaines Schlumberger 2015 Les Princes Abbés Riesling (Alsace)

description: Delightful peachy notes define the fruity friendly nose. The palate adds zesty lemon to this rich fruit to create one of those dramatic and moreish Rieslings that teeter enticingly on the brink of peachy richness and citrus tang. The palate is slender, light footed and dry, the finish is whistle clean and wonderfully appetizing.
title: Domaine Charles Baur 2015 Cuvée Charles Riesling (Alsace)

description: Some yeasty funk hits the nose first. Underneath that sits and earthy, if slender, dry Riesling which has a subtle understated richness that seems very firmly anchored in earth. Pithy citrus zest frames and illuminates and promises future pleasure. This needs a little bottle age. Drink 2018–2030.
title: Domaine Barmès-Buecher 2014 Leimental Riesling (Alsace)

description: Some yeasty funk hits the nose first. Underneath that sits and earthy, if slender, dry Riesling which has a subtle understated richness that seems very firmly anchored in earth. Pithy citrus zest frames and illuminates and promises future pleasure. This needs a little bottle age. Drink 2018–2030.
title: Domaine Barmès-Buecher 2014 Leimental Riesling (Alsace)

description: The latest vintage from this estate is still very young. It has typical stalky black fruits, layers of wood aging that give spice and dark toast and following acidity. As it balances, the stalkiness will subside to give a richly structured wine. Drink from 2019.
title: Château du Coudray Montpensier 2015 Le Grand Bouqueteau Réserve  (Chinon)

description: This light, fresh wine, with its concentration on raspberry flavors, has lifted acidity and an edge of bitterness. The tannins are there, but relatively subdued, so it's likely to age quickly.
title: Louis Latour 2005  Morey-Saint-Denis

description: Dense and structured via dark, dry tannins, this is a big wine, showing power but not great subtlety. If you want solid Burgundy, this is the wine.
title: Domaine de l'Arlot 2005 Les Petits Plets  (Nuits-St.-Georges)

description: A cool wine that shows fresh fruitiness and a firm sense of structure. There is an attractive red berry character, laced with considerable acidity. It should age for a few months, so drink from 2014.
title: Vignerons de Bel Air 2012 Eté Fleuri  (Chiroubles)

description: This is a very fresh and fragrant style of Tavel, which can often be a bit weightier in style. Bubble gum and passion fruit aromas give way to citrus and berry flavors on the palate, finishing soft and easy. It should easily last at least well into the spring.
title: Château de Trinquevedel 2012  Tavel

description: A broad, ripe wine, it is simply fruity with attractive lemon and grapefruit flavors, touched by gooseberries. It's tangy, textured and likely to age for a 2–3 years, but you can also drink now.
title: Caves de Pouilly sur Loire 2012 Les Moulins à Vent  (Pouilly-Fumé)

description: A very pale flamingo-pink rosé, this is moderately confected in style, but vibrant and fresh. Cotton candy notes are balanced by peachy fruit and some floral elements, while the finish is mouthwatering. Drink up.
title: Louis Bernard 2012 Rosé (Côtes du Rhône)

description: With its smoky aromas, this early-drinking red is soft, light and full of red berry fruit. That dominant fruit is backed by light tannins and plenty of succulent acidity. Drink this crisp wine now.
title: Jean Perrier et Fils 2016 Cuvée Gastronomie Mondeuse Mondeuse (Savoie)

description: With its smoky aromas, this early-drinking red is soft, light and full of red berry fruit. That dominant fruit is backed by light tannins and plenty of succulent acidity. Drink this crisp wine now.
title: Jean Perrier et Fils 2016 Cuvée Gastronomie Mondeuse Mondeuse (Savoie)

description: Soft and full of red fruit, with balanced acidity, this is a rich style of rosé. Its generous texture has a crisp edge that lifts its full, creamy character. Drink now.
title: Clos Teddi 2016 Rosé (Patrimonio)

description: Soft and full of red fruit, with balanced acidity, this is a rich style of rosé. Its generous texture has a crisp edge that lifts its full, creamy character. Drink now.
title: Clos Teddi 2016 Rosé (Patrimonio)

description: This beautifully perfumed wine offers spicy Cabernet Franc notes and ripe red berry flavors. The tannins are still firm while not masking the spice, smokiness and blackberry fruit. For medium-term aging, from 2020.
title: Château Tour d'Horable 2016  Castillon Côtes de Bordeaux

description: A toasty, spicy aroma reveals the wood-aging flavors that are still firmly in place in this wine. Underneath, there is fine, juicy black currant fruit, crisp acidity and good potential. Drink from 2019.
title: Château Seguin 2015 Réserve  (Blaye Côtes de Bordeaux)

description: This structured wine is firm with tannins and stalky black currant fruit. It's dry, with a bitter edge from high extraction. A smoky character indicates aggressive wood aging and the need to soften further. Drink from 2020.
title: Château Les Gatines 2015  Blaye Côtes de Bordeaux

description: Aged in oak for 12 months, this rich wine is supple, lightly toasty and full of ripe red fruit. With a background of tannins, it's ready to age for another year. Drink from late 2018.
title: Château Laubès 2015  Bordeaux

description: The mineral texture that marks out a fine Meursault is very present here. Yellow fruits balance with this perfumed and intense wine. Still young and crisp, the acidity gives a tight, nervy edge. The wine obviously needs to age, so drink from 2017.
title: Alex Gambal 2013  Meursault

description: The mineral texture that marks out a fine Meursault is very present here. Yellow fruits balance with this perfumed and intense wine. Still young and crisp, the acidity gives a tight, nervy edge. The wine obviously needs to age, so drink from 2017.
title: Alex Gambal 2013  Meursault

description: This interesting and complex rosé—made from 65% Grenache, 25% Mourvèdre, 7% Vermentino and 3% Viognier—is aged for six months in oak. The resulting wine is a cellar-worthy selection that boasts upfront notes of toasted spice, lemon custard, vanilla bean and ripe red berries. The oak influence currently dominates the plush and generous palate, while the creamy texture and lingering smoky spice are enticingly decadent. While you can enjoy this rich wine now, give it some time for the oak to mellow and further integrate with the fruit; drink now–2017.
title: Gérard Bertrand 2014 Château La Sauvageonne GMVV Rosé (Coteaux du Languedoc)

description: This interesting and complex rosé—made from 65% Grenache, 25% Mourvèdre, 7% Vermentino and 3% Viognier—is aged for six months in oak. The resulting wine is a cellar-worthy selection that boasts upfront notes of toasted spice, lemon custard, vanilla bean and ripe red berries. The oak influence currently dominates the plush and generous palate, while the creamy texture and lingering smoky spice are enticingly decadent. While you can enjoy this rich wine now, give it some time for the oak to mellow and further integrate with the fruit; drink now–2017.
title: Gérard Bertrand 2014 Château La Sauvageonne GMVV Rosé (Coteaux du Languedoc)

description: This wine is ripe, with good balance between acidity and the rich yellow fruits. It has a lightly tangy character, although it is more about delicious juiciness and a warm, generous character that is lightly sustained by toast. Drink from 2017.
title: Domaine de la Croix Senaillet 2013  Pouilly-Fuissé

description: Tender notions of ripe pear make for an enticing nose. The palate has apple freshness and a rounded earthy aspect, despite its lightness. Drink soon.
title: Jean-Baptiste Adam 2015 Les Natures Pinot Blanc (Alsace)

description: The third wine of Château Valandraud, this is a lighter version of the estate. With its generous tannins and concentration, it is smoky, full of blackberry fruits and the potential to age for a few years. Drink from 2020.
title: Château Valandraud 2014 3 de Valandraud  (Saint-Émilion)

description: Crisp and fresh, this is a bright wine. It has some attractive tannins as well as fine acidity. With a light structure and black-currant fruit, it should be ready to drink soon, certainly from 2021.
title: Château Potensac 2014 La Chapelle de Potensac  (Médoc)

description: Dense with almost 100% Merlot, this is a rich wine. It has tannins that are cushioned by the ripe fruit and lifted by the acidity. The wine is dense with fruit, likely to develop quickly. Drink from 2022.
title: Château Nenin 2014 Fugue de Nenin  (Pomerol)

description: In the south of the Médoc, close to Bordeaux, this chateau has produced a ripe fruity wine. It has a fine balance between tannins and juicy black fruits. The blend, with its equal balance between Cabernet Sauvignon and Merlot, gives richness along with firm structure. Drink from 2019.
title: Château Magnol 2014  Haut-Médoc

description: In the south of the Médoc, close to Bordeaux, this chateau has produced a ripe fruity wine. It has a fine balance between tannins and juicy black fruits. The blend, with its equal balance between Cabernet Sauvignon and Merlot, gives richness along with firm structure. Drink from 2019.
title: Château Magnol 2014  Haut-Médoc

description: One of the group of vineyards that make up Domaines Lapalu, this wine is attractive and soft. It has generous black cherry and plum fruit along with gentle tannins that are already softening. Drink from 2019.
title: Château Liversan 2014  Haut-Médoc

description: From one of the two properties owned by the Mulliez family of Château Belle-Vue, this wine is full of dense tannins as well as black currants. It is likely to develop into a rich although always firm wine. Drink from 2020.
title: Château de Gironville 2014  Haut-Médoc

description: This fruity wine offers attractive cherry flavors that are spoiled by touches of banana. However, the acidity is good, keeping the wine fresh and indicating that it will be very drinkable in 2015.
title: Domaine du Haut-Poncié 2013  Saint-Amour

description: The wine is full of ripe bananas as well as cherry flavors, very much in the style of a nouveau. It's soft and rounded, with plenty of fruitiness as well as soft tannins. The wine is ready to drink now.
title: Domaine de la Madone 2013 Tradition  (Beaujolais-Villages)

description: With its bold aromas of cotton candy and two-cent bubblegum, this is just too tutti-frutti to rate higher. That said, if you like the style, it's a solid, well-made example, filled with bouncy fruit while finishing dry and refreshing.
title: Dauvergne & Ranvier 2013 Domaine des Muretins  (Tavel)

description: This ripe, fruity wine is ready to drink. With red berry fruits and fresh acidity spiced with wood flavors, it's an easy wine that is ripe and soft.
title: Patient Cottat 2012 Le Grand Caillou Pinot Noir (Vin de France)

description: Light and fruity, this wine is soft, with a sweeter touch than is sometimes found in Provence rosés. The blend includes Cabernet Sauvignon, giving a tannic edge as well as caramel and sweet raspberry flavors.
region: Vin de Pays de la Méditerranée
title: Les Vignobles Gueissard 2013 Le Petit Gueissard Rosé (Vin de Pays de la Méditerranée)

description: This is a blend of Pinot Noir from Burgundy and the south of France, giving a warm and rich character with soft tannins and juicy red plum fruit flavors. Cherry and fresh acidity complete this attractive, easy wine.
title: Simonnet-Febvre 2012 Pinot Noir (Vin de France)

description: Expanding from his Provence château, Sacha Lichine's new rosé is a blend from across the south of France. It's crisp, fruity, with a touch of sweetness, giving a soft, red berry fruit texture and light, fresh acidity.
title: Sacha Lichine 2013 SLS Single Blend Rosé (Vin de France)

description: A fresh, herbaceous Sauvignon Blanc, mainly from the French south-west. It has a lively, crisp, totally fruity character with grapefruit, gooseberry and a more tropical fruit hint. Drink now.
title: François Lurton 2013 Les Fumées Blanches Sauvignon Blanc (Vin de France)

description: The wine is all fruitiness, with attractive acidity and almond and lemon flavors. Made to be drunk instantly, it has the lightest texture, white fruit flavors and a fresh, crisp aftertaste.
title: Domaine Vincent Carême 2014 Spring  (Vouvray)

description: This ripe, pineapple- and peach-flavored wine has a soft texture, hints of vanilla and light acidity. It is rounded, full in the mouth and with a light textured aftertaste. Drink now.
title: Trenel Fils 2014 Homage to Heritage  (Mâcon-Villages)

description: This is a light, fruity wine with lemon and apricot flavors and a citrus tang that gives a lift. It's attractive, fresh and with a ripe, warm aftertaste.
title: Vignerons de Mancey 2014  Mâcon

description: Although less common than it once was, Malbec is still often part of the blend in red Bergerac. However, this pure Malbec is unusual. It's dark in color, with an almost medicinal aroma. The palate is pure black fruit with firm tannins to support the smoky blackberry flavors. Drink young for the fruitiness.
title: Château Laulerie 2013 Malbec (Bergerac)

description: With fruit drawn from all over Burgundy, this is a light, bright and refreshing wine. It has light acidity, spice and apple flavors and a bright, tight aftertaste. Drink now.
title: Jean-Luc and Paul Aegerter 2013 Colette  (Coteaux Bourguignons)

description: The Malbec in the blend adds its tannins to this wine meant to drink young. The spice and wood aging are balanced with acidity and a juicy aftertaste. Drink from late 2016.
title: Château Bélingard 2014 Bélingard Rouge Red (Bergerac)

description: The Malbec in the blend adds its tannins to this wine meant to drink young. The spice and wood aging are balanced with acidity and a juicy aftertaste. Drink from late 2016.
title: Château Bélingard 2014 Bélingard Rouge Red (Bergerac)

description: Proprietor Jean Marot's entry-level blend of 70% Grenache and 30% Syrah is aged entirely in cement and stainless steel, resulting in a fruit-driven, medium-bodied red that delivers cherry fruit, supple tannins and a slightly peppery finish. Drink now–2014.
title: Vindemio 2009 Regain Red (Ventoux)

description: Proprietor Jean Marot's entry-level blend of 70% Grenache and 30% Syrah is aged entirely in cement and stainless steel, resulting in a fruit-driven, medium-bodied red that delivers cherry fruit, supple tannins and a slightly peppery finish. Drink now–2014.
title: Vindemio 2009 Regain Red (Ventoux)

description: Pale salmon rosé, with peach and melon aromas. It's dry and minerally on the palate, with mouthwatering acids that linger on the finish.
title: Marrenon 2010 Grand Toque Rosé (Luberon)

description: Pale salmon rosé, with peach and melon aromas. It's dry and minerally on the palate, with mouthwatering acids that linger on the finish.
title: Marrenon 2010 Grand Toque Rosé (Luberon)

description: A full, rich and rounded wine that brings out the concentration from the low yielding old vines. It has rich black cherry and spice flavors that go with the delicious acidity and solid structure. This could be a wine to age, but it's so good now. If you want, drink until 2018.
title: Pascal Aufranc 2012 Vignes de 1939  (Chénas)

description: A full, rich and rounded wine that brings out the concentration from the low yielding old vines. It has rich black cherry and spice flavors that go with the delicious acidity and solid structure. This could be a wine to age, but it's so good now. If you want, drink until 2018.
title: Pascal Aufranc 2012 Vignes de 1939  (Chénas)

description: This is a full-bodied, extracted wine, loaded with cedar and vanilla notes that frame concentrated dark fruit. It's rich and velvety in texture yet manages to retain a sense of mouthwatering tension on the finish. Give it a few years to absorb some of the oak; drink 2020–2028.
title: LePlan-Vermeersch 2010 Grand Terroir GT-1 Red (Châteauneuf-du-Pape)

description: A rich, dry wine that has a honeyed character as well apricot and green plum flavors. It has a juicy, full-feeling structure and a texture that shows some minerality. It's a delicious, powerful white wine, reveling in its richness. Drink now, but better wait until 2015.
title: Château d'Aydie 2012 Odé d'Aydie  (Pacherenc du Vic Bilh)

description: A rich, dry wine that has a honeyed character as well apricot and green plum flavors. It has a juicy, full-feeling structure and a texture that shows some minerality. It's a delicious, powerful white wine, reveling in its richness. Drink now, but better wait until 2015.
title: Château d'Aydie 2012 Odé d'Aydie  (Pacherenc du Vic Bilh)

description: The folks at Jaboulet have nailed the texture of this wine, which is pure silk in the mouth. Mild hickory and menthol notes accent raspberry fruit, while slightly meaty, herbal and savory notes add complexity. Approachable now, it should easily evolve through 2025.
title: Paul Jaboulet Aîné 2010 Domaine des Pierrelles  (Côte Rôtie)

description: For a Bordeaux rosé, this is fresh and delicious in a light, fruity style, and immediately appealing. Not for aging, of course, but with a good touch of acidity as well as vanilla. Screwcap.
title: Château Suau 2010 Rosé (Bordeaux Rosé)

description: On the austere side, this shows more tannin than fruit, based around a dry core that has spread through the wine. There is some black plum skin and black currant fruit, but it is hard to find.
title: Château Moulin de Canhaut 2008  Médoc

description: Billed as a dessert wine, this is in fact more of an apéritif wine, with its botrytis sweetness muted by a soft, open character. It has ripe apricot flavors, hints of honey and a tang of orange peel.
title: Château Suau 2009 500 ml  (Cadillac)

description: Dense tannins and a solid, chunky character suggest a wine with richness. The black fruits are concentrated, with juiciness coming through over time. It has the ripe power of the 2009 vintage.
title: Château des Demoiselles 2009  Castillon Côtes de Bordeaux

description: This is a ripe, full wine that has both citrus fruit and richer pineapple and melon flavors. It is a spicy wine, touching on pepper and finishing with tight acidity. With its attractive fruit, it is ready to drink.
title: Marquis de Goulaine 2015 Cuvée du Millénaire Sur Lie  (Muscadet Sèvre et Maine)

description: This is a ripe, full wine that has both citrus fruit and richer pineapple and melon flavors. It is a spicy wine, touching on pepper and finishing with tight acidity. With its attractive fruit, it is ready to drink.
title: Marquis de Goulaine 2015 Cuvée du Millénaire Sur Lie  (Muscadet Sèvre et Maine)

description: Totally fresh, this is crisp and packed with citrus. A complex, tight texture brings out nervy acidity, a strongly mineral character and a firm structure. Age this youthful wine and drink from 2018.
title: Pascal Bouchard 2013 Montmains Premier Cru  (Chablis)

description: With a majority of Chardonnay from Grand Cru vineyards, this finely sculpted Champagne has crisp apple fruit and a steely, tight texture that suggests the need for bottle age. A light softness at the end rounds out this elegant wine.
title: Pannier NV Blanc Velours Brut  (Champagne)

description: The wine is tight and closed, hiding its natural fruitiness. For the moment, what is showing is acidity and a strongly mineral texture. This complex wine needs aging to fill out the structure. Drink from 2017.
title: Simonnet-Febvre 2012 Montmains Premier Cru  (Chablis)

description: Ripe and creamy in apple and pear fruitiness, this is cut by just the right amount of acidity. It's balanced, with fruit and and bright steeliness working well together. Drink from 2016.
title: Simonnet-Febvre 2012 Fourchaume Premier Cru  (Chablis)

description: Ripe and creamy in apple and pear fruitiness, this is cut by just the right amount of acidity. It's balanced, with fruit and and bright steeliness working well together. Drink from 2016.
title: Simonnet-Febvre 2012 Fourchaume Premier Cru  (Chablis)

description: With its beautiful pale pink color and bright fruitiness, this delicious wine also has a good depth of texture, mineral strength and tight acidity. Even though it is now six years old, it is showing no sign of maturity, so drink from 2016.
title: Mailly Grand Cru 2008 L'Intemporelle Brut Rosé  (Champagne)

description: A wood-dominated wine, all the dryness coming from barrels rather than fruit. Will it broaden out? It's hard to find the fruit at the moment, but there is weight under the wood, so perhaps.
title: Château Leboscq 2007  Médoc

description: A tight wine, the tannins almost too much for the fresh but lightweight fruits. The wood element is poised to soften the edges of the acidity and black currant fruits, but it needs another six months. The aftertaste is dominated by soft Merlot.
title: Château Grivière 2007  Médoc

description: A tight wine, the tannins almost too much for the fresh but lightweight fruits. The wood element is poised to soften the edges of the acidity and black currant fruits, but it needs another six months. The aftertaste is dominated by soft Merlot.
title: Château Grivière 2007  Médoc

description: Very perfumed wine, from organic grapes, the black plum and black currant flavors rounded by wood and dried with tannins. Flavorful, very friendly, with well-integrated fruit and acidity.
title: Château de Lagarde 2007 L de Lagarde  (Bordeaux)

description: Remember those vaguely anise-like white gumdrops? That describes the aromas and flavors found in the 2006 Les Sinards, albeit without the sugar. It's a medium- to full-bodied largely neutral white that should be consumed over the next year or two.
title: Perrin & Fils 2006 Les Sinards White (Châteauneuf-du-Pape)

description: Remember those vaguely anise-like white gumdrops? That describes the aromas and flavors found in the 2006 Les Sinards, albeit without the sugar. It's a medium- to full-bodied largely neutral white that should be consumed over the next year or two.
title: Perrin & Fils 2006 Les Sinards White (Châteauneuf-du-Pape)

description: A showy, aromatic white, the '07 Côté Jardin features assertive notes of orange zest and anise around a core of wet stones. It's full bodied without being blowsy, but should be consumed over the near term.
title: Vignobles Boudinaud 2007 Côté Jardin White (Côtes du Rhône)

description: Fairly deep in color for a sparkling rosé, Sparr's Brut Rosé offers bold, berry-like aromas with hints of spring flowers and a plump, slightly corpulent feel in the mouth. The flavors are a bit rustic, with hints of underbrush and scorched earth.
title: Pierre Sparr NV Brut Rosé Sparkling (Alsace)

description: Fairly deep in color for a sparkling rosé, Sparr's Brut Rosé offers bold, berry-like aromas with hints of spring flowers and a plump, slightly corpulent feel in the mouth. The flavors are a bit rustic, with hints of underbrush and scorched earth.
title: Pierre Sparr NV Brut Rosé Sparkling (Alsace)

description: The vineyards of the 13th century abbey of La Ferté produces some of the best Givry. This wine has great structure with firm tannins, and also rich, juicy fruitiness that offers delicious acidity and a more solid base for aging. Drink from 2016.
designation: Clos du Cellier aux Moines Premier Cru
title: Domaines Devillard 2011 Clos du Cellier aux Moines Premier Cru  (Givry)

description: Warm, fragrant and juicy, this is an off-dry, just peppery wine, full of ripe peach and pear flavors. Very fruity and delicious.
title: Kuentz-Bas 2011 Trois Châteaux Pinot Auxerrois (Alsace)

description: Fresh and very crisp, this is a distinctive, fragrant wine. It has concentration, tight acidity, with apples and minerality. At the end, the wine is more floral, open and ripe. Drink after 2016.
title: Jean-Marc Bernhard 2011 Vieilles Vignes Riesling (Alsace)

description: The winemaking team of Château Lafite makes one of the better branded Bordeaux. This 2006 has tobacco aromas followed by flavors of fresh black currants with an attractive smoky character and a fine line of balancing acidity.
title: Domaines Barons de Rothschild (Lafite) 2006 Réserve Spéciale  (Pauillac)

description: This is a simple, freshly red-fruited wine that needs to be drunk now. The structure is light, fruity, with a hint of smokiness and an appetizing finish.
title: Château Fontis 2006  Médoc

description: This is a simple, freshly red-fruited wine that needs to be drunk now. The structure is light, fruity, with a hint of smokiness and an appetizing finish.
title: Château Fontis 2006  Médoc

description: An almost medicinal, tart wine that certainly has the dry texture of botrytis, but then shows more in the way of a herbal character.
title: Château Caillou 2006  Sauternes

description: A more serious attempt at crafting a good Pinot Noir in Languedoc-Roussillon and quite a successful one as well. Vanilla dominates the nose but yields to cherry pie filling and cherry jam flavors in the mouth. Mineral and strawberry notes shine through on the crisp, moderately long finish.
title: Gérard Bertrand 2006 Réserve Spéciale Pinot Noir (Vin de Pays d'Oc)

description: 92-94 Barrel sample. Smooth, the wood almost dominant but finally integrating well with the ripe yellow fruits. It is rich, creamy, with some toastiness, but well balanced.
title: Château Larrivet Haut-Brion 2008 Barrel sample  (Pessac-Léognan)

description: 92-94 Barrel sample. A big, concentrated, powerful wine, yet also one restrained by elegant fresh fruits. There is plenty of style here, a complex mix of fruits, acidity and balanced tannins.
title: Château Langoa Barton 2008 Barrel sample  (Saint-Julien)

description: 92-94 Barrel sample. This is a dark, firm, strongly tannic but impressive wine, with a dry core of dark fruits. They open slowly to reveal a rich undertow of blackberry jelly fruit flavors.
title: Château Haut-Bailly 2008 Barrel sample  (Pessac-Léognan)

description: 92-94 Barrel sample. This is a dark, firm, strongly tannic but impressive wine, with a dry core of dark fruits. They open slowly to reveal a rich undertow of blackberry jelly fruit flavors.
title: Château Haut-Bailly 2008 Barrel sample  (Pessac-Léognan)

description: 92-94 Barrel sample. Firm, richly structured, powered through with botrytis, a dried apricot and peach character, which is tight, the acidity compensating with a great vivid character.
title: Château Guiraud 2008 Barrel sample  (Sauternes)

description: 92-94 Barrel sample. Firm, richly structured, powered through with botrytis, a dried apricot and peach character, which is tight, the acidity compensating with a great vivid character.
title: Château Guiraud 2008 Barrel sample  (Sauternes)

description: 92-94 Barrel sample. Firm, but ripe, very sweet Merlot coming through a core of tense acidity. This is chunky, foursquare, remaining fruity while also tannic.
title: Château Clinet 2008 Barrel sample  (Pomerol)

description: 92-94 Barrel sample. A serious, but elegant wine. It has structure, but that is put in second place to the fresh black plum and dried fig fruits. Lively acidity to give the wine an extra freshness
title: Château Trottevieille 2008 Barrel sample  (Saint-Émilion)

description: 92-94 Barrel sample. Rich rather than sweet, this is stuffed full of botrytis. The wine is powered through with this dusty texture, rolling richly but catching the dried fruit character.
title: Château Rieussec 2008 Barrel sample  (Sauternes)

description: 92-94 Barrel sample. Rich rather than sweet, this is stuffed full of botrytis. The wine is powered through with this dusty texture, rolling richly but catching the dried fruit character.
title: Château Rieussec 2008 Barrel sample  (Sauternes)

description: La Gaffelière, now under the expert guidance of Saint-Emilion's guru Stéphane Derenoncourt, is producing serious wine. None more so than this firmly closed but powerful and dense 2006. Bitter chocolate and dark tannins come together to form a shell covering the weight of the fruit. It will probably always be firm, but the black currant fruit flavors will come through eventually—maybe in 5–7 years.
title: Château la Gaffelière 2006  Saint-Émilion

description: A richly liquorous wine, ripe and packed with harmonious sweet textures. At the same time over the ripe structure there is a layer of lively lemon, spice and ginger, spiked with fresh tangerines. The end result is smooth, balanced and vibrant.
title: Château Doisy-Védrines 2006  Barsac

description: A big, dark, rich wine with an impressively opulent structure allied to fresh, bright Merlot character. The flavors of black berry juice are followed by chocolate, bitter coffee and vibrant acidity, which gives freshness to the finish.
title: Château Canon 2006  Saint-Émilion

description: With a high proportion of Cabernet Sauvignon, this wine has both structured and superbly rich fruit. The tannins are firm, but show a sweet, enticing edge to them, giving a full body and classic, fresh black currant acidity. An impressive wine, which definitely needs to age—five years or more.
title: Château Sociando-Mallet 2006  Haut-Médoc

description: With a high proportion of Cabernet Sauvignon, this wine has both structured and superbly rich fruit. The tannins are firm, but show a sweet, enticing edge to them, giving a full body and classic, fresh black currant acidity. An impressive wine, which definitely needs to age—five years or more.
title: Château Sociando-Mallet 2006  Haut-Médoc

description: Beautifully ripe Cabernet dominates this dense, complex wine. It is balanced so finely, as if on the point of a pin, with black currant juice freshness set against dark tannins and powerful structure. A wine to age, and one of the successes of 2006.
title: Château Pichon Longueville 2006  Pauillac

description: Beautifully ripe Cabernet dominates this dense, complex wine. It is balanced so finely, as if on the point of a pin, with black currant juice freshness set against dark tannins and powerful structure. A wine to age, and one of the successes of 2006.
title: Château Pichon Longueville 2006  Pauillac

description: This wine appears to mark a departure from Trottevieille's normally strict style, showing more opulence, new wood and ripeness. There is still a touch of austerity initially, but from that point, the wine opens out with a great burst of fresh blackberry jelly and stylish texture.
title: Château Trottevieille 2006  Saint-Émilion

description: Beautifully dense, this generous, rich wine combines great fruit with a firm but sweet structure. The new wood element is still prominent, but this is now beginning to blend well with the ripe fruit. To finish, the tannins reassert themselves.
title: Château Léoville Poyferré 2006  Saint-Julien

description: The character of this wine, a straight line of tannins and black currant fruit flavors, is the model of a classic Pauillac. It has all the structure as well as some austerity and severity at this stage in its development. But the fruit texture is rich enough, dried fruits and spice followed by licorice and bitter chocolate. Age for five years at least.
title: Château Duhart-Milon 2006  Pauillac

description: The character of this wine, a straight line of tannins and black currant fruit flavors, is the model of a classic Pauillac. It has all the structure as well as some austerity and severity at this stage in its development. But the fruit texture is rich enough, dried fruits and spice followed by licorice and bitter chocolate. Age for five years at least.
title: Château Duhart-Milon 2006  Pauillac

description: A beautifully crafted wine that has both richness and sweetness. It brings together the fresh character of 2006 with more powerful elements, such as new wood and spice, enveloped plushly with ripe fruit. The tannins have a dark element, but fit well with the sweet fruit. All in all, a delicious wine that also has aging potential.
title: Château du Tertre 2006  Margaux

description: A beautifully crafted wine that has both richness and sweetness. It brings together the fresh character of 2006 with more powerful elements, such as new wood and spice, enveloped plushly with ripe fruit. The tannins have a dark element, but fit well with the sweet fruit. All in all, a delicious wine that also has aging potential.
title: Château du Tertre 2006  Margaux

description: A wine that succeeds in combining great depth of flavor and structure with an impressive array of flavors. On top of the tannins is juicy black fruit, cocoa, a welter of spice and ripeness. The acidity and new wood put the wine into a more modern style. Wait for at least 5–7 years.
title: Château Troplong Mondot 2006  Saint-Émilion

description: A big, brooding wine, the fruit ripe and dense. Richness surrounds structure, giving a sumptuous layer to the dusty tannins. Flavors of currants, spice and juicy berries flow through the wine, giving power and suavity. The freshness of 2006 shows on the finish of this important wine.
title: Château Palmer 2006  Margaux

description: A big, brooding wine, the fruit ripe and dense. Richness surrounds structure, giving a sumptuous layer to the dusty tannins. Flavors of currants, spice and juicy berries flow through the wine, giving power and suavity. The freshness of 2006 shows on the finish of this important wine.
title: Château Palmer 2006  Margaux

description: Year after year, Lynch-Bages is able to produce sumptuous wines, typically rich, powerful and structured. This is solid, the blackberry ripe fruit enveloping this structure with a velvet sheen. This is developing into one of the successes of the vintage.
title: Château Lynch-Bages 2006  Pauillac

description: Year after year, Lynch-Bages is able to produce sumptuous wines, typically rich, powerful and structured. This is solid, the blackberry ripe fruit enveloping this structure with a velvet sheen. This is developing into one of the successes of the vintage.
title: Château Lynch-Bages 2006  Pauillac

description: After initial tastings suggested there was too much tannin, the wine has undergone a welcome transformation. It has become powerful and ripe, deliciously sumptuous, allying the tannins with densely ripe, sweet black fruits. It keeps its sense of balance, but all this density gives aging potential.
title: Château Giscours 2006  Margaux

description: After initial tastings suggested there was too much tannin, the wine has undergone a welcome transformation. It has become powerful and ripe, deliciously sumptuous, allying the tannins with densely ripe, sweet black fruits. It keeps its sense of balance, but all this density gives aging potential.
title: Château Giscours 2006  Margaux

description: A firm, densely structured wine, with the sweetness turned as much into richness. The flavors are of Seville orange zest, the richness coming from honey and almonds, balanced with dry botrytis. An impressive wine that needs time for aging.
title: Château de Fargues 2006  Sauternes

description: A firm, densely structured wine, with the sweetness turned as much into richness. The flavors are of Seville orange zest, the richness coming from honey and almonds, balanced with dry botrytis. An impressive wine that needs time for aging.
title: Château de Fargues 2006  Sauternes

description: This very ripe wine tastes of supermature grapes; it' s soft and formless.
title: Château Timberlay 2009  Bordeaux Supérieur

description: This very ripe wine tastes of supermature grapes; it' s soft and formless.
title: Château Timberlay 2009  Bordeaux Supérieur

description: Lean and rather dry, this has old wood and lean fruit flavors.
title: Château Majoureau 2009 Hyppos  (Bordeaux Supérieur)

description: This wine's fruit is overripe, which spoils the structure that has been built around it.
title: Château Bellevue 2010  Bordeaux Supérieur

description: An unattractive green-herb aroma is followed by a green-pepper- and dill-flavored palate.
title: Maison Sichel 2010 Sirius  (Bordeaux Blanc)

description: Big and bold with great strawberry and red cherry flavors, this wine has all the elements of dense fruit, intense acidity and rich tannins. The structure is dark and full of potential. With acidity at the end to give a lift of freshness, this is a wine for the long-term. Drink from 2020.
title: Joseph Drouhin 2012 Petit Monts Premier Cru  (Vosne-Romanée)

description: Big and bold with great strawberry and red cherry flavors, this wine has all the elements of dense fruit, intense acidity and rich tannins. The structure is dark and full of potential. With acidity at the end to give a lift of freshness, this is a wine for the long-term. Drink from 2020.
title: Joseph Drouhin 2012 Petit Monts Premier Cru  (Vosne-Romanée)

description: This offers a firm, dense structure, with dark tannins and big, ripe, opulent fruits. At the same time the elegance that is the hallmark of the domaine is equally present with stylish red fruits and a velvet texture. The wine needs to age to be at its peak, although it is beautiful now. Drink from 2020.
title: Domaine Jean Grivot 2013  Clos de Vougeot

description: This wine is very young, still with layers of wood. It is going to be a structured, dense and packed with a strong mineral texture. To contrast, generous red plum fruits and intense acidity are ready to convey a deep, rich character. Drink this impressive wine from 2019
title: Domaine Jean Grivot 2013  Echézeaux

description: This wine is perfumed with gorgeous fruit that contrasts with the strict minerality. The tannins under the fruit are severe, solid, dark and promising enormous potential. Concentrated even while it celebrates great fruit, it is going to last for many years. Drink from 2023.
title: Louis Jadot 2013  Chambertin Clos de Bèze

description: Packed with tannins and boasting an enormous structure, this wine is opulent while very firm. At the same time, smoky acidity shoots through all this density. From a great terroir, this wine shows minerality and its great structure well. Drink from 2023.
title: Louis Jadot 2013  Chapelle-Chambertin

description: A firm and tannic wine, this has dry spices, dark fruits and concentration. Great depth of flavor gives a serious wine that also has a fruit-driven profile. Concentrated dark tannins push this wine to a great height and impressive length. Drink from 2020.
title: Joseph Drouhin 2012  Grands-Echezeaux

description: This blend of the very local Petit Courbu and Petit Manseng grapes comes from the same region as Madiran. The wine is dry but rich—very rich—with apricot and honey flavors. It has concentration, a great tang of lemon and just enough acidity to keep everything in order. This is ready to drink.
title: Vignobles Brumont 2012 Château Bouscassé Les Jardins  (Pacherenc du Vic Bilh)

description: This is deliciously hedonistic in the best traditions of Volnay, opulent and powered with flavors of blackberry jelly, dry tannins and perfumed violets. This is a big, ripe, solid wine whose perfumes give an enticing exotic aftertaste.
title: Roux Père et Fils 2004 Les Santenots Premier Cru  (Volnay)

description: A beautifully proportioned wine, from its rich yet mineral texture to its full grapefruit and gooseberry flavors. It gradually shows toast as well as wonderful acidity. For aging over 4–6 years.
title: Simonnet-Febvre 2008 Les Clos Grand Cru  (Chablis)

description: Taut and edgy, very steely in character, with almost an austere character in its youth. Its fruits are definitely on the citrus side of the spectrum, crisp yet rich as well. The acidity shoots right through the wine.
title: Simonnet-Febvre 2008 Blanchots  (Chablis)
