description: This firm Pinot Noir has made subtle use of wood aging to round out and become rich. Red cherry fruits fill the mouth with soft tannins and toasty spice giving some complexity. The wine could age, although it is ready to drink now.
title: François Millet 2012  Sancerre

description: With the palest pink color, this crisp wine is made from Pinot Noir and Chardonnay. It's fruity, layered with red currants and cherries that are tightly textured. The aftertaste, dry and fresh with a hint of spice suggests the wine could do with some more bottle aging.
title: Duval-Leroy NV Prestige Premier Cru Brut Rosé  (Champagne)

description: With the palest pink color, this crisp wine is made from Pinot Noir and Chardonnay. It's fruity, layered with red currants and cherries that are tightly textured. The aftertaste, dry and fresh with a hint of spice suggests the wine could do with some more bottle aging.
title: Duval-Leroy NV Prestige Premier Cru Brut Rosé  (Champagne)

description: This is a generous wine, although one that will need some serious aging. It is rich in tannins and powered by a firm structure. The fruit offers the weight to counter the tannins. It just needs time. Drink from 2024.
title: Chanson Père et Fils 2015 Les Fèves Premier Cru  (Beaune)

description: This is a generous wine, although one that will need some serious aging. It is rich in tannins and powered by a firm structure. The fruit offers the weight to counter the tannins. It just needs time. Drink from 2024.
title: Chanson Père et Fils 2015 Les Fèves Premier Cru  (Beaune)

description: This wine is firm yet ripe, with a bold yet tight character that foreshadows a rich wine in the future. The cherry and red plum flavors are lush and generous. It is going to be a delicious wine, full of concentration. Drink from 2023.
title: Louis Latour 2015 En Chevret Premier Cru  (Volnay)

description: This wine is firm yet ripe, with a bold yet tight character that foreshadows a rich wine in the future. The cherry and red plum flavors are lush and generous. It is going to be a delicious wine, full of concentration. Drink from 2023.
title: Louis Latour 2015 En Chevret Premier Cru  (Volnay)

description: This is a rich wine with great potential. Its juicy spice and acidity are balanced with the red fruits, the generous texture and the fine structure. It is a wine that sums up the ripeness of the vintage. Drink from 2024.
title: Seguin-Manuel 2015 Champs Pimont Premier Cru  (Beaune)

description: Ripe and rounded, this softly textured wine has swathes of yellow fruits that are deliciously cut with lime and lemon acidity. The wine, with its touches of toast is balanced, promising a fine future. Drink from 2021.
title: Domaine Buisson Battault 2015 Les Gouttes d'Or Premier Cru  (Meursault)

description: Aged for a year in new wood barrels, this powerful, concentrated wine shows both richness and considerable aging potential. It is a powerhouse of ripe damson fruits and impressive tannins. Structured and intense, it needs to age for many years. Don't drink before 2026.
title: Domaine Bertagna 2015  Clos Saint-Denis

description: This structured wine comes from one of the lesser-known Grand Crus of Vosne-Romanée. But it does have the structure and density of the wines from this run of grand crus, with bold tannins over the red-cherry fruits. It is likely to be a structured wine for many years. Drink from 2027.
title: Louis Latour 2015 Les Quatre Journaux  (Romanée-St.-Vivant)

description: This wine from the Corton Grand Cru vineyard is packed with tannins as well as smoky fruit. It is richly structured and firm, yet the fruit is equally powerful, showing bold black fruits struck against bright acidity. The wine will need considerable aging; drink from 2025.
title: Louis Latour 2015 Château Corton Grancey  (Corton)

description: This is Burgundian opulence, with generous, rounded black-fruit and -berry flavors. Supporting this richness are the tannins that will allow the wine to age. From Louis Latour Domaine vineyards, it has a solid, dense structure that needs plenty of time. Drink from 2027.
title: Louis Latour 2015 Cuvée Héritiers Latour  (Chambertin)

description: Big, rich while also smooth, this is going to be a impressive wine. It has power and firm tannins as well as plenty of ripe black fruits and acidity. This wine, from one of the range of grand crus in Vosne-Romanée, will age well. Drink from 2026.
title: Henri de Villamont 2015  Grands-Echezeaux

description: Ripe, warm and with delicious strawberry and red-plum fruits, the wine is generous and full of fruit. The tannins are also there, a structure just to support all this fruit. It will be an opulent and beautiful wine as it ages. Drink from 2025.
title: Albert Morot 2015 Les Cent Vignes Premier Cru  (Beaune)

description: Ripe, warm and with delicious strawberry and red-plum fruits, the wine is generous and full of fruit. The tannins are also there, a structure just to support all this fruit. It will be an opulent and beautiful wine as it ages. Drink from 2025.
title: Albert Morot 2015 Les Cent Vignes Premier Cru  (Beaune)

description: From one of the high-quality Premier Crus that have much of the reflected glory of the Vosne-Romanée grand crus, the beautiful wine is ripe and packed with great red fruits. Its wood aging is a rich support to this opulent wine with considerable potential. Drink from 2025.
designation: Domaine du Clos Frantin Les Malconsorts Premier Cru
title: Albert Bichot 2015 Domaine du Clos Frantin Les Malconsorts Premier Cru  (Vosne-Romanée)

description: A flagship wine for this producer, this is rich and seductive, opulent even. Bold yellow fruits, ripe apples and pears are surrounded by a youthful texture that will allow it to age. The fruit and the touches of wood are still present, but will integrate beautfully. Drink this wine from 2023.
title: Louis Latour 2015  Corton-Charlemagne

description: With spice as well as ripe fruit, this is warm, rich wine. It is tangy with acidity and lemon zest while being full with hints of yellow fruits. This generous wine is ready to drink.
title: Mommessin 2014  Saint-Véran

description: At this stage, the wine seems to have too much wood. Hopefully this will dissipate because round yellow fruits are all there, along with fresh, crisp acidity. It is a wine with potential and will be better from 2017.
title: Domaine Ferret 2014 Tête de Cru Les Perrières  (Pouilly-Fuissé)

description: Philip the Bold was Duke of Burgundy in the 14th century and owner of this estate. This wine that comes from vines next to Saint-Aubin is cool and fresh, emphasizing red currants and acidity. It needs to broaden out, which will happen in the next two to three years. Drink from 2019.
title: Château de Santenay 2014 Clos Philippe le Hardi  (Hautes Cotes de Beaune)

description: This has a mineral character that shines through the crisp, fresh citrus and green plums. It is immediately attractive and is delicious to drink now.
title: Albert Bichot 2014  Pouilly-Fuissé

description: Crisp and tight, this is a steely, mineral-driven wine. The texture is taut and nervy, lively with acidity and just hinting at a more creamy future. The toasty edge is attractive and fills the wine. Drink from 2017.
title: Seguin-Manuel 2014  Pouilly-Fuissé

description: At 1,100 feet, this high-altitude vineyard yields a crisp and tangy wine. The brothers, whom Becky Wasserman lists among the Fuissé “revolutionaries,” employ biodynamic practices. The wine has great swathes of bright acidity and a tight, mineral texture. With lively acidity, it is a bright, fruity wine to drink now.
title: Bret Brothers 2014 Climat En Carementrant  (Pouilly-Fuissé)

description: This wine is initially soft and rounded. Only as it opens does the tight, crisp texture becomes apparent, bringing out crisp, green, citrus flavors as well as hinting at warmer apricots. The wine is still young; drink from late 2016.
title: Saget la Perrière 2014 Domaine de la Perrière  (Sancerre)

description: Ripe and juicy, this attractive offering from winemaker Marie-Dominique Watrin has a rich seam of blackberry fruits and balanced acidity. The aftertaste with its fresh character shows that the wine is nearly ready to drink; enjoy from the end of 2016. The 20 acres of Merlot, Cabernet Sauvignon and Cabernet Franc vines are hand picked; no herbicides are used.
title: Château le Doyenne 2012  Côtes de Bordeaux

description: Ripe and juicy, this attractive offering from winemaker Marie-Dominique Watrin has a rich seam of blackberry fruits and balanced acidity. The aftertaste with its fresh character shows that the wine is nearly ready to drink; enjoy from the end of 2016. The 20 acres of Merlot, Cabernet Sauvignon and Cabernet Franc vines are hand picked; no herbicides are used.
title: Château le Doyenne 2012  Côtes de Bordeaux

description: Though 60% Sémillon and 40% Sauvignon Blanc, this wine reflects herbaceous Sauvignon in style. It is lightly perfumed while also having intense acidity. The aftertaste, all fresh fruit, conveys a lifted green-fruit character. Drink now. In 1991, enologist Jacques Chardat bought the estate where 19th-century windmills (moulins) still stand above the Gironde Estuary. Consulting enologist is Eric Delacroix.
title: Château Lacaussade-Saint-Martin 2014  Blaye Côtes de Bordeaux

description: This wine is dry, packed with acidity at this young stage. It is crisp and lightly nutty in character, perfumed and still tangy with orange zest. Drink from 2016.
title: Château de la Roulerie 2014 Chenin Blanc (Anjou)

description: This is the top wine from Château Haute-Serre, a powerful expression of Malbec, very dense and solid, but certainly not overpowering. It has ripe fruit that is held in check by brooding tannins and a firm structure, giving it weight but also surprising restraint. Age for 4–5 years.
designation: Château de Haute-Serre Cuvée Géron Dadine
title: Georges Vigouroux 2005 Château de Haute-Serre Cuvée Géron Dadine Malbec (Cahors)

description: This is wonderfully rich and dense, with dry and dusty tannins that float in the depths of the powerful black fruits, well integrated with the wood. This is impressive Malbec, showing its juicy qualities allied with its huge tannins. It could do with 3–4 years' aging.
title: Clos Troteligotte 2005 K Lys Malbec (Cahors)

description: This is a dense, ripe and fruity wine, with forward aromas and flavors of black plum, cherry and muddled berries that are kissed by sweet spice. Medium acidity and supple tannins result in a plush yet accessible and well-balanced palate. Drink now.
title: Le Paradou 2014 Grenache (Vin de France)

description: This is a crisp wine, tight with minerality. It has apple fruits as well as citrus, although the wine tends to a tight texture. There is potential and the wine will soften from 2016, but it will always have this tension.
title: Manciat-Poncet 2014 Le Clos  (Saint-Véran)

description: This is a crisp wine, tight with minerality. It has apple fruits as well as citrus, although the wine tends to a tight texture. There is potential and the wine will soften from 2016, but it will always have this tension.
title: Manciat-Poncet 2014 Le Clos  (Saint-Véran)

description: A deep purple color, this ripe selection leads with lush aromas of raspberry jam, blueberry and boysenberry, all of which carry through to the fruit-forward palate. Medium tannins and ample acidity provide good framing to the fruity richness, resulting in a crushed velvet texture. Drink now.
title: La Vieille Ferme 2015 Red (Vin de France)

description: Strong wood flavors dominate this wine. While there are hints of the juicy red fruits, the burnt toast is too strong. While that will soften, it seems likely that woodiness will be with the wine a long time.
title: Patriarche Père et Fils 2014 Les Chaboeufs Premier Cru  (Nuits-St.-Georges)

description: This wine has wood acidity more than fruit freshness, but its citrus and apple flavors show potential. Although spice and toast dominate for the moment, a crisper character comes through at the end.
title: Patriarche Père et Fils 2013 Les Vergers Premier Cru  (Chassagne-Montrachet)

description: This is a ripe, red fruit and caramel flavored wine. With its strawberry flavor, balanced acidity and touch of spice, it is soft and rounded yet finishes with a fresh touch.
title: Famille Laplace 2015 Aramis Rosé (Vin de France)

description: Sourced from grapes grown in the Côte Chalonnaise, this is a soft, red-fruit-flavored wine, with a ripe, jammy character that makes it almost sweet. It is ready to drink.
title: Château de Santenay 2014 Vieilles Vignes  (Bourgogne)

description: Sourced from grapes grown in the Côte Chalonnaise, this is a soft, red-fruit-flavored wine, with a ripe, jammy character that makes it almost sweet. It is ready to drink.
title: Château de Santenay 2014 Vieilles Vignes  (Bourgogne)

description: Ripe yellow fruits give this wine a soft and rich character. With a tangy, citrus edge it is also crisp and fresh. The combination makes for a lively, light wine that is ready to drink.
title: Jean-Luc and Paul Aegerter 2014 Vieilles Vignes  (Bourgogne)

description: Ripe yellow fruits give this wine a soft and rich character. With a tangy, citrus edge it is also crisp and fresh. The combination makes for a lively, light wine that is ready to drink.
title: Jean-Luc and Paul Aegerter 2014 Vieilles Vignes  (Bourgogne)

description: The 18-month wood aging has made this both a rich wine and a structured one. Black fruits are beginning to emerge from the dense texture. It is serious, complex and worth aging. Drink from 2018.
title: Mas des Etoiles 2012 Malbec (Cahors)

description: While there are powerful tannins at work here, this wine is mainly full of rich black fruits that have a juicy side from the acidity. The addition of Tannat brings even more tannin to the wine while also giving it density and longevity. Drink from 2019. The wine comes from a long-time wine family that tended the few remaining Malbec grapes that survived phylloxera of late 1800s. Alain Gayraud is the current owner.
title: Château Lamartine 2012 Cuvée Particulière Malbec-Tannat (Cahors)

description: Made from organic grapes, this wine blends every variety grown in Gaillac. Everything gels together to give a concentrated wine that is both solid and powerful with a dry core. Rich berry fruits are complemented by a stream of acidity. It's a wine to age; drink from 2017.
title: Château de Rhodes 2012 Red (Gaillac)

description: Named after the dry wind that blows through the Jurançon vineyards, this light, poised sweet wine has typical freshness, the botrytis never cloying but immersed in currants, fresh apricots. The wine has a lively, buoyant, sweet character.
title: Lionel Osmin & Cie 2008 Foehn  (Jurançon)

description: This 100% Chenin Blanc is a beautiful exaple of what the variety can express: soft florals loaded with garrigue notes alongside tropical fruit aromas of mango, guava and pineapple. It's vibrant in the mouth, with moderate acidity and a lifting backbone of lemon verbena. The finish lingers gracefully, and overall the wine is ripe and attractive without being sweet or cloying.
title: Château Rives-Blanques 2008 Dédicace Chenin Blanc (Limoux)

description: This 100% Chenin Blanc is a beautiful exaple of what the variety can express: soft florals loaded with garrigue notes alongside tropical fruit aromas of mango, guava and pineapple. It's vibrant in the mouth, with moderate acidity and a lifting backbone of lemon verbena. The finish lingers gracefully, and overall the wine is ripe and attractive without being sweet or cloying.
title: Château Rives-Blanques 2008 Dédicace Chenin Blanc (Limoux)

description: This a tight and mineral wine from Mesnil-sur-Oger in the heart of the Côte des Blancs of Champagne. It's still youthful, fresh and crisp, with lemon and tangy citrus flavors. The lively character will certainly round out in 5–6 years.
designation: Cuvée Pierre Moncuit-Delos Grand Cru Brut
title: Pierre Moncuit NV Cuvée Pierre Moncuit-Delos Grand Cru Brut Chardonnay (Champagne)

description: Firm and solid tannins with a dry core offers a dark character and density. Along with this, the wine has a ripe, fruity character that's packed with acidity and layered with wood.
title: Château Haut-Simard 2010  Saint-Émilion

description: This is a very complete wine, with all the fruit and tannin elements in place. There's a fine and rich character here as well as a more austere, mineral side. The combination results in supporting tannins, dark fruits and good aging potential.
title: Château Haut Dina 2010  Castillon Côtes de Bordeaux

description: Since this is 100% Sauvignon Blanc, it is intensely crisp, with grapefruit flavors and bright acidity that lead into a lemongrass aftertaste. It's clean and fresh, and is likely to mature quickly.
title: Château Couhins-Lurton 2010  Pessac-Léognan

description: Since this is 100% Sauvignon Blanc, it is intensely crisp, with grapefruit flavors and bright acidity that lead into a lemongrass aftertaste. It's clean and fresh, and is likely to mature quickly.
title: Château Couhins-Lurton 2010  Pessac-Léognan

description: Densely tannic while also fruity, this is a product of ripe fruits that give a black currant flavor as well as a solid structure. The acidity gives great lift to the end of this finely made wine.
title: Château Chantemerle 2010  Blaye Côtes de Bordeaux

description: This intensely juicy, fruity wine is high in acidity. It's dominated by fresh black currants as well as spice from wood aging. It has fruit concentration, but needs time to round out and soften. Drink from 2015.
title: Domaine de Courteillac 2011  Bordeaux Supérieur

description: This is a perfumed wine with eucalyptus aromas and new wood flavors. The wood element is held in balance by flavors of ripe berry fruits and delicate acidity. Keep this wine until 2015.
designation: Les Hauts de Palette Vieilles Vignes
title: Château Saintongey 2011 Les Hauts de Palette Vieilles Vignes  (Bordeaux)

description: With its fresh black-currant fruits and ever-present acidity, this is a wine that sums up the vintage. The tannins are there, giving a sense of dryness to this fragrant wine. On the finish, there is also an attractive juiciness.
title: Château Gromel Bel Air 2011 Cuvée Eva  (Bordeaux Supérieur)

description: A mineral, textured wine, this is full of grassy gooseberry and grapefruit flavors. Fruit on the palate is accented with a chalky character and strong, very present acidity. Drink in six months.
title: Château Bonnet 2012  Bordeaux Blanc

description: Made by Pierre Clément at Domaine de Châtenoy for the Xavier Flouret range, this is smooth, rich and soft. Generous and ripe with red berry fruits and gentle tannins, it could age until late 2015 before drinking.
title: Xavier Flouret 2012 Domaine de Châtenoy Rouge Noir  (Menetou-Salon)

description: Only red wine can be produced under the Cahors appellation, so this is released as a Côtes du Lot. It does however come from the Château de Mercuès vineyard, producing a floral, fresh and creamed-apple flavored wine. It is now ready to drink.
title: Georges Vigouroux 2012 Chenin de Mercuès Chenin Blanc (Côtes du Lot)

description: Only red wine can be produced under the Cahors appellation, so this is released as a Côtes du Lot. It does however come from the Château de Mercuès vineyard, producing a floral, fresh and creamed-apple flavored wine. It is now ready to drink.
title: Georges Vigouroux 2012 Chenin de Mercuès Chenin Blanc (Côtes du Lot)

description: This is a fresh, almond and apple-flavored sparkling wine. With crisp acidity and some attractive bottle aging, it's ripe but cut by a steely aftertaste, and is ready to drink.
title: Domaine Vincent Carême 2012 Cuvée T  (Vouvray)

description: The small region of Buzet halfway between Bordeaux and Toulouse produces fruity, ripe and full-bodied Bordeaux-blend wines. This rich example has soft tannins and a smooth texture. Blackberry fruit flavors are right up front with a light amount of juicy acidity at the end. It is ready to drink.
title: Lionel Osmin & Cie 2012 Red (Buzet)

description: With its high elevation, it is logical that Chiroubles produces some of the coolest Beaujolais cru wines. This is fruity with a tang of acidity and a mineral texture that is enhanced by a crisp character. The wine has light tannins and a final juicy finish.
title: Domaine de la Combe au Loup 2015  Chiroubles
winery: Domaine de la Combe au Loup

description: For many consumers, Guigal remains a reference point for Rhône wines. This Saint-Joseph is a fine example, showcasing black-cherry fruit, earth and leather notes. It's firmly structured, with crisp acids as well, and should drink well for up to a decade or more.
title: E. Guigal 2013  Saint-Joseph

description: This contains a higher proportion of Roussanne than Nalys's regular white cuvée, and more barrel influence as well. Toast accents pineapple, melon and honey flavors, finishing clean and pleasant.
title: Domaine de Nalys 2014 Eicelènci White (Châteauneuf-du-Pape)

description: Despite Christophe Delorme's untimely passing before the 2015 harvest, this Tavel stands as a fine testament to his family's perseverance. It's full, round and rich, with cherry-berry fruit and hints of peach and crushed stone. Drink it over the rest of 2017.
title: Domaine de la Mordorée 2015 La Dame Rousse  (Tavel)

description: Despite Christophe Delorme's untimely passing before the 2015 harvest, this Tavel stands as a fine testament to his family's perseverance. It's full, round and rich, with cherry-berry fruit and hints of peach and crushed stone. Drink it over the rest of 2017.
title: Domaine de la Mordorée 2015 La Dame Rousse  (Tavel)

description: Full-bodied and richly textured, this isn't a prototypically delicate Côte Rôtie, but it's still very enjoyable. Clove and black olive notes are backed by plummy fruit, capped off by a long, dusty finish. Drink now–2025.
title: Jean-Luc Colombo 2012 La Divine  (Côte Rôtie)

description: Gérard Charvet took over Rosiers from his father in 1983 and remains focused on the art of vinification. A percentage (30%) of wood aging has give this ripe wine its dense texture. That contrasts with the generous black fruits that are still developing. This is a serious, dense wine that will age. Drink from 2018.
title: Georges Duboeuf 2015 Domaine des Rosiers  (Moulin-à-Vent)

description: A solid, structured cru wine with a fine line in tannins and black-cherry fruits. It is dense with a firm, dry core. Surrounding it are ripe fruits and acidity. A wine to keep a few more months, so drink from late 2017.
title: Domaine des Vieilles Caves 2015  Saint-Amour

description: Hugely black and darkly dense, this wine, which recalls the medieval practice of heating the must for concentration, is a massive construction. It has weight and dark tannins, serious black fruits and intense final acidity. Drink from 2017.
designation: Clos Triguedina The New Black Wine
title: Jean-Luc Baldès 2011 Clos Triguedina The New Black Wine Malbec (Cahors)

description: A heady and rich wine right from the start, this opens with seductive notes of brambly blackberry, wild raspberry, sweet spice, licorice and toast. It's full and weighty, with a texture like crushed velvet and a deep palate that continues to provide additional layers of flavor with each sip. Sweet spice, cocoa powder and mocha flavors linger on the evolving finish. Drink from 2017-2020. Monsieur Touton Selection Ltd, Dalbavie Selection LLC.
title: Domaine Thunevin-Calvet 2008 Hugo Red (Côtes du Roussillon Villages)

description: A heady and rich wine right from the start, this opens with seductive notes of brambly blackberry, wild raspberry, sweet spice, licorice and toast. It's full and weighty, with a texture like crushed velvet and a deep palate that continues to provide additional layers of flavor with each sip. Sweet spice, cocoa powder and mocha flavors linger on the evolving finish. Drink from 2017-2020. Monsieur Touton Selection Ltd, Dalbavie Selection LLC.
title: Domaine Thunevin-Calvet 2008 Hugo Red (Côtes du Roussillon Villages)

description: A very rich wine, spicy and complex. Dark fruits, rich tannins and layers of berries, exuding power and density. There is a sense of fine tannin as well, suspended in the texture of the wine. Firm and solid and with a great aging potential. Drink from 2019.
title: Château de Chambert 2010 Grand Vin Malbec (Cahors)

description: A very rich wine, spicy and complex. Dark fruits, rich tannins and layers of berries, exuding power and density. There is a sense of fine tannin as well, suspended in the texture of the wine. Firm and solid and with a great aging potential. Drink from 2019.
title: Château de Chambert 2010 Grand Vin Malbec (Cahors)

description: A solid and structured wine from this premier cru vineyard which is a Rodet monopoly. Dense and full in the mouth, the wine has delicious juicy fruits as well as powerful tannins and layers of acidity over the red fruit. Keep for 6–8 years.
title: Antonin Rodet 2010 Clos de Thorey Premier Cru  (Nuits-St.-Georges)

description: This is a stunning selection, with layers of aromas and flavors that unfold with each passing moment. Concentrated primary notes of blackberry, plum and boysenberry lead, with accents of sweet spice, licorice, soft char, tobacco leaf and menthol following shortly after. The palate is intense and lush, with a full weight and a gripping, thick texture. Hints of oaky spice and cocoa powder linger through the endless finish. Delicious now, but should continue to develop well through 2018.
title: Domaine du Clos des Fées 2008 Le Clos des Fées Red (Côtes du Roussillon Villages)

description: Because of such small harvests in 2013 because of hail, Alex Gambal decided to make one wine from all his premier cru parcels in Savigny-lès-Beaune. This wine is rich and ripe, full of sweet crushed strawberry flavors as well as a dry core of structure. Age this fine wine and drink from 2017.
title: Alex Gambal 2013 Premier Cru  (Savigny-lès-Beaune)

description: Because of such small harvests in 2013 because of hail, Alex Gambal decided to make one wine from all his premier cru parcels in Savigny-lès-Beaune. This wine is rich and ripe, full of sweet crushed strawberry flavors as well as a dry core of structure. Age this fine wine and drink from 2017.
title: Alex Gambal 2013 Premier Cru  (Savigny-lès-Beaune)

description: Tender notes of ripe, juicy pear with more golden inflections of ripe yellow plum and peach on nose and palate close into a central seam of bright, sprightly and immensely toning acidity. Lightness, concentration and lip-smacking freshness are framed by rounded fruit. Structure and grace signal ageing potential. The finish is wonderfully dry and full of verve.
title: Henri Schoenheitz 2013 Herrenreben Riesling (Alsace)

description: This is a concentrated, dark and brooding wine. Its complexity comes from the interplay of tannins and rich red fruits, laced with tight acidity. Serious and dense, it is a wine for long aging. Drink this impressive wine from 2019.
title: Jean-Luc and Paul Aegerter 2012  Corton Vergennes

description: This is a concentrated, dark and brooding wine. Its complexity comes from the interplay of tannins and rich red fruits, laced with tight acidity. Serious and dense, it is a wine for long aging. Drink this impressive wine from 2019.
title: Jean-Luc and Paul Aegerter 2012  Corton Vergennes

description: Smoky and aromatic, this wine shows great fruitiness against dark, structured tannins. Raspberries and black cherries are layered with wood, spice and final intense acidity. Drink this still-firm wine from 2018.
title: Domaine Méo-Camuzet 2013 Les Argillières Premier Cru  (Nuits-St.-Georges)

description: Smoky and aromatic, this wine shows great fruitiness against dark, structured tannins. Raspberries and black cherries are layered with wood, spice and final intense acidity. Drink this still-firm wine from 2018.
title: Domaine Méo-Camuzet 2013 Les Argillières Premier Cru  (Nuits-St.-Georges)

description: From the top range produced at the estate, this rich wine is kept refreshing by the acidity. Peach and pineapple fruits balance with a squeeze of lemon giving the wine a light touch. There is a tangy, orange zest accent in the crisp aftertaste.
title: Château Saint-Maur 2014 L´Excellence White (Côtes de Provence)

description: From the top range produced at the estate, this rich wine is kept refreshing by the acidity. Peach and pineapple fruits balance with a squeeze of lemon giving the wine a light touch. There is a tangy, orange zest accent in the crisp aftertaste.
title: Château Saint-Maur 2014 L´Excellence White (Côtes de Provence)

description: Named after the creation of the estate in 1610, this is a big, rich and extracted wine. The tough tannins need to soften further, with a powerful core of dryness. As it develops, the wine will reveal more of the rich red fruits and juicy final acidity that are there. Drink from 2017.
title: Château Grand Boise 2012 Cuvée 1610 Red (Côtes de Provence)

description: Named after the creation of the estate in 1610, this is a big, rich and extracted wine. The tough tannins need to soften further, with a powerful core of dryness. As it develops, the wine will reveal more of the rich red fruits and juicy final acidity that are there. Drink from 2017.
title: Château Grand Boise 2012 Cuvée 1610 Red (Côtes de Provence)

description: Fresh fruit with apple acidity gives this wine a ready-to-drink character. It has an attractive lift of citrus and a light, crisp and fresh aftertaste.
title: Christophe Cordier 2013 Vieilles Vignes  (Mâcon)

description: Fresh fruit with apple acidity gives this wine a ready-to-drink character. It has an attractive lift of citrus and a light, crisp and fresh aftertaste.
title: Christophe Cordier 2013 Vieilles Vignes  (Mâcon)

description: This medium-weight, slightly creamy rosé opens with soft aromas of white cherry, peach, cantaloupe and cranberry. The melony flavors continue through to the palate, while the finish offers an astringent citrus-pith flavor. Drink now.
title: Blanville 2014 Solal Rosé (Pays d'Oc)

description: Fresh and brightly crisp, this is a light and fruity wine. Full of acidity, juicy apples and with a lemon zest texture, it is ready to drink.
title: William Fèvre 2014  Petit Chablis

description: With grapes coming from the Mâcon region in southern Burgundy, this is ripe, fresh and roundly crisp. With attractive acidity and a sweetened lemon character, it's all fruit, ready to drink now.
title: Domaine Laroche 2014  Bourgogne

description: Made from Malbec, this lightly structured wine tastes rich while also fruity. Caramel flavors go over the red berry fruits and give a rounded, still fresh aftertaste.
title: Château Famaey 2013 Chevalier Famaey Rosé (Côtes du Lot)

description: This blend of 65% syrah, 30% Grenache and 5% Mourvèdre comes across as slightly confected in style, featuring bright, raspberry pastilles accented by herbal notes. It's bouncy and fresh, and resembles Beaujolais stylistically, including the faint tannic structure and crisp finish. Drink up.
title: Château de Campuget 2012 Tradition de Campuget Red (Costières de Nîmes)

description: This balanced, fruity wine has gentle tannins and juicy red fruit flavors. It's fresh with acidity and a floral character that makes it already drinkable.
title: Château Coutinel 2011 Red (Fronton)

description: Surprisingly austere for a Beaujolais-Villages, the wine has a firm, dry character that hides the natural fruitiness of the Gamay. Dense tannins and acidity give a cool feel to this stalky wine. It has red fruits, intense and tight acidity and a perfumed aftertaste. Drink now.
title: Louis Tête 2013 Les Combes  (Beaujolais-Villages)

description: The wine is soft and fruity with attractive red cherry favors and light acidity. It's smooth, round and ready to drink, with lively acidity and a touch of tannin on the finish.
title: Louis Tête 2013  Beaujolais-Villages

description: The wine is soft and fruity with attractive red cherry favors and light acidity. It's smooth, round and ready to drink, with lively acidity and a touch of tannin on the finish.
title: Louis Tête 2013  Beaujolais-Villages

description: Bright and fruity, this is a ready-to-drink wine. Fruitiness and lively acidity are balanced by the cherry juice flavors and a light structure to finish.
title: Domaine des Terres Dorées 2013 Le Buissy  (Beaujolais)

description: Bright and fruity, this is a ready-to-drink wine. Fruitiness and lively acidity are balanced by the cherry juice flavors and a light structure to finish.
title: Domaine des Terres Dorées 2013 Le Buissy  (Beaujolais)

description: With intense, mineral aromas, this is a complex, tight and nervy wine. It has great concentration, serious amounts of acidity and a final series of herbaceous flavors that give a totally dry, steely aftertaste. Age until 2015 to round it out.
title: Patient Cottat 2013 Anciennes Vignes  (Sancerre)

description: Very mineral and textured from the limestone soil, this is a concentrated and complex wine. It boasts considerable acidity and very crisp fruit, with grapefruit and juicy lemons coming through strongly. Age until at least 2016.
title: Vincent Vatan 2012 Sélection Silex  (Pouilly-Fumé)

description: Made from young vines from the Vaulorent portion of the Fourchaume vineyard, this is an open, rounded and lively wine with white fruits and weight, just lifted by acidity.
title: William Fèvre 2005 Fourchaume Premier Cru  (Chablis)

description: A rounded, fruity wine, packed with yellow peaches and apricots, but held in check by freshness, green herbs and a firm, steely character. It's not a wine to age for long, but it is delicious, and very seductive now.
title: Simonnet-Febvre 2005 Mont-de-Milieu Premier Cru  (Chablis)

description: A big, toasty wine, full of ripe, delicious fruit, veering toward opulence. There are open yellow fruits along with toast and butter tastes. This is almost ready to drink now; only the acidity promises some aging.
title: Pascal Bouchard 2006 Fourchaume Vieilles Vignes Premier Cru  (Chablis)

description: Closed up and firm with a hint of vanilla, honey and refined acidity. There is some crispness here, green apples and a plum skin character. This is going to be serious Chardonnay; the minerality already in evidence.
designation: Domaine Long-Depaquit Les Bougnons Premier Cru
title: Albert Bichot 2005 Domaine Long-Depaquit Les Bougnons Premier Cru  (Chablis)

description: There's a fine balance here between minerality and rich toast. The result is a very pure but ripe wine, dominated by a good mix of ripe white fruits and honey.
title: William Fèvre 2005 Montmains Premier Cru  (Chablis)

description: Rough around the edges, this is a dry and tannic wine. It has mint, red currant fruit and a dry center. It needs a year or two, but is likely to remain rustic.
title: Vieux Château Gaubert 2011 Benjamin de Vieux Château Gaubert  (Graves)

description: Tightly herbaceous and very crisp, grassy and citrusy, this is the epitome of cool, fresh Sauvignon Blanc. It's a light, bright, easy-drinking wine that's ready to go now.
title: Domaine Uby 2012 Sauvignon Blanc (Côtes de Gascogne)

description: There is just a touch of sweetness here, with apricot and nut flavors offering ripeness and a soft, full-in-the-mouth character. The wine has a light touch, and should be a delicious apéritif wine, or try it paired with Chinese food.
title: Domaine de l'Herré 2011 Gros Manseng (Côtes de Gascogne)

description: Smoky wine, rich as well as structured. The acidity of the year is integrated into the structure, the firm tannins and juicy red berry fruits a balanced pleasure to taste.
title: Richard Rottiers 2010  Moulin-à-Vent

description: Smoky wine, rich as well as structured. The acidity of the year is integrated into the structure, the firm tannins and juicy red berry fruits a balanced pleasure to taste.
title: Richard Rottiers 2010  Moulin-à-Vent

description: Griottes are a type of bitter cherry used in cooking, and this wine shares some of that character. It is firmly structured with acidity and an edge of attractive lightness. Age for 2–3 years.
title: Mommessin 2010 Les Griottes  (Morgon)

description: Griottes are a type of bitter cherry used in cooking, and this wine shares some of that character. It is firmly structured with acidity and an edge of attractive lightness. Age for 2–3 years.
title: Mommessin 2010 Les Griottes  (Morgon)

description: High acidity cuts through this wine from the get-go. The tannins also show a hard edge. This is a wine for the future, always with a sense of austerity and minerality.
title: Château Grand Maréchaud 2010  Blaye Côtes de Bordeaux

description: A fresh and fruity wine, with black currant notes, yet somewhat stalky in character. The aftertaste is bright and light.
title: Château Anniche 2010  Côtes de Bordeaux

description: Rich black fruits are supported by a dark structure and intensely juicy, youthful acidity. It is powerful, ripe and full of potential. Definitely young with its exuberant fruit, it is going to need serious aging. Drink this wine from 2020.
title: Roche de Bellene 2011  Echézeaux

description: With just a touch of bottle age giving a toasty character, this impressive wine is already showing some maturity. That said, the apple and citrus character, the mineral tight texture and crisp acidity promise some aging. The wine conveys a sense of elegance, intensity and richness. Drink now, but the wine will also age.
designation: Comtes de Champagne Blanc de Blancs Brut
title: Taittinger 2005 Comtes de Champagne Blanc de Blancs Brut Chardonnay (Champagne)

description: With just a touch of bottle age giving a toasty character, this impressive wine is already showing some maturity. That said, the apple and citrus character, the mineral tight texture and crisp acidity promise some aging. The wine conveys a sense of elegance, intensity and richness. Drink now, but the wine will also age.
designation: Comtes de Champagne Blanc de Blancs Brut
title: Taittinger 2005 Comtes de Champagne Blanc de Blancs Brut Chardonnay (Champagne)

description: This is a great vintage of Le Cèdre. With dark tannins and impressive structure, it is big and fruity while never overwhelming. Dense black fruits, bitter cherries and dark chocolate combine with mineral, juicy acidity. It's a wine to age for many years, don't drink before 2018.
title: Château du Cèdre 2010 Le Cèdre Malbec (Cahors)

description: This is a great vintage of Le Cèdre. With dark tannins and impressive structure, it is big and fruity while never overwhelming. Dense black fruits, bitter cherries and dark chocolate combine with mineral, juicy acidity. It's a wine to age for many years, don't drink before 2018.
title: Château du Cèdre 2010 Le Cèdre Malbec (Cahors)

description: Spice and mint dominate this intensely aromatic wine. Solid and very structured, it is still showing its wood aging and extraction. But its bright future is certain, with the weight of black fruits, the firm tannins and the mineral texture. Guard this wine and don't drink before 2020.
title: Roche de Bellene 2011  Clos de la Roche

description: This most powerful of Grand Cru vineyards has yielded another blockbuster. Even in the 2011 vintage, the wine is a massive statement, packed with rich fruits, dark tannins and layers of blackberry and juicy acidity. The wine has a dry texture, that will soften slowly over many years. Drink from 2019.
title: Roche de Bellene 2011  Chambertin

description: This wine has great power along with magnificently rich fruit. Wood aging provides a judicious support to its fullness and opulence. Acidity, black cherries and red berry fruits come together with firm tannins. Combined they are already in balance, but the wine needs to wait. Drink from 2018.
title: Roche de Bellene 2011  Bonnes-Mares

description: This extravagantly perfumed wine has great juicy, ripe fruits. The tannic structure is almost secondary in the welter of ripe fruits, but it is enough to promise aging. Acidity and rich fruitiness partner each other to give a wine that is both fresh and powerful. Drink from 2020.
title: Château Pétrus 2011  Pomerol

description: This extravagantly perfumed wine has great juicy, ripe fruits. The tannic structure is almost secondary in the welter of ripe fruits, but it is enough to promise aging. Acidity and rich fruitiness partner each other to give a wine that is both fresh and powerful. Drink from 2020.
title: Château Pétrus 2011  Pomerol

description: There's a subtle hint of toasted brioche to the ripe peach and baked apple core of this medium-bodied wine. Ample acidity keeps the palate fresh, while accents of citrus rind, peach pit and baking spice carry through to the close.
title: Arrogant Frog 2015 Lily Pad White Chardonnay (Pays d'Oc)

description: A subdued nose of earth leads to an off-dry palate with a core of ripe, yellow plums framed by pithy citrus. It is pith rather than freshness that defines this rounded wine.
title: Antoine Moltès & Fils 2015 Tradition Gewurztraminer (Alsace)

description: This estate-grown wine has a really fresh character. With red-currant and red-cherry flavors, it has a juicy fruity style that is ready to drink. Light and perfumed, it is delicious now.
title: Georges Duboeuf 2015 Château d'Ouilly  (Beaujolais)

description: This estate-grown wine has a really fresh character. With red-currant and red-cherry flavors, it has a juicy fruity style that is ready to drink. Light and perfumed, it is delicious now.
title: Georges Duboeuf 2015 Château d'Ouilly  (Beaujolais)

description: The subdued nose leads to a fresh, bright, easy-drinking palate dominated by lemony acidity. This is clean and refreshing. Drink soon.
title: Helfrich 2015 Riesling (Alsace)

description: Made from 100% grenache Gris, this soft rosé opens with scents of powder, sweet pea, white cherry, watermelon rind and Anjou pear. The light-weight palate is direct and easygoing, with subtle flavors of cherry and melon flesh that finish abruptly.
designation: Domaine le Pive Vie de Bohème
title: Vignobles Jeanjean 2015 Domaine le Pive Vie de Bohème Rosé (Sable de Camargue)

description: Made with organic grapes, this rosé is a blend of 30% Grenache Gris, 30% Grenache Noir, 30% Merlot and 10% Cabernet Franc. It's a dainty and floral selection, with forward scents of sweet pea, lavender, laurel and white tea. The palate offers some tart white cherry and currant fruitiness, with medium acidity and a subtle sweet-spice accent on the close.
title: Vignobles Jeanjean 2015 Domaine le Pive Gris Rosé (Sable de Camargue)

description: Made with organic grapes, this rosé is a blend of 30% Grenache Gris, 30% Grenache Noir, 30% Merlot and 10% Cabernet Franc. It's a dainty and floral selection, with forward scents of sweet pea, lavender, laurel and white tea. The palate offers some tart white cherry and currant fruitiness, with medium acidity and a subtle sweet-spice accent on the close.
title: Vignobles Jeanjean 2015 Domaine le Pive Gris Rosé (Sable de Camargue)

description: This wine, bottled with minimum sulfur, is ripe with concentration and firm tannins. It is fruity although there is also a bitter edge to the ripe cherry flavors. The wine is ready to drink.
title: Vignerons de Bel Air 2015 Natural  (Beaujolais-Villages)

description: Firmly structured, this is a rich wine in a style that is rounded and ripe. It has light tannins and spicy acidity to balance the general richness of the wine. Drink now.
title: Patriarche Père et Fils 2015  Beaujolais-Villages

description: Very perfumed in style, this is classic Gewurztraminer. It is full of candy shop flavors and slightly blowsy. It doesn't take itself too seriously, and it's ready to drink now.
title: Hubert Meyer 2011 Gewurztraminer (Alsace)

description: Light gold in color, this rose scented wine has a touch of honey and some richness. There is dryness as well, bringing out walnuts and an edge of bitterness. This is wine to drink now.
title: Wunsch & Mann 2008 Hengst Grand Cru Gewurztraminer (Alsace)

description: This is a wine that is lightly touched with a mineral texture while also having rich layers of acidity and green herbs. It is fragrant, perfumed and, on the finish, deliciously light and fruity.
title: Sipp Mack 2011 Tradition Riesling (Alsace)

description: Pushing in the direction of freshness and herbaceousness, this is a tight, textured wine. The wine's grapefruit and lime flavors are balanced by touches of wood and spice. The final feel is soft, yet brisk.
title: Château Olivier 2010  Pessac-Léognan

description: Smooth and rich, this is an opulent wine. It has ripe acidity and tropical fruit notes, while also crisp at the edges, like biting into a ripe pear. The wine, with its structured core, has good aging potential.
title: Château de Fieuzal 2010  Pessac-Léognan

description: From a small north-east facing vineyard in the Vallée de la Marne, this ripe, soft, generous wine also has great intensity. It is full and concentrated, with pear and apple fruits allied to touches of bitter almonds, wood and fruit. It's a vintage that could age, although it is just right to drink now.
title: Tarlant 2003 La Vigne d'Or Extra Brut Pinot Meunier (Champagne)

description: A rich, chocolaty wine, with the structure right up front. Under the same ownership as Château Montrose, this is a wine that reveals all its attractions early with sweet blackberry fruit and powerful tannins. There is some freshness as well, giving fruitiness and acidity at the end.
title: Château Tronquoy-Lalande 2010  Saint-Estèphe

description: Continuing the great improvements at this estate, this 2010 is firm and solidly tannic, showing severity. As a contrast, it also shows acidity and black currant fruits that offer weight and richness. A balanced wine with a good future.
title: Château Olivier 2010  Pessac-Léognan

description: This plump, medium-bodied blend of Grenache blanc, Roussanne, Viognier, Clairette and Bourboulenc features notes reminiscent of ginger, nectarine and melon, then finishes with fresh, zesty citrus. Drink it through mid-2018.
title: M. Chapoutier 2016 Belleruche White (Côtes du Rhône)

description: This blend of 60% Syrah, 30% Grenache and 10% Carignan is bright and fruit-driven, with rich notes of plum, cherry and boysenberry on the nose and mouth. It's medium in weight, with accessible tannins and good balance, finishing fresh and fruity, with just a subtle hint of earthy spice.
title: Calmel & Joseph 2014 Les Terroirs Red (Saint-Chinian)

description: This blend of 60% Syrah, 30% Grenache and 10% Carignan is bright and fruit-driven, with rich notes of plum, cherry and boysenberry on the nose and mouth. It's medium in weight, with accessible tannins and good balance, finishing fresh and fruity, with just a subtle hint of earthy spice.
title: Calmel & Joseph 2014 Les Terroirs Red (Saint-Chinian)

description: This pale copper rosé is made from 30% Grenache Gris, 30% Grenache Noir, 30% Merlot and 10% Cabernet Franc. It leads with extremely soft scents of peach skin and strawberry hull that continue through to the medium-weight palate with more intensity. Ample orangy acidity lends freshness to the palate and lift to the finish.
title: Vignobles Jeanjean 2016 Domaine Le Pive Gris Rosé (Sable de Camargue)

description: This succulent, medium-bodied rosé is a blend of Grenache and Carignan. Cherries, berries and ripe peach are fruity and direct, but finish dry and satisfying. Drink now.
title: Domaine du Père Caboche 2016 Rosé (Vin de Pays de Vaucluse)

description: This 65% Merlot wine is ripe, fruity and soft. Coming from a light vintage, it is ready to drink with its blackberry fruits and supporting tannins.
title: Château Vieux Cardinal Lafaurie 2013  Lalande de Pomerol

description: Red-berry fruits and a core of tannins make up a wine that has structure and the potential of some fine fruits. It is juicy with plenty of acidity at the end to give the wine a lift.
title: Château Toudenac 2015  Bordeaux Supérieur

description: The wine is structured and firm with considerable wood flavors. It also has the fruit weight that will develop as the wine matures. Give this wine, with its potential, until 2019.
title: Château Roques Mauriac 2015 Grand Vin  (Bordeaux Supérieur)

description: The wine is structured and firm with considerable wood flavors. It also has the fruit weight that will develop as the wine matures. Give this wine, with its potential, until 2019.
title: Château Roques Mauriac 2015 Grand Vin  (Bordeaux Supérieur)

description: This producer, based in the eastern edge of Saint-Emilion, has these vines in the flat plain that leads to the Dordogne river. The wine has richness that comes from the vintage while also having structure and power. The juicy acidity and blackberry fruits are still developing, so drink from 2019.
title: Château Robin des Moines 2010  Saint-Émilion

description: Closed and tight, this wine is full of tangy acidity, giving it an almost too-fresh character lifted by spice and a mineral aftertaste.
title: Seguin-Manuel 2014  Mâcon-Villages

description: At the moment, this is a tight, young wine with fruit that is masked. There is some potential that will give a wine with apple flavors. Wait to drink this until 2017.
title: Georges Duboeuf 2014  Saint-Véran

description: Aromas of yellow melon and flowers form the core of the bouquet, with additional hints of straw and grapefruit peel in the background. The light-weight palate offers good balance, with rich tropical-fruit tones of pineapple and mango that finish clean and mouthwatering.
title: Louis de Camponac 2015 White (Vin de France)

description: This lush wine leads with rich aromas of vanilla-infused blackberry, raspberry preserves and plum sauce. The medium-weight palate is plush and velvety in texture, with supple blackberry and plum flavors that carry through to the medium-length finish.
title: Kiwi Cuvée 2015 Bin 168 Malbec (Vin de France)

description: This open, fruity wine is ready to drink. It offers some spice as well as a light smattering of apple and toast flavors. The aftertaste is all about fruit and acidity.
title: Château de Beauregard 2014  Saint-Véran

description: This open, fruity wine is ready to drink. It offers some spice as well as a light smattering of apple and toast flavors. The aftertaste is all about fruit and acidity.
title: Château de Beauregard 2014  Saint-Véran

description: For a Listrac, this is soft and open, a generous wine that has weight while showing ripe Merlot character. Full black plum skin flavors go with spice, licorice and touches of wood. It's ready to drink now.
title: Grands Terroirs de France 2010  Listrac-Médoc

description: For a Listrac, this is soft and open, a generous wine that has weight while showing ripe Merlot character. Full black plum skin flavors go with spice, licorice and touches of wood. It's ready to drink now.
title: Grands Terroirs de France 2010  Listrac-Médoc

description: Varois is a small enclave surrounded by Côtes de Provence vineyards. This wine, with its softness, touches of vanilla as well as the proper rich red fruits, is a gentle rosé, easy and ready to drink.
title: Gassier 2012 Abbaye Saint-Hilaire Rosé (Coteaux Varois en Provence)

description: Varois is a small enclave surrounded by Côtes de Provence vineyards. This wine, with its softness, touches of vanilla as well as the proper rich red fruits, is a gentle rosé, easy and ready to drink.
title: Gassier 2012 Abbaye Saint-Hilaire Rosé (Coteaux Varois en Provence)

description: A fruity, strawberry flavored wine with some depth and structure. It has richness as well as a fresh citrus character. It could benefit from some aging although it's certainly ready to drink this summer.
title: Château Saint-Pierre 2012 Tradition Rosé (Côtes de Provence)

description: Full wine, soft on the palate, its berry fruits ripe and forward. It has some weight although the acidity is as fresh as it can be. The aftertaste  is clean, clear refreshing. Screwcap.
title: Château Routas 2012 Rosé (Coteaux Varois en Provence)

description: A bright, herbaceous and fresh wine, showing green fruits, lively acidity and and a steely edge that adds a fine texture.
title: Château Rousset-Caillau 2011  Entre-Deux-Mers

description: Château Magnol, owned by negociant Barton & Guestier, has produced a 2011 that is wood-laden at this stage. It boasts tannins, a tight line in black currant fruit, and a dry core of wood. This needs at least three years to round out and soften.
title: Château Magnol 2011  Haut-Médoc

description: A green, herbal wine, very crisp, still young with acidity, mineral acidity and a bright, lively aftertaste. The wine is tangy with citrus at the end. Keep for six months to a year. Screwcap.
title: Château de Beauregard-Ducourt 2012  Entre-Deux-Mers

description: A green, herbal wine, very crisp, still young with acidity, mineral acidity and a bright, lively aftertaste. The wine is tangy with citrus at the end. Keep for six months to a year. Screwcap.
title: Château de Beauregard-Ducourt 2012  Entre-Deux-Mers

description: Crisp, lightly herbaceous wine with a delicious creamy apple and pear character. This is finely balanced with a lively, crisp aftertaste. Screwcap.
title: Château Briot 2012  Bordeaux Blanc

description: There is obvious wood here, a toasty, dry character that shows through the fruit. The wine is young and with the sufficient weight of juicy black currant fruit, it should integrate well to give a solid, chunky wine in two years.
title: Château Bois Pertuis 2011  Bordeaux

description: Made by the Abeille family of Château Mont-Redon in Châteauneuf-du-Pape, this striking, peppery, spicy wine is rich with a fine texture as well as plenty of red berry fruits. It is a concentrated wine, very dry and likely to be much better with food.
title: Château Riotor 2015 Rosé (Côtes du Rhône)

description: This will turn into a smooth, ripe wine as it ages. It already has concentration and power as well as generous rich Merlot fruits. Dark berries and firm tannins are balanced and shot through with acidity. Keep this wine at least until 2020
title: Château Bourseau 2012 La Croix de Bourseau  (Lalande de Pomerol)

description: Still firm with tannins, this is also a rich, generous wine. It has mint aromas that follow through on to the palate with wood-aging flavors. Bold blackberry fruit and juicy acidity balance the structure and give the wine a ripe character. The wine will be ready to drink from 2018.
title: Château Bel-Air Ortet 2012  Saint-Estèphe

description: Produced from a selection of 80-year-old vines, this is a dense, smooth wine. It has a dry core although this is surrounded by such rich fruit and spice. The wine is now almost mature, ripe and full with a great shot of final acidity.
title: Château Beauséjour 2009  Puisseguin Saint-Émilion

description: This is a strong showing for Nalys, surprisingly full-bodied and creamy-textured for the estate. Hints of wood char and roasted meat mark the nose, while the flavors of mocha and brown sugar carry through the plush, velvety finish. Drink now–2023.
title: Domaine de Nalys 2013 Red (Châteauneuf-du-Pape)

description: From one of those rare properties in Pauillac that are not classified growths, this wine is ripe, dark, still smoky and very structured. It has some of the weight of the vintage although in a restrained way, giving juicy black currant fruits behind the tannic structure. Drink from 2017.
title: Château Gaudin 2010  Pauillac

description: Crisp and lively, this is a tight and mineral wine. Baked-apple fruitiness is balanced by bright acidity and a tangy aftertaste. Drink from 2018.
title: Domaine des Deux Roches 2015 Tradition  (Saint-Véran)

description: Crisp and lively, this is a tight and mineral wine. Baked-apple fruitiness is balanced by bright acidity and a tangy aftertaste. Drink from 2018.
title: Domaine des Deux Roches 2015 Tradition  (Saint-Véran)

description: This is a herbal wine, crisp and with a lively gooseberry and spice character. It is full of acidity that lifts the fruitiness and gives it a mineral texture. Drink the wine now.
title: Château du Carrubier 2016 White (Côtes de Provence)

description: This crisp, citrus-flavored wine has bright acidity and a touch of vanilla. It has great fruitiness, dominated by lemon with the tang of orange zest. It is ready to drink.
title: Château de Pizay 2016  Bourgogne

description: This crisp, citrus-flavored wine has bright acidity and a touch of vanilla. It has great fruitiness, dominated by lemon with the tang of orange zest. It is ready to drink.
title: Château de Pizay 2016  Bourgogne

description: Apple aromas give this wine a lift even before it has begun. The crispness and the delicious acidity are refreshing, bringing out minerality and brightness. Drink from 2018.
title: Cave des Grands Crus Blancs 2016 Floréal  (Mâcon Chaintré)

description: There are pretty white-flower aromas that grace the bouquet of this wine, with a supporting core of pink apple, peach and ripe honeydew. Despite its light weight, there's a pleasant roundness to the midpalate, with lasting fruit impressions on the close.
title: Calmel & Joseph 2016 Villa Blanche Chardonnay (Pays d'Oc)

description: There are pretty white-flower aromas that grace the bouquet of this wine, with a supporting core of pink apple, peach and ripe honeydew. Despite its light weight, there's a pleasant roundness to the midpalate, with lasting fruit impressions on the close.
title: Calmel & Joseph 2016 Villa Blanche Chardonnay (Pays d'Oc)

description: There's a slight mealy presence to this wine, with warm aromas of muddled plum and cherry. Hints of black tea and plum skin lend some texture and astringency to the palate, coupled with soft tannins and an overall light, approachable character. Drink now.
title: Lorgeril 2016 Château de Pennautier Syrah-Viognier (Pays d'Oc)

description: This wine is bright and fruity at first, with ripe and juicy black-fruit tones that dominate the nose. Hints of banana cream and vanilla sauce lend an overwhelming richness to the plush, medium-weight palate, finishing with loads of sweet spice.
title: Lorgeril 2016 1620 Cabernet Franc (Pays d'Oc)

description: This is a soft wine, ripe with apricot and melon flavors. It shows the warmth of the vintage, round and gently fruity. Almonds and a tangy aftertaste give a crisp finish.
title: L. Tramier & Fils 2015 Laurent Dufouleur Cuvée Eléonore  (Bourgogne)

description: There is an attractive orange-zest tang to this rounded wine. It brings out ripe yellow fruits that have acidity to add to the mineral texture of this balanced wine. It is ready to drink.
title: L. Tramier & Fils 2015 Collection  (Saint-Véran)

description: There is an attractive orange-zest tang to this rounded wine. It brings out ripe yellow fruits that have acidity to add to the mineral texture of this balanced wine. It is ready to drink.
title: L. Tramier & Fils 2015 Collection  (Saint-Véran)

description: Almonds and a strongly yeasty element are the main characters of this sparkling wine. It's full, but the fruit still has a texture to it, leaving good acidity to finish. Good value, enjoyable wine.
title: Marquis de la Tour NV Brut White (Vin Mousseux)

description: Superripe Grenache gives this fortified dessert wine (16% alcohol) distinctly chocolaty overtones, but there's also an overripe note of prunes. Despite that, it doesn't pack the alcoholic punch or massive weight of Port, making it relatively easy to drink, with an affinity for chocolate desserts.
title: Les Clos de Paulilles 2005 Rimage  (Banyuls)

description: Superripe Grenache gives this fortified dessert wine (16% alcohol) distinctly chocolaty overtones, but there's also an overripe note of prunes. Despite that, it doesn't pack the alcoholic punch or massive weight of Port, making it relatively easy to drink, with an affinity for chocolate desserts.
title: Les Clos de Paulilles 2005 Rimage  (Banyuls)

description: Under the ownership of American Stephen Adams, this estate is showing promise. The wine is finely structured, a smoky bacon element mingling well with fresh red plum and firm tannins. The core is dry, solid, showing wood, finishing with vivid minerality and acidity.
title: Château Lagarosse 2006  Premieres Côtes de Bordeaux

description: A firm, dark and concentrated wine that boasts big tannins, dark fruit and a seriously dry element. Powerful and extracted, it needs time to soften and show its more fruity side.
title: Château la Grande Maye 2010  Castillon Côtes de Bordeaux

description: Quite pale, this blend of Cabernet Sauvignon and Merlot is soft, fruity and ready to drink. Attractive red fruits and light acidity give a tangy, fresh aftertaste.
title: Château Bélingard 2014 Bélingard  (Bergerac Rosé)

description: This wine is soft, creamy and light. Attractive acidity along with a fresh apple character gives a fresh aftertaste. Drink now. This is one of the first vintages since Labouré-Roi, which was hit by scandal in 2012, passed into new ownership.
title: Labouré-Roi 2014  Mâcon-Villages

description: There are hints of bottle age on this strawberry-flavored wine. They give it a more woody, toasty character that takes away from the freshness that a wine like this needs. The aftertaste conveys caramel and spice.
title: Domaine des Baumard NV Extra Brut Rosé Sparkling (Crémant de Loire)

description: While this wine is packed with red-berry flavors, it is still too young with its stalky edge. Tannins and smoky flavors are there along with intense acidity. Keep it until late 2016 for it to be at its best.
title: Château Laulerie 2014 Merlot (Bergerac)

description: A soft wine, full of cherry preserve flavors, along with a bright, fresh waft of acidity. It is just spoilt by the banana flavor from the vinification.
title: Signé Vigneron 2008 Le Chat Rouge  (Beaujolais)

description: An intensely spiced, aromatic wine, packed with classic lychee fruits and offering good concentration. The wine is rich, weighty and just hinting at acidity. Full-bodied and young, it could age 1–2 years.
title: René Sparr 2011 Excellence Gewurztraminer (Alsace)

description: An intensely spiced, aromatic wine, packed with classic lychee fruits and offering good concentration. The wine is rich, weighty and just hinting at acidity. Full-bodied and young, it could age 1–2 years.
title: René Sparr 2011 Excellence Gewurztraminer (Alsace)

description: A very herbaceous, aromatic wine. The acidity cuts through the grapefruit flavor, giving a touch of minerality at the end.
title: Domaine des Levrys 2012  Sancerre

description: A wine that is dominated by minerality, tannins and acidity. It contains some severe characteristics yet is leaner than some others in Saint-Emilion. Still, there is aging potential.
title: Château Beausejour-Duffau-Lagarrosse 2008  Saint-Émilion

description: A wine that is dominated by minerality, tannins and acidity. It contains some severe characteristics yet is leaner than some others in Saint-Emilion. Still, there is aging potential.
title: Château Beausejour-Duffau-Lagarrosse 2008  Saint-Émilion

description: Dark-colored wine, with smoky, bitter chocolate flavors: cocoa plus spice and jammy black plums. It's powerful, densely textured, finishing with good acidity.
title: Château Clinet 2008  Pomerol

description: Complex and structured, this has rich tannins and a strawberry jam flavor from the ripe fruit. With its fine balance between the dry core and the fruity exterior, this should be cellared for at least four years.
title: Vincent Sauvestre 2010 Les Maréchaudes Premier Cru  (Aloxe-Corton)

description: This is a big, wood-laden smoky wine, with notes of spice and enticing toast to go with the firm tannins. At the same time, the fruit is vying to show its rich red-plum character. Give this 4–5 years to begin to show its best.
title: Vincent Prunier 2010 Les Chaponnières Premier Cru  (Pommard)

description: The tannins are already finely integrated into the rich, ripe fruit. It has a smoky character along with a note of wood spice, and the black plum fruit serves as a juicy underlay. Given its weight and structure, this should for age five years at least.
title: Jean-Claude Boisset 2009 Les Chardannes  (Chambolle-Musigny)

description: This is a very mineral driven wine—the ripe fruit is cut with acidity, green fruits and herbs. Textured and ripe, its freshness is a counterpoint to the full fruit flavors.
title: Domaine Vincent Girardin 2010 Les Chaumes Premier Cru  (Chassagne-Montrachet)

description: While this is currently firm and closed, it promises fine things to come. Weight and richness combine with a solid core of tannins. The intense, refreshing acidity is a counterpoint to the ripe black-plum flavor. With all of this concentration, this should age for over 5–6 years.
title: Domaine Heresztyn 2010 Les Champonnets Premier Cru  (Gevrey-Chambertin)

description: Round and rich, this has streaks of lemon and orange zest that cut through the vanilla and creamed apple texture. A note of spice makes the wine complex and rich. This is worth aging for several years.
title: Château de Maligny 2010 Fourchaume Premier Cru  (Chablis)

description: Round and rich, this has streaks of lemon and orange zest that cut through the vanilla and creamed apple texture. A note of spice makes the wine complex and rich. This is worth aging for several years.
title: Château de Maligny 2010 Fourchaume Premier Cru  (Chablis)

description: There is a touch of wood here, partnering with the wine's weight, minerality and crisp character. White fruit flavors of apple and pear lend further brightness.
title: Joseph Drouhin 2010  Meursault

description: Concentrated and rich, with some wood influence, this has ripe yellow fruits that are balanced with an intense streak of acidity, lending a sense of tension. It's very full, round and already a delight to drink.
title: Jean-Claude Boisset 2009 En Remilly Premier Cru  (Saint-Aubin)

description: With its intense red fruits and acidity, this initially seems so fruity. Slowly the powerful structure comes into play, yielding a concentrated, cellar-worthy wine.
designation: Domaine des Perdrix Aux Perdrix Premier Cru
title: Domaines Devillard 2010 Domaine des Perdrix Aux Perdrix Premier Cru  (Nuits-St.-Georges)

description: With its straw color and wood aging aromas, this is rich, bearing yellow peach and pear fruits, along with a toast note and juicy acidity. It's already impressive but should drink well for another three years at least.
title: Domaines Devillard 2010 Château de Chamirey  (Mercurey)

description: With its straw color and wood aging aromas, this is rich, bearing yellow peach and pear fruits, along with a toast note and juicy acidity. It's already impressive but should drink well for another three years at least.
title: Domaines Devillard 2010 Château de Chamirey  (Mercurey)

description: A typical medium-bodied Côtes du Rhône, the 2007 Bastide de Beauvert features aromas of cherry, clove and sweaty leather, and flavors that run along similar lines. Mature; drink now.
title: Les Vignobles Foncalieu 2007 Bastide de Beauvert Red (Côtes du Rhône)

description: A medium-sweet, spicy wine that offers good fresh guava flavor to balance the ripe texture. The finish is fresh. Screw cap.
title: Domaine Zinck 2008 Gewürztraminer (Alsace)

description: Simple but charming, with uncomplicated black fruit upfront followed by cherry and garrigue in the mouth, this is a good choice for a Labor Day barbecue; the fresh acidity and soft tannins put us in mind of something in the pork or veal family.
title: Domaine Saint Andrieu 2007 Red (Coteaux Varois)

description: Opens with a classic nose of cream, citrus and spice, giving way to cotton candy, cardamon and café latte in the mouth. The crisp, dry finish of roasted nuts is attractive but doesn't really linger.
title: Jean-Baptiste Adam 2007 Kaefferkopf Vielles Vignes Grand Cru Riesling (Alsace)

description: Classic spice and lychee aromas lead to a wine that is medium sweet, attractive but one-dimensional. It has perfumed, candy shop flavors, almost exaggerated. Screwcap.
title: Helfrich 2009 Gewürztraminer (Alsace)

description: Light, soft and fresh, an easy-drinking Pinot Blanc, with pear and fresh apricot flavors. A great apéritif style, ready to drink. Screwcap.
title: Cave de Beblenheim 2009 Baron de Hoen Pinot Blanc (Alsace)

description: Colombo is based in the northern Rhône, but ventured down to the south to make this wine, a blend of 45% Syrah, 35% Grenache and 20% Mourvèdre. Leather, dark-skinned plums and mocha mark the palate, which is firmly tannic yet without much hidden richness. Drink it with rare meats over the short term.
title: Jean-Luc Colombo 2014 Les Bartavelles Red (Châteauneuf-du-Pape)

description: In its antique bottle, this wine (one of a limited series) is laden with more wood than fruit. It will certainly soften, allowing the black fruits to come through, but this amount of wood will be hard to balance out. Drink from 2020.
title: Belliard Vins Selections 2014 Excellence de Belliard  (Pomerol)

description: This medium-bodied wine takes all the elements you might find in a tack room—liniment, bandages, sweaty leather—and adds red cherry fruit and a silky texture. It's interesting, complex and enjoyable, ready to drink now through 2020.
title: Ogier 2014 Héritages Red (Châteauneuf-du-Pape)

description: Behind the main slope of the Côte de Beaune, Saint-Romain produces some delicious white wines that have extra freshness. This wine, all fruit and light mineral texture, offers apricot and peach flavors that are cut with acidity. The aftertaste adds a more mineral element. Drink from 2016.
title: Alex Gambal 2013  Saint-Romain

description: Behind the main slope of the Côte de Beaune, Saint-Romain produces some delicious white wines that have extra freshness. This wine, all fruit and light mineral texture, offers apricot and peach flavors that are cut with acidity. The aftertaste adds a more mineral element. Drink from 2016.
title: Alex Gambal 2013  Saint-Romain

description: From vines at least 30 and up to 90 years old, this is the top of the Chablis range from La Chablisienne. Lightly wooded to bring out extra richness from the fruit, the wine has vanilla and honey as well as creamed apple and apricot fruits. The aftertaste is aromatic and fresh. Drink now.
title: La Chablisienne 2013 Les Vénérables  (Chablis)

description: A rich wine laden with juicy blackberry fruits and wood tannins, lapping up the ripe vintage. Soft and ready to drink.
title: Domaines Lapalu 2009 La Patache  (Médoc)

description: A rich wine laden with juicy blackberry fruits and wood tannins, lapping up the ripe vintage. Soft and ready to drink.
title: Domaines Lapalu 2009 La Patache  (Médoc)

description: There's a strong floral edge to this wine, with assertive aromas of peony and carnation dominating the rich and jammy cherry and strawberry fruit center. Lightweight with low tannins, it's an easy drink with good balance and versatility.
title: Domaine Sainte-Eugénie 2009 La Réserve Red (Corbières)

description: Although it does have attractive structure with some dry tannins, the wine is ready to drink. Its attractive berry fruits are layered with acidity and a touch of coffee. Balanced and fresh.
title: Château Tour d'Auron 2009  Bordeaux Supérieur

description: A red fruit flavored wine, light and packed with acidity. The wine may not have the richness of the vintage, but it does have a fine line in red cherry flavors. Drink now.
title: Louis Chevallier 2009  Beaujolais-Villages

description: This is a very new-wood dominated wine, that will appeal to lovers of California Cabernet. Blackcurrant jelly fruits are there as well, very modern, very polished. It is a fine wine, but maybe not Bordeaux.
title: Château Talbot 2000  Saint-Julien

description: Under new ownership, Prieuré-Lichine continues its rapid quality improvement. The wine is concentrated, with dark tannins and brooding fruit, dominated by new wood. It is rich, but also structured for a steady development over 10-15 years.
title: Château Prieuré-Lichine 2000  Margaux

description: The wine is rich and ripe, revealing purity of fruit as well as prominent new wood flavors. Otto Rettenmaier, whose cellar is full of wooden cuves named after opera stars, now operates in a biodynamic way and that seems to give an intensity of flavor as well as lusciousness and opulence. Drink from 2010.
title: Château La Tour Figeac 2000  Saint-Émilion

description: A hugely concentrated wine showing chewy, but ripe tannins. Smooth, polished fruit combines with well-balanced wood and suppressed power. This is certainly a wine that will develop well, making it drinkable in five years and mature in 10-15 years.
title: Château Cantenac Brown 2000  Margaux

description: A modern, smooth wine, with polished fruit and a dark purple color. The wine is full of new wood, but still dominated by liquorice and dark chocolate flavors. It should develop relatively quickly, over the next 10 years.
title: Château Grand Mayne 2000  Saint-Émilion

description: There is a sense of pent-up energy with this wine. It has powerful fruit along with flavors of chocolate, but it is all masked and repressed by tight firm tannins. A wine that will develop slowly.
title: Château Malartic-Lagravière 2000 Pessac-Léognan  (Bordeaux)

description: Under any new classification, this should certainly be a classed growth. Today it is among the leaders of the crus bourgeois. The 2000 is opulent, generous, stylish. The tannins are ripe and sweet, the fruit is finely balanced. It will develop well over the next 10-15 years.
title: Château Chasse-Spleen 2000  Moulis

description: Under any new classification, this should certainly be a classed growth. Today it is among the leaders of the crus bourgeois. The 2000 is opulent, generous, stylish. The tannins are ripe and sweet, the fruit is finely balanced. It will develop well over the next 10-15 years.
title: Château Chasse-Spleen 2000  Moulis

description: This is a big, powerful, firm wine, with a top layer of ripe, glamorous fruit flavors. Blackcurrant jelly fruits are shot through with ripe acidity and soft tannins. It should develop relatively fast, but then last well.
title: Château Giscours 2000  Margaux

description: This is initially a somewhat austere wine, but that derives from the tannins of Saint-Estèphe. Underneath those tannins are solid, chunky fruits and a great generosity and richness.
title: Château Phélan-Ségur 2000  Saint-Estèphe

description: The Becots, Gérard and Dominique, have produced a stylish, modern wine that powers black, sweet fruits through the deceptively soft tannins. Tarry flavors and layers of new wood give the wine a new world character. How long it will last is open to question at this stage. It is certainly developing quickly.
title: Château Beau-Séjour Bécot 2000  Saint-Émilion

description: This is a powerful statement of ripe Cabernet Sauvignon. It has rich concentrated fruit, with ripe but dry tannins and considerable wood flavors. It is stylish, with layers of acidity and wood complementing the fruit.
title: Château Pichon Longueville 2000  Pauillac

description: For the vintage, this is an austere style of wine, emphasising tannins over fruit. The fruit is certainly rich, and the tannins are dusty rather than dry, but it is a wine which is developing more slowly, suggesting it is also a wine for long-term aging.
title: Château Haut-Bailly 2000 Pessac-Léognan  (Bordeaux)

description: For the vintage, this is an austere style of wine, emphasising tannins over fruit. The fruit is certainly rich, and the tannins are dusty rather than dry, but it is a wine which is developing more slowly, suggesting it is also a wine for long-term aging.
title: Château Haut-Bailly 2000 Pessac-Léognan  (Bordeaux)

description: Dusty and nuanced with soft aromas of cocoa, dried raspberry and cherry, reminiscent of a chocolate cherry latte from Starbucks. Light weight in the mouth with approachable tannins and a clean, dry finish. Drink now.
title: Château Comte Devaugelas 2007 Red (Minervois)

description: Medium intense notes of sweet grass, fresh red apple slices, green melon and lime citrus on the nose and mouth. Medium weight with moderate, supporting acidity and a clean finish. Drink now.
title: Château Cabezac 2009 Alice Blanc White (Minervois)

description: Starting with green acidity, this wine opens up well to give cool lemon and mineral flavors. These are followed by a creamy texture that softens the acidity, giving a ripe, full finish.
title: Maison Champy 2006  St.-Romain

description: Definitely on the dry side, showing the tannic face of Pinot Noir. This is a serious wine that reflects its status as a premier cru, a powerful mix of cranberry fruits and dark tannins, but marked by a hot, hard aftertaste.
title: Louis Latour 2005 Les Chaillots Premier Cru  (Aloxe-Corton)

description: Muscat's typical sweetness and delicacy give this an attractive balance of crisp acidity and ripe raspberry flavor. It's light, lively and intensely fruity.
title: Royal Muscato NV Pink Sparkling (Vin Mousseux)

description: Minty aromas go along with firm, barely bitter tannins. They dominate the wine, smothering the fruit and lending a burnt quality to the palate.
title: Château Bréhat 2010  Castillon Côtes de Bordeaux

description: A softly juicy wine, this is missing structure while it has plenty of fruit. It's ripe, rich and juicy; a pleasure to drink in 2–3 years.
title: Château Langrange Monbadon 2010  Castillon Côtes de Bordeaux

description: A strongly wood-aged wine, very dark and brooding. It has high extract and concentration, with a flash of black pepper on the palate. Tough and finishing hard.
title: Château Ampélia 2010  Castillon Côtes de Bordeaux

description: This is a fruity, ready-to-drink wine, with acidity cutting through the juicy black currant fruits. This is attractive and bright, yet structured.
title: Château Acker-Perreau 2010  Bordeaux

description: Based in Epernay, this Champagne house specializes in bone-dry Champagnes. Like this bottling, they need some time before the acidity calms down. This has the potential to be delicious, crisp, and full of a bright mineral texture and citrus fruitiness. Drink from 2018.
title: Lombard et Cie NV Extra Brut Premier Cru  (Champagne)

description: The merest hint of red currant plays on the subtle nose. The tender red-currant fruit is enhanced by the very lively frothy mousse that fizzes away on the palate. This is light, fruit-driven, refreshing and easy—ideal as an enlivening apéritif.
title: Joseph Cattin NV Brut Rosé Sparkling (Crémant d'Alsace)

description: As is often the case when a rosé has been made taking the color from the skins rather than the more usual addition of red wine, this perfumed Champagne is dark colored—very pink. The fruit of this dry wine gives a red-currant flavor, with lively acidity and a crisp, tang aftertaste.
designation: Rosé de Saignée Premier Cru Brut
title: Bertrand-Delespierre NV Rosé de Saignée Premier Cru Brut  (Champagne)
