title: Faniel et Fils NV Oriane Brut  (Champagne)

description: Aromas of green apples bring a fresh burst of acidity. The wine is bright, with a firm texture of lime zest and red apple skins.
region: Vin de Pays des Côtes de Gascogne
title: Domaine de Mirail 2008 Colombard Colombard (Vin de Pays des Côtes de Gascogne)

description: Aromas of green apples bring a fresh burst of acidity. The wine is bright, with a firm texture of lime zest and red apple skins.
region: Vin de Pays des Côtes de Gascogne
title: Domaine de Mirail 2008 Colombard Colombard (Vin de Pays des Côtes de Gascogne)

description: The bottling from the Delorme family is a fruit bomb in the best sense. It's not unnuanced, just offers masses of black cherries and plums that pick up hints of chocolate on the finish. Drink now–2020.
title: Domaine de la Mordorée 2014 La Dame Rousse Red (Lirac)

description: This is a full-bodied yet succulent, supple wine, loaded with dark fruit. Black cherries and plums hint at sur-maturité, framed in a soft wrap of baking spices and mocha. Drink now–2020.
title: Clos de L'Oratoire des Papes 2014 Red (Châteauneuf-du-Pape)

description: This eco-friendly wine is demure and elegant on the nose, with medium-intense aromas of black fruit, incense, tree bark, licorice root and schist. The palate offers more oomph, with firm, gripping tannins that yield a tight structure. Slightly smoky black cherry and berry flavors help to flesh out the palate, before transitioning into the peppery, gamy finish. Drink 2018–2022.
title: Château Veronique 2012 Carignan-Grenache (Saint-Chinian)

description: This eco-friendly wine is demure and elegant on the nose, with medium-intense aromas of black fruit, incense, tree bark, licorice root and schist. The palate offers more oomph, with firm, gripping tannins that yield a tight structure. Slightly smoky black cherry and berry flavors help to flesh out the palate, before transitioning into the peppery, gamy finish. Drink 2018–2022.
title: Château Veronique 2012 Carignan-Grenache (Saint-Chinian)

description: This is a solid drive, a middle-of-the-fairway rosé. It's medium-pink in hue and medium bodied in style. Peach, berry and melon aroma and flavors end with a refreshing dose of citrus on the finish. Drink now.
title: Ferraton Pere et Fils 2016 Samorëns Rosé (Côtes du Rhône)

description: This is a solid drive, a middle-of-the-fairway rosé. It's medium-pink in hue and medium bodied in style. Peach, berry and melon aroma and flavors end with a refreshing dose of citrus on the finish. Drink now.
title: Ferraton Pere et Fils 2016 Samorëns Rosé (Côtes du Rhône)

description: Grown in smallest of the so-called Saint-Emilion satellite appellations but within sight of Saint-Emilion's church, the wine is finely balanced and impressive. It has the fruit and the acidity of the vintage: ripe while also crisp with black currants. Drink from 2019.
title: Château Saint-André Corbin 2014  Saint-Georges-Saint-Émilion

description: This is a ripe wine, already approaching maturity. It has rich tannins and a generous structure. The wine is full with plenty of black fruits and balanced acidity. Black currants and spices mingle easily. The wine will be ready to drink from 2018.
title: Château Moya 2014  Castillon Côtes de Bordeaux

description: This estate, belonging to the Compagnet family, is in the northern Médoc. Some firm tannins are contrasted with the attractive acidity and berry fruits to create a warm spicy wine. Almost equal amounts of Cabernet Sauvignon and Merlot give a balanced wine. Drink from 2018.
title: Château le Pey 2015  Médoc

description: This estate, belonging to the Compagnet family, is in the northern Médoc. Some firm tannins are contrasted with the attractive acidity and berry fruits to create a warm spicy wine. Almost equal amounts of Cabernet Sauvignon and Merlot give a balanced wine. Drink from 2018.
title: Château le Pey 2015  Médoc

description: The second wine of the Kressmann family's Latour-Martillac, produced from young vines, has some of the same firm structure and ripe black-currant fruit. Everything is just that bit more mature, giving a ripe fruit-packed wine with a balanced core of tannins. Drink from 2019.
title: Château Latour-Martillac 2014 Lagrave-Martillac  (Pessac-Léognan)

description: This is a special cuvée, produced from the estate of the Prissette family. It is certainly rich and dense but it also has a crisp edge coming from the black-currant fruits. The tannins are still firm and young, underlining the weight of the wine. With a final dry edge, the wine has considerable potential. Drink from 2020.
title: Château du Roc 2014 Libelula  (Castillon Côtes de Bordeaux)

description: The wine is balanced: it is firm with tannins and rich with berry fruits. It has a fine structure that will stand it in good stead as it matures. Drink from 2019.
title: Château de Parenchère 2015  Bordeaux Supérieur

description: The wine is balanced: it is firm with tannins and rich with berry fruits. It has a fine structure that will stand it in good stead as it matures. Drink from 2019.
title: Château de Parenchère 2015  Bordeaux Supérieur

description: This 10-acre estate dates from the 16th century. Today, it has produced a solidly structured wine with firm tannins and a dense textured character. The black fruits are firm with considerable intensity and backed with spice and acidity. Drink from 2021.
title: Château Cruzeau 2015  Saint-Émilion

description: Just the right amount of wood aging gives this ripe wine great style. It has juicy blackberry fruits to balance the spice and toast character, offering richness and a full, fruity character finished with acidity.
title: Château Haut Claribes 2012 Grande Réserve  (Bordeaux)

description: Doussot is a producer in the Aube region in southern Champagne, which explains the high alcohol for Champagne. However the wine still has all the crisp, mineral character of Champagne, broadened out with pineapple and ripe orange flavors. It's a youthful wine, showing tight acidity and that would soften and round in 3–4 more years.
title: Veuve Doussot 2008 Ernestine Brut  (Champagne)

description: Doussot is a producer in the Aube region in southern Champagne, which explains the high alcohol for Champagne. However the wine still has all the crisp, mineral character of Champagne, broadened out with pineapple and ripe orange flavors. It's a youthful wine, showing tight acidity and that would soften and round in 3–4 more years.
title: Veuve Doussot 2008 Ernestine Brut  (Champagne)

description: This is a full, rich wine that has pears and yellow fruits to contrast a fresh minerality and brisk acidity. As the wine opens, it's increasingly bright and crisp in character. A well balanced wine that's full of fruitiness.
title: Canard-Duchêne NV Charles VII Brut  (Champagne)

description: This is a full, rich wine that has pears and yellow fruits to contrast a fresh minerality and brisk acidity. As the wine opens, it's increasingly bright and crisp in character. A well balanced wine that's full of fruitiness.
title: Canard-Duchêne NV Charles VII Brut  (Champagne)

description: A dry wine with mature white fruit and tight acidity, this wine will take time to coax out the rich, mineral character that hides within. It's touched with toast, but freshness and fruitiness dominate for a refreshing aftertaste.
title: Esterlin NV Blanc de Blancs Brut Chardonnay (Champagne)

description: This is a full, ripe wine, with elegant impressions of toast. Robust notes of melon and peach show strongly, giving a rich, warm feel that is brightened with acidity. Drink now through 2017.
title: Château Routas 2011 Coquelicot Viognier-Chardonnay (Vin de Pays Var)

description: Full in the mouth, this is a ripe wine, showing wood, dark plums and a firm layer of tannins. There is a good black-fruit feel, brought out by the wine's acidity. This is serious and worth aging. Drink from 2017.
title: Château la Jorine 2011  Lussac Saint-Émilion

description: This is rich, structured and full-bodied. It bursts with superripe Merlot, darkly tannic and dense. Rich berry and black plum fruits add their weight to this concentrated wine. Drink from 2016.
title: Château au Pont de Guitres 2010  Lalande de Pomerol

description: This is rich, structured and full-bodied. It bursts with superripe Merlot, darkly tannic and dense. Rich berry and black plum fruits add their weight to this concentrated wine. Drink from 2016.
title: Château au Pont de Guitres 2010  Lalande de Pomerol

description: Based in the southern Champagne vineyards of the Aube, the Charles Clément cooperative has made a rich, full-bodied and fruity non-vintage wine. It has forward apple flavor and a soft, creamy texture brightened with lemon zest and brisk acidity. A touch of toast adds complexity to this bottling.
title: Charles Clément NV Cuvée des Vignerons Brut  (Champagne)

description: Superripe Merlot has pushed up the alcohol in this wine. It gives a rich, opulent texture of blackberry jam flavors that are well balanced by the acidity and perfumed character. The broad, generous character gets a fresh lift from the final acidity. Drink from 2018. This Guinjard family wine is 95% Merlot, 3% Cabernet Franc and 2% Cabernet Sauvignon from a 19-acre vineyard.
title: Château de Roquebrune 2012 Cuvée Reine  (Lalande de Pomerol)

description: Touches of vanilla and caramel give this wine an extra dimension of richness. It is full while remaining crisp and herbaceous, with a lively, bright aftertaste. Drink from 2016. The Richard family's two-acre Sauvignon Blanc vineyard is certified organic.
title: Château Cru Godard 2014  Francs Côtes de Bordeaux

description: Touches of vanilla and caramel give this wine an extra dimension of richness. It is full while remaining crisp and herbaceous, with a lively, bright aftertaste. Drink from 2016. The Richard family's two-acre Sauvignon Blanc vineyard is certified organic.
title: Château Cru Godard 2014  Francs Côtes de Bordeaux

description: One of the single-vineyard wines produced by Dauny, this is a wine with great freshness while also having a rich character from the southerly exposure of the vines. Still young, it is all tangy acidity and needs to age. Drink from 2016.
title: Vignoble Dauny 2013 Clos du Roy  (Sancerre)

description: One of the single-vineyard wines produced by Dauny, this is a wine with great freshness while also having a rich character from the southerly exposure of the vines. Still young, it is all tangy acidity and needs to age. Drink from 2016.
title: Vignoble Dauny 2013 Clos du Roy  (Sancerre)

description: Barely off dry, this wine is rich and very perfumed, hinting at an attractive light oxidation from the wood aging. Almonds, white fruits and a fine, tight texture round it out. It will age, so drink from 2014.
title: Domaine Vincent Carême 2011 Le Peu Morier  (Vouvray)

description: Like oak? Yes? Then this is the Vacqueyras for you. There's ample fruit weight to support the lush lashings of toasted coconut and luxurious vanilla notes and pull them through a long, velvety-textured finish. Drink now–2018.
title: Tardieu-Laurent 2010 Vieilles Vignes Red (Vacqueyras)

description: A rich dessert Vouvray with a marvelous tension between acidity and honeyed sweetness. There is a floral character, offering a contrast and bringing out a fresher side to the wine. With the tension and texture, the wine will age. Drink from 2017.
title: Domaine Pichot 2011 Le Marigny  (Vouvray)

description: Slightly bruised apple on nose and palate also becomes apparent on the textured, balanced palate of this wine that aligns citric freshness with more mellow and sonorous tones of ripeness. The finish is dry and whistle-clean.
title: Lucien Albrecht 2015 Réserve Riesling (Alsace)

description: A closed nose opens into the taut but streamlined body of this wine. There is tension on the slender but concentrated palate and a fearlessly brisk freshness, leading to a dry finish. The wine will benefit from bottle age and reward patience with glorious apple fruit. Drink 2018–2028.
title: René Muré 2014 Cote de Rouffach Riesling (Alsace)

description: The nose of this wine is restrained, just giving away pear and citrus, but the dry palate is concentrated and spiced with almond and marzipan. Ample tone from mouthwatering acidity will make this a huge winner at any table. It has great poise and balance.
title: Domaines Schlumberger 2014 Les Princes Abbés Pinot Gris (Alsace)

description: Tropical hints of pineapple rise from the glass but the dry palate of this wine focuses on tangerine and ripe lemon. It offers poise and slenderness in a clean-cut, dry style that promises refreshment and leaves a citrus-scented aftertaste.
title: Domaine Sipp-Mack 2015 Tradition Riesling (Alsace)

description: Soft notes of ripe Comice pear are laced with fresh lemon hints in this Pinot Gris that is both textured and refreshing, a great example of the 2014 zestiness. Dry, precise and lasting, it is lovely now but will develop. Drink now until 2020.
title: Domaine Pfister 2014 Tradition Pinot Gris (Alsace)

description: Earth and citrus pith make for an untypical opening. The soft palate follows with far more fruit than expected, underscored by a dollop of sweetness that brings out perfumed apricot and ripe, yellow peach. The depth of fruit and its purity is beguiling, like a cloud of juicy, generous ripeness.
title: Domaine Ostertag 2015 Vignoble d'E Gewurztraminer (Alsace)

description: An open and inviting scent of ripe pear is freshened by an impression of wet pebbles, cold stone and citrus. The palate is textured and expressive, giving a broader canvas to these fruity, fresh flavors that have a lovely edge of gentle bitterness. The palate finishes just off dry.
title: Domaine Fernand Engel 2014 Cuvée Engel Pinot Gris (Alsace)

description: A fruity wine, full of red cherries and plenty of acidity. There is dry structure, making it food friendly, but the wine is not for aging.
title: Gérard Brisson 2010  Beaujolais-Villages

description: There is a layer of tannins here that impart a dry edge to what is otherwise sweetly fruity wine. It is full and juicy, with strawberry fruit flavors.
title: Georges Duboeuf 2011 Nouveau  (Beaujolais)

description: A fresh, lemon-scented wine, with white flower aromas and soft, crisp lime flavors. The wine has some softness as well as an attractive zesty finish. Screwcap.
title: Cave de Lugny 2010 La Côte Blanche  (Mâcon-Villages)

description: A fresh, lemon-scented wine, with white flower aromas and soft, crisp lime flavors. The wine has some softness as well as an attractive zesty finish. Screwcap.
title: Cave de Lugny 2010 La Côte Blanche  (Mâcon-Villages)

description: Wood and spice, as well as ripe fruit, come together in this generous wine. It does have a tight texture that will soften as it ages. What is so attractive at the moment are the beautiful acidity and crisp apple favors. It's a wine with good aging potential, so drink from 2018.
title: Alex Gambal 2013  Chassagne-Montrachet

description: With noticeable wood flavors, this sophisticated wine is smooth, rich and creamy. It has enough fruit to sustain all this toast, giving a wine that has a fresh line that runs right through it, passing apples and fresh apricots on the way. Drink from 2016.
title: Georges Duboeuf 2013 Domaine Beranger  (Pouilly-Fuissé)

description: This wine is textured and tight with delicious, refreshing acidity that is softened by a round vanilla edge. It is still young, still developing its balance and rich, honeyed fruit character. Drink this rich and stylish wine from 2017.
title: Domaine Jean-Paul et Benoît Droin 2013 Vaillons Premier Cru  (Chablis)

description: Rich fruit is boosted by the wood aging. Together they give a ripe wine full of acidity and juicy yellow fruits at the same time. It's a delicious wine, smooth while lined with acidity. The wood flavors sustain it, and it should be ready to drink from 2016.
title: Domaine du Chalet Pouilly 2013  Pouilly-Fuissé

description: Rich fruit is boosted by the wood aging. Together they give a ripe wine full of acidity and juicy yellow fruits at the same time. It's a delicious wine, smooth while lined with acidity. The wood flavors sustain it, and it should be ready to drink from 2016.
title: Domaine du Chalet Pouilly 2013  Pouilly-Fuissé

description: This wine is ripe, with a warm, yellow fruit character. It is bright and poised, elegant and sophisticated. Acidity shoots through the richness, bringing a strong citrus element. Sunny in character, it will still age; drink from late 2016.
title: Albert Bichot 2013  Pouilly-Fuissé

description: Baked pear and sweet, baked apple make for an inviting opening. The same friendly duet plays on the off-dry palate all the way to the lingering finish. Along the way, there are highlights of zesty lemon and richer hints of honey and melon. It's simple, fun and even a little bit intriguing.
title: Dopff Au Moulin 2014 Réserve Pinot Gris (Alsace)

description: The subdued nose gives way on the palate to earthy apple, reminiscent of Russet, underlined by a vein of lemony acidity that brightens from the inside out. Lemony earthiness lingers on the dry finish.
title: Domaine Schoffit 2013 Harth Tradition Riesling (Alsace)

description: This Chardonnay-led blend, with 20% Viognier and 10% Sauvignon, opens with mature notes of apple peel, orange rind, toasted walnut, honeycomb and baking spice. The round, robust offers those same notes, followed by a subtle, refreshing salinity that appears on the finish.
title: Gérard Bertrand 2013 Cigalus White (Aude Hauterive)

description: This Chardonnay-led blend, with 20% Viognier and 10% Sauvignon, opens with mature notes of apple peel, orange rind, toasted walnut, honeycomb and baking spice. The round, robust offers those same notes, followed by a subtle, refreshing salinity that appears on the finish.
title: Gérard Bertrand 2013 Cigalus White (Aude Hauterive)

description: There's an assertive garrigue character to this wine, with strong aromas of thyme, bay, lavender, fennel and white pepper that overwhelm the red fruit tones. The medium-weight palate offers a bit more fruit, with flavors of strawberry and raspberry to partner with the assertive mentholated-herb notes. Accents of oak and sweet spice unfold on the finish.
title: Blanville 2013 Helios Red (Languedoc)

description: There's an assertive garrigue character to this wine, with strong aromas of thyme, bay, lavender, fennel and white pepper that overwhelm the red fruit tones. The medium-weight palate offers a bit more fruit, with flavors of strawberry and raspberry to partner with the assertive mentholated-herb notes. Accents of oak and sweet spice unfold on the finish.
title: Blanville 2013 Helios Red (Languedoc)

description: Light in color while full of fruit, this is a ripe and jammy wine. A good core of tannins are surrounded by ripe cherry and strawberry-flavored fruits. There is a good future for this dense wine, so drink from 2017.
title: Louis Max 2013 Vignes du Domaine  (Mercurey)

description: Notes of bruised apple peel make this wine appear older than it is, but it is not without charm. The apple fruit is tied into a streak of bright, lemony freshness concluding in a just off-dry, invigorating finish.
title: Kuentz-Bas 2014 Trois Chateaux Riesling (Alsace)

description: Light and refreshing, with hints of berries and citrus alongside some herbal elements. The bead is a little on the large side, making the mouthfeel a bit rustic, but it'll do fine at the season's big holiday gatherings.
title: Kriter NV Eclat Carmin Rosé Sparkling (France)

description: A light-bodied, somewhat austere sparkler that's short on fruit but long on mineral and earthy notes suggesting wet clay and chalk. Finishes fresh.
title: Pierre Sparr NV Brut Réserve Sparkling (Crémant d'Alsace)

description: Sure it's a bit simple and fruity—the flavors run toward berries and citrus—but it's also cleanly made, with a slightly creamy mouthfeel and a soft, easy-drinking finish.
title: Patriarche Père et Fils NV Eclat Carmin Rosé Sparkling (Vin Mousseux)

description: Lively and juicy, this is packed with fresh red cherry fruits, red currants and some wood. It's round, soft, only lightly tannic.
title: Barton & Guestier 2005 Bistro Wine Pinot Noir (Vin de Pays d'Oc)

description: A quirky wine, but largely successful, with upfront tones of clove-spiced orange peel and baking bread followed by dried fruit notes in the mouth. The long finish is on the sweet side and winds down to a note of Asian candy.
title: Marc Kreydenweiss 2007 Le Moine Mœnchberg Grand Cru Pinot Gris (Alsace)

description: A quirky wine, but largely successful, with upfront tones of clove-spiced orange peel and baking bread followed by dried fruit notes in the mouth. The long finish is on the sweet side and winds down to a note of Asian candy.
title: Marc Kreydenweiss 2007 Le Moine Mœnchberg Grand Cru Pinot Gris (Alsace)

description: Another wacky Riesling from Marc Kreydenweiss, this one somehow works. There's Asian spice here and an odd collection of oxidative aromas but also undeniable concentration and good length. Serve this unusual wine by itself or with Indian fare.
title: Marc Kreydenweiss 2007 Le Château Kastelberg Grand Cru Riesling (Alsace)

description: An herbal Sauvignon that is fresh and on the lean side. The flavors are of crisp green apples, very fruity, with a structure of lime zest and vivid acidity on the finish. Screwcap.
region: Vin de Pays des Côtes de Gascogne
title: Domaine du Tariquet 2007 Sauvignon Blanc (Vin de Pays des Côtes de Gascogne)

description: A deliciously light, fresh rosé, its crisp raspberry flavors enhanced by acidity. The finish is a full burst of fruit salad.
title: Domaine des Corbillières 2007 Rosé Pinot Noir (Touraine)

description: A deliciously light, fresh rosé, its crisp raspberry flavors enhanced by acidity. The finish is a full burst of fruit salad.
title: Domaine des Corbillières 2007 Rosé Pinot Noir (Touraine)

description: This intriguing blend of Chardonnay and Sauvignon Blanc works well, displaying richness as well as an intense herbaceousness. This is a lively wine, with its apple and pear flavors, topped with grapefruit acidity.
region: Vin de Pays des Côtes de Gascogne
title: Domaine du Tariquet 2007 Chardonnay-Sauvignon (Vin de Pays des Côtes de Gascogne)

description: This intriguing blend of Chardonnay and Sauvignon Blanc works well, displaying richness as well as an intense herbaceousness. This is a lively wine, with its apple and pear flavors, topped with grapefruit acidity.
region: Vin de Pays des Côtes de Gascogne
title: Domaine du Tariquet 2007 Chardonnay-Sauvignon (Vin de Pays des Côtes de Gascogne)

description: This is a light, citrus-fruit dominated wine. It has attractive fruitiness, tang and zest, and its acidity is crisp and refreshing. Apples and green fruits add a little richness at the end. Screwcap.
title: Château de la Ragotiere 2011 Vieilles Vignes Sur Lie  (Muscadet Sèvre et Maine)

description: Only the least of Dagueneau's wines is under $30, but a darn fine wine it is. Smoke, green herbs, flint and lime aromas and green fern, honeysuckle and powdered quartz flavors make for a complex drink that finishes ultraclean.
title: Didier Dagueneau 2000 En Chailloux  (Pouilly-Fumé)

description: Not for the fainthearted, this is a huge, mouthfilling wine bursting with yellow plum, hazelnut and peach aromas, and accented by smoke, butter and toast. Yet for all its size, it manages to marry that power with a sense of mineral elegance. Drink now–2010.
title: Louis Latour 2000  Bâtard-Montrachet

description: Not quite as big as the Bâtard, Latour's Corton-Charlie is the house's flagship (the company owns 10 hectares of the grand cru) and most ageable wine. The 2000 boasts aromas of gunflint, pear, smoked meat and buttered toast. White peaches emerge on the palate, but the primary flavors are of minerals and spice. Finishes with tons of citrus and an almost tannic feel. Give it two or three years to begin to soften.
title: Louis Latour 2000  Corton-Charlemagne

description: Not quite as big as the Bâtard, Latour's Corton-Charlie is the house's flagship (the company owns 10 hectares of the grand cru) and most ageable wine. The 2000 boasts aromas of gunflint, pear, smoked meat and buttered toast. White peaches emerge on the palate, but the primary flavors are of minerals and spice. Finishes with tons of citrus and an almost tannic feel. Give it two or three years to begin to soften.
title: Louis Latour 2000  Corton-Charlemagne

description: This wine is still young, tight and on the crisp acid side. That doesn't mean it won't soften and fill out, although it will probably stay ultrafresh and packed with red-currant flavors for some time. Wait to drink until 2018.
title: Au Pied du Mont Chauve 2013 Le Charmois Premier Cru  (Saint-Aubin)

description: This wine is still young, tight and on the crisp acid side. That doesn't mean it won't soften and fill out, although it will probably stay ultrafresh and packed with red-currant flavors for some time. Wait to drink until 2018.
title: Au Pied du Mont Chauve 2013 Le Charmois Premier Cru  (Saint-Aubin)

description: This plump, dry rosé features hints of wet stone, strawberry and barely ripe melon. It's vibrant, refreshing and an ideal thirst-quencher for the warm months ahead.
title: Famille Perrin 2014 Réserve Rosé (Côtes du Rhône)

description: This limited-production wine is still tight and not yet revealing its full potential. As it develops over the next few months, it will show its flavors of ripe red apples and an intense texture. The wine is full bodied while remaining crisp. Give it until 2017 before drinking.
title: Domaine Daniel Reverdy et Fils 2014 Anthéa  (Sancerre)

description: Named after the soft yellow stone that dominates the central Loire vineyards, this wine is firm, and still young. It is now delicious with ripe, perfumed black fruits and juicy acidity. But it will develop and deepen, and will be worth keeping, so drink from 2017.
title: Domaine Damien Lorieux 2014 Tuffeaux Cabernet Franc (Bourgueil)

description: Very young, this firm, structured wine has dense tannins and a dry core. All of this will open up to bring in the red fruits waiting behind this formidable facade. It needs to age, so drink from 2019.
title: Louis Chevallier 2014 Les Vaucrains Premier Cru  (Nuits-St.-Georges)

description: Very young, this firm, structured wine has dense tannins and a dry core. All of this will open up to bring in the red fruits waiting behind this formidable facade. It needs to age, so drink from 2019.
title: Louis Chevallier 2014 Les Vaucrains Premier Cru  (Nuits-St.-Georges)

description: Light, fruity and fragrant, this is an attractive, crisp wine that highlights red-berry fruits and soft acidity. It's a wine to drink now.
title: Château Frédignac 2011 Cuvée Prestige  (Blaye Côtes de Bordeaux)

description: Light, fruity and fragrant, this is an attractive, crisp wine that highlights red-berry fruits and soft acidity. It's a wine to drink now.
title: Château Frédignac 2011 Cuvée Prestige  (Blaye Côtes de Bordeaux)

description: With considerable acidity, this wine shows as much black currant fruitiness as it does structure. Fruit on the palate is accented with just a touch of toast and light tannins. This is an attractive wine for early drinking.
title: Donjon de Bruignac 2011  Bordeaux

description: With considerable acidity, this wine shows as much black currant fruitiness as it does structure. Fruit on the palate is accented with just a touch of toast and light tannins. This is an attractive wine for early drinking.
title: Donjon de Bruignac 2011  Bordeaux

description: This lively, fruity wine is simple in character but full of grapefruit and lemon crispness. It is softly textured, but has a final bite of lemon zest and tight acidity.
title: Château Seguin 2012  Bordeaux Blanc

description: This is an austere wine that's tough on the palate and with high acidity. The black currant fruitiness is still developing, so the wine shouldn't be drunk before 2016.
title: Château Recougne 2011  Bordeaux Supérieur

description: This is a spicy wine that shows rich fruit along with nutmeg and cinnamon flavors. Baked apple and ripe pear underly the spice, while acidity on the finish accentuates a fresh aftertaste.
title: Château Grand Jean 2012  Bordeaux Blanc

description: Obviously wood aged, this wine's dryness comes from the attenuating character of the barrels. That leaves little room for lean fruit flavors. Maybe it will soften, but the wood is always going to be dominant.
title: Château de Ricaud 2011 Réserve des Côteaux  (Cadillac Côtes de Bordeaux)

description: Here is a concentrated wine that has dense tannins and acidity. Black currant freshness offers lively pleasure already, but should intensify in fruitiness in two years.
title: Baron Philippe de Rothschild 2011 Mouton Cadet  (Bordeaux)

description: There is a touch of smoke and stone that lends a darker aspect to the ripe but crisp apple fruit. The palate has that same taut but very full-fruited feel—of very tightly held ample fruit reminiscent of red-cheeked, aromatic apples. This is both powerful and svelte. The palate is dry and finishes very clean, leaving you with haunting apple notes and fresh lemon.
title: Domaine Vincent Stoeffler 2014 Kirchberg de Barr Grand Cru Riesling (Alsace)

description: This wine clearly needs to breathe. It is only after a few minutes of airtime that it shows its true colors: then very tart and aromatic apples appear, alongside a hint of smoke and a sheer touch of lemon freshness. The palate continues on that lemony streak and is absolutely dry. The body is lithe and slender and shows great freshness and intensity. Apple and stone flavors linger. Drink 2020–2030.
title: Domaine Schoffit 2013 Clos Saint-Théobald Grand Cru Rangen Riesling (Alsace)

description: Tender notes of honeysuckle and rose rise from the glass. On the palate they perfume the generous peach and mirabelle plum fruit, supported by some residual sweetness. This strikes a very harmonious balance between tender opulence an sprightly freshness. The finish is intense, tangy, medium sweet and superbly balanced.
title: Domaine Saint-Rémy 2014 Ehrhart Hengst Grand Cru Gewurztraminer (Alsace)

description: Tender notes of honeysuckle and rose rise from the glass. On the palate they perfume the generous peach and mirabelle plum fruit, supported by some residual sweetness. This strikes a very harmonious balance between tender opulence an sprightly freshness. The finish is intense, tangy, medium sweet and superbly balanced.
title: Domaine Saint-Rémy 2014 Ehrhart Hengst Grand Cru Gewurztraminer (Alsace)

description: A slightly brooding nose suggests brambly fruit as well as freshness. The palate crunches with red and black cherry, imbued with a kind of boyish impish joy. This is disarmingly rustic, but also very, very unusual and utterly moreish in its singular and honest simplicity. Drying tannins coat the mouth while juicy tart freshness makes you want to take another sip. This is all about stormy, romantic wilderness. Beware, this might just steal your heart.
title: Domaine Marcel Deiss 2014 Burlenberg Red (Alsace)

description: There is the merest hint of chamomile lift on the nose, pulling all the other flavors heavenwards with it. There is apple as well as lemon zest. The palate is wonderfully pure and totally dry. Here and there more herbal inflections show and more mellow hints of baked apple. This is dry, taut and aromatic, but also clean-cut and precise. Lovely now but with definite aging potential. Drink now through 2030.
title: Domaine Charles Baur 2013 Brand Grand Cru Riesling (Alsace)

description: From the vineyard on the slope above Château Pavie, this is a beautiful, juicy and ripe wine. It has a mineral character with great swathes of black-currant fruit. This is a very fine wine, well delineated, ripe and with a delicious red-currant aftertaste. Drink from 2026.
title: Château Pavie Decesse 2014  Saint-Émilion

description: Tightly structured, this is a dense wine. Packed with dry tannins, it is starting life as a firm wine. It is equally rich in fruit, a panoply of black plums and red currants. Drink this concentrated wine from 2026.
title: Château Latour-Martillac 2014  Pessac-Léognan

description: Tightly structured, this is a dense wine. Packed with dry tannins, it is starting life as a firm wine. It is equally rich in fruit, a panoply of black plums and red currants. Drink this concentrated wine from 2026.
title: Château Latour-Martillac 2014  Pessac-Léognan

description: This is a deliciously balanced wine. Spice from the wood aging makes a happy contrast with the black-currant fruit and acidity. It is elegant and with great fruitiness. The wine, with its tannic base, will age well. The estate is to the west of Saint-Emilion, close to Château Figeac. Drink from 2023.
title: Château la Grâce Dieu 2014  Saint-Émilion

description: This is a structured wine that still has serious layers of ripe fruit and rich tannins. The black currant from the Cabernet Sauvignon is balanced by the jammy richness of the delicious Merlot. It's an impressive wine that continues the progress of this estate, owned by Lafite-Rothschild. Drink from 2024.
title: Château Duhart-Milon 2014  Pauillac

description: This is a structured wine that still has serious layers of ripe fruit and rich tannins. The black currant from the Cabernet Sauvignon is balanced by the jammy richness of the delicious Merlot. It's an impressive wine that continues the progress of this estate, owned by Lafite-Rothschild. Drink from 2024.
title: Château Duhart-Milon 2014  Pauillac

description: Packed with the dark tannins and structure of Cabernet Sauvignon, this wine, produced by the team of Calon Ségur is intense, concentrated and dark. It has a firm structure, solid and with a luscious aftertaste. The acidity of the year just shows at the end. Drink from 2026.
title: Château Capbern 2014  Saint-Estèphe

description: A lovely lemony lift jumps from the glass and immediately signals maturing Riesling. The palate is still taut with freshness but has the harmonious balminess of bottle age. Hints of dried pear and candied lemon peel appear. The palate is as precise and taut as ever, brightened by utter apple and citrus crispness. The finish is long, dry and utterly clean cut.
title: Paul Blanck 2012 Schlossberg Grand Cru Riesling (Alsace)

description: Rich and opulent, this is a gorgeously perfumed, sweet wine. The Eichberg vineyard produces opulent wines, and this is no exception. A touch of honey matches the intense spiciness and general sense of flamboyance. It's a ripe wine, while still structured and dense. Drink from 2017.
title: Domaine Zinck 2011 Eichberg Grand Cru Gewurztraminer (Alsace)

description: This is pure Riesling, very mineral, steely and direct. With intense acidity as well as the crispest green and citrus fruits, it's still very young. The fresh current gives an initial lift while keeping the concentrated texture in mind. Drink from 2017.
title: Domaine Weinbach 2013 Cuvée Théo Riesling (Alsace)

description: This is pure Riesling, very mineral, steely and direct. With intense acidity as well as the crispest green and citrus fruits, it's still very young. The fresh current gives an initial lift while keeping the concentrated texture in mind. Drink from 2017.
title: Domaine Weinbach 2013 Cuvée Théo Riesling (Alsace)

description: The wine is rich, full in the mouth but finely balanced. It has retained plenty of freshness, the white fruits aromatic, mineral and stylish. The ripeness gives an opulent style that leaves a powerful aftertaste. Drink from 2018.
title: Domaine Schoffit 2011 Sommerberg Grand Cru Riesling (Alsace)

description: From one of the many recent exceptional years in Sauternes, this ripe, unctuous wine has balanced the rich honeyed fruit and the drier edge of botrytis. It's full in the mouth, with Seville orange and a light touch of ginger. Drink from 2019.
title: Château Raymond-Lafon 2011  Sauternes

description: While it is dry, this wine is so rich that it has a honeyed, sweet character. It is very full, ripe, full of grapefruit, white stone fruits and tight Meyer lemon. It is still in its youthful fruity phase and needs to age. Drink from 2018.
title: Boeckel 2012 Wiebelsberg Grand Cru Riesling (Alsace)

description: While it is dry, this wine is so rich that it has a honeyed, sweet character. It is very full, ripe, full of grapefruit, white stone fruits and tight Meyer lemon. It is still in its youthful fruity phase and needs to age. Drink from 2018.
title: Boeckel 2012 Wiebelsberg Grand Cru Riesling (Alsace)

description: Still young and chock full of acidity, it has considerable potential. It's a tight, bright wine, the lemon zest acidity still dominant. It's going to be a major wine as it ages, keeping bone dry while developing its aromatic, beautifully fragrant side. Drink from 2019.
designation: Clos Saint Landelin Vorbourg Grand Cru
title: René Muré 2012 Clos Saint Landelin Vorbourg Grand Cru Riesling (Alsace)

description: Still young and chock full of acidity, it has considerable potential. It's a tight, bright wine, the lemon zest acidity still dominant. It's going to be a major wine as it ages, keeping bone dry while developing its aromatic, beautifully fragrant side. Drink from 2019.
designation: Clos Saint Landelin Vorbourg Grand Cru
title: René Muré 2012 Clos Saint Landelin Vorbourg Grand Cru Riesling (Alsace)

description: Produced from organically grown grapes, this soft wine has red fruits that miss much definition, only hinting at some stalky acidity. It is ready to drink.
title: Les Vignerons Réunis de Monségur 2014 Le Roi Pépin  (Bordeaux)

description: Produced from organically grown grapes, this soft wine has red fruits that miss much definition, only hinting at some stalky acidity. It is ready to drink.
title: Les Vignerons Réunis de Monségur 2014 Le Roi Pépin  (Bordeaux)

description: The song of the frogs, aka the croak, is an odd name for this wine made from organically grown grapes. The wine itself is soft, easy and light, with red berry fruits and some perfumed acidity. Drink now.
title: Les Vignerons Réunis de Monségur 2014 Le Chant des Grenouilles Rosé (Bordeaux Rosé)

description: Dark pink in color, this full wine offers tannins as well as crisp red fruits, giving it structure and a firm texture. The wine blends nearly all Bordeaux grapes: Malbec, Cabernet Franc, Cabernet Sauvignon and Merlot. Drink it chilled, like a rosé.
title: Château Landereau 2014  Bordeaux Clairet

description: While the wine's aromas are all about wood and smoky toast, it proffers reassuring hints of fruit on the palate. However, it is still an over-oaked wine that will likely never have enough fruitiness.
title: Château La Branne 2013  Médoc

description: For a white Bordeaux, this is hugely rich and ripe. With its spice and toast, the wood-aging of the Muscadelle has added extra complexity. The alcohol gives the wine a peppery character that is less attractive while also removing freshness. Consider this wine a curiosity.
title: Château de Bel 2014  Bordeaux Blanc

description: For a white Bordeaux, this is hugely rich and ripe. With its spice and toast, the wood-aging of the Muscadelle has added extra complexity. The alcohol gives the wine a peppery character that is less attractive while also removing freshness. Consider this wine a curiosity.
title: Château de Bel 2014  Bordeaux Blanc

description: This wine is lean and stalky, with firm, dry tannins that don't give much room for fruitiness. It will be ready to drink from 2017.
title: Château Blaignan 2013  Médoc

description: From the east of the Bordeaux region, this light and juicy wine has attractive, forward acidity and the gentlest of tannins. Fresh and fruity, it is ready to drink.
title: Château Caville 2014  Bordeaux

description: This soft, ready-to-drink wine is all about black-currant fruitiness, with only the lightest of tannins. Juicy, fresh acidity finishes an attractive wine.
title: De Luze 2014 Cuvée Fashion  (Bordeaux)

description: This wine is dry, dark and packed with too many tannins and not enough fruit. A strong, tough character is the dominant feature and it is tough to see how this will broaden out.
title: Château Seguin 2013  Pessac-Léognan

description: This wine is dry, dark and packed with too many tannins and not enough fruit. A strong, tough character is the dominant feature and it is tough to see how this will broaden out.
title: Château Seguin 2013  Pessac-Léognan

description: This wine is not balanced, with wood and acidity opposing each other. It has spice, high toast flavors and stalky black currants. Although it could have potential, it is likely to remain tough. The property is unusual—133 acres in one block.
title: Château la Garde 2013  Pessac-Léognan

description: This unbalanced wine is caught between acidity and wood. It is hard to see how well this will develop. Owner Francis Boutemy, an inventor, created the “Bout'mobile” which glides seated pickers along rows as they cut clusters that are dropped directly into a mobile sorting machine.
title: Château Haut Lagrange 2013  Pessac-Léognan

description: Light in color, the wine is equally light in flavor–a soft, gentle wine with only hints of tannins. Fruity without much depth, it is ready to drink, .
title: Château Fonfroide 2013  Bordeaux

description: Light in color, the wine is equally light in flavor–a soft, gentle wine with only hints of tannins. Fruity without much depth, it is ready to drink, .
title: Château Fonfroide 2013  Bordeaux

description: Tight and stalky, this wine has smoky red-berry fruits and a strong layer of acidity. Still young, it will certainly soften, although it is likely to remain light and lean. Drink from 2018.
title: Château Fleur la Mothe 2013  Médoc

description: This wine is lean, austere with high acidity that leaves fruit well behind. It is structured and dry, only hinting at black-currant freshness. This third-generation family estate also hosts monthly musical and tasting events and sells fruit, vegetables and honey.
title: Château Bardins 2013  Pessac-Léognan

description: Maturing well, this ripe red-berry flavored wine is soft and rounded. It has just a hint of tannins and wood along with generous ripe fruitiness. The wine is full bodied, likely to be ready to drink from 2018.
title: Roger et Didier Raimbault 2015  Sancerre

description: The ripeness of mirabelle plums and the satisfying tartness of ripe Cox apples are met on nose and palate by wonderfully fresh lemon notes. The citrus zestiness works it way through the slender dry body all the way to the lip-smacking, fresh and even brisk finish.
title: Pierre Sparr 2015 Grande Réserve Riesling (Alsace)

description: The ripeness of mirabelle plums and the satisfying tartness of ripe Cox apples are met on nose and palate by wonderfully fresh lemon notes. The citrus zestiness works it way through the slender dry body all the way to the lip-smacking, fresh and even brisk finish.
title: Pierre Sparr 2015 Grande Réserve Riesling (Alsace)

description: An earthy element touches upon the lemon freshness on the nose and palate. The dry style lets the citrus freshness express itself fully. There is the tang of zest and the bright juiciness of lemon fruit. The palate is concentrated and taut, submerging any earthy tones to end in brisk, clean freshness.
title: Paul Blanck 2015 Rosenbourg Riesling (Alsace)

description: This is a smooth wine with gentle tannins and red berry fruit. It has juicy acidity and a slight toastiness from oak. With spice and acidity, it will be an attractive wine to drink from 2018.
title: Nuiton-Beaunoy 2015  Beaune

description: Ripe and soft, this is a fruity wine with refreshing lemon and apple flavors. Its rich texture is balanced by good acidity—unsurprising since the grapes grow near the white wine vineyards of Meursault and Puligny-Montrachet.
title: Maison Champy 2015  Bourgogne

description: Ripe and soft, this is a fruity wine with refreshing lemon and apple flavors. Its rich texture is balanced by good acidity—unsurprising since the grapes grow near the white wine vineyards of Meursault and Puligny-Montrachet.
title: Maison Champy 2015  Bourgogne

description: From vineyards owned by the Gagey family, this wine is ripe, easy to drink and full of fruit. Its strawberry and red cherry flavors are lifted by acidity and grounded in balancing tannins. It is made to be drunk young and will be ready from late 2017.
title: Louis Jadot 2014 Le Chapitre  (Bourgogne)

description: Equal parts Clairette, Grenache Blanc and Roussanne, this is vinified in a combination of concrete eggs, stainless-steel tanks and oak barrels. Pineapple and melon aromas and flavors dominate this warm, broad wine, picking up a slightly bitter edge on the finish.
title: Domaine du Pegau 2015 Cuvée à Tempo White (Châteauneuf-du-Pape)

description: This is a second wine of Château Tournelles. Soft and generously ripe, it has attractive tannins that just give the bright fruit a support. The wine, a blend of Bordeaux grapes typical of this appellation, is ready to drink.
title: Château Tournelles 2014 Voluptabilis Red (Buzet)

description: With touches of botrytis, apricot and bitter orange flavors and perfumed sweetness, this is a textured wine that has plenty of the acidity of the year. It is ripe, still with its primary fruitiness intact. Drink from 2019.
title: Château Bélingard 2013 Réserve  (Monbazillac)

description: This wine has equal amounts of ripe berry fruit and structure. There is a smoky character, wood and spice notes, balanced acidity and a leather-like touch to the texture. It is slowly developing, and it has the potential to be rich. Age this for 6–8 years.
title: Albert Bichot 2010 Domaine du Clos Frantin  (Vosne-Romanée)

description: This is a tight, currently closed wine, but it has the potential to exude intense fruit and balancing acidity. It has weight and a taut, minerally texture, and the finish is fresh and lively. It will age over the medium term.
title: Olivier Leflaive 2010 Grande Montagne Premier Cru  (Chassagne-Montrachet)

description: Showing the structure of Gevrey-Chambertin and the ripe fruit of the 2009 vintage, this bottling is immediately opulent and seductive. With its red plum flavor and balanced tannins and acids, this is a solid wine to drink now.
title: Jaffelin 2009  Gevrey-Chambertin

description: Showing the structure of Gevrey-Chambertin and the ripe fruit of the 2009 vintage, this bottling is immediately opulent and seductive. With its red plum flavor and balanced tannins and acids, this is a solid wine to drink now.
title: Jaffelin 2009  Gevrey-Chambertin

description: Made from fruit that was sourced from a 2.4-acre plot on the steep slopes of Vergisson, this is an intense, ripe, wood-aged wine. The acidity is allied to the spice and yellow fruit flavors. A concentrated wine of great purity, this is worth aging for several years.
title: Domaine Ferret 2010 Tête de Cru Les Perrières  (Pouilly-Fuissé)

description: Made from fruit that was sourced from a 2.4-acre plot on the steep slopes of Vergisson, this is an intense, ripe, wood-aged wine. The acidity is allied to the spice and yellow fruit flavors. A concentrated wine of great purity, this is worth aging for several years.
title: Domaine Ferret 2010 Tête de Cru Les Perrières  (Pouilly-Fuissé)

description: This is a structured, fruity wine that has ripe strawberry and red plum flavors. Its tannins are condensed at the core, and the finish is marked by refreshing acidity. The vineyard is wholly owned by Faiveley.
title: Domaine Faiveley 2010 Clos de L'Ecu Premier Cru  (Beaune)

description: Rich, elegant and classic, this wine is made from fruit sourced from old vines—some as much as 70 years old. It has a tannic structure, but the dominant elements are the dense red- and black-plum flavors, which are supported by the wine's acids. Age it for 5–6 years.
title: Domaine Bruno Clair 2010 Les Longeroies  (Marsannay)

description: This wine is perfumed, with delicious notes of plum and spice that are balanced by light tannins and fine, elegant acids. A touch of mineral marks the finish.
title: David Moreau 2010 Clos Rousseau Premier Cru  (Santenay)

description: This wine is perfumed, with delicious notes of plum and spice that are balanced by light tannins and fine, elegant acids. A touch of mineral marks the finish.
title: David Moreau 2010 Clos Rousseau Premier Cru  (Santenay)

description: Full bodied, rich and ripe, this wine has a minerally texture and is loaded with tropical fruit, citrus and apricot flavors. It's a serious selection that needs some aging. This is one of a series of single-vineyard wines from the Comte de Ternay estate.
designation: Château de Rully La Bressande Cuvée Comte R. de Ternay Premier Cru
title: Antonin Rodet 2010 Château de Rully La Bressande Cuvée Comte R. de Ternay Premier Cru  (Rully)

description: Full bodied, rich and ripe, this wine has a minerally texture and is loaded with tropical fruit, citrus and apricot flavors. It's a serious selection that needs some aging. This is one of a series of single-vineyard wines from the Comte de Ternay estate.
designation: Château de Rully La Bressande Cuvée Comte R. de Ternay Premier Cru
title: Antonin Rodet 2010 Château de Rully La Bressande Cuvée Comte R. de Ternay Premier Cru  (Rully)

description: Rounded and rich, this is already a delicious wine. It has great fruitiness combined with a fine, tight texture. There is a crisp edge that contrasts with the depth of flavor and warm, ripe feel. Drink now, or, better yet, keep for a year. Scewcap.
title: Vignobles Dubergé 2012 Esprit de Saint Sulpice  (Bordeaux Blanc)

description: There is an earthy, animal element to this wine that adds complexity to ripe fruit flavors. Currently, it's a wine that is all potential, sweet and dense with a finish of intense acidity. Drink from 2017.
title: Château Sigalas Rabaud 2010  Sauternes

description: This is a complex wine that offers firm tannins and rich fruit. It has weight, density and a strong sense of ripeness. With balance and depth, it's a wine with good aging potential. Drink from 2015.
title: Château Loumelat 2011 Cuvée J-J Lesgourgues  (Bordeaux)

description: This is a perfumed wine with soft acidity and flavors of ripe apricot, nutmeg and spiced apple. It's full of character and the aftertaste retains the freshness of the vintage.
title: Château la Croix de Roche 2012  Bordeaux Blanc

description: While structured and firm, this is a ripe and juicy wine. Its texture has some minerality, lending an edge to intensely youthful acidity. As the wine ages, all these elements will integrate well, so drink from 2016.
title: Château La Clarière Laithwaite 2011  Castillon Côtes de Bordeaux

description: While structured and firm, this is a ripe and juicy wine. Its texture has some minerality, lending an edge to intensely youthful acidity. As the wine ages, all these elements will integrate well, so drink from 2016.
title: Château La Clarière Laithwaite 2011  Castillon Côtes de Bordeaux

description: Dry, firm and tannic, this is a wine with great potential. It has weight, ripe berry fruits and a solid character. Wood aging shows lightly, allowing the ripeness of the fruit to dominate. Drink from 2016.
title: Château des Demoiselles 2011  Castillon Côtes de Bordeaux

description: This is an attractive, aromatic wine, full of fruitiness and soft tannins. There is a strongly juicy element with black currant fruits adding freshness. There is a touch of spice from wood aging. Drink this enjoyable wine now.
designation: La Grande Dame du Château de Lavagnac
title: Château de Lavagnac 2011 La Grande Dame du Château de Lavagnac  (Bordeaux Supérieur)

description: Lean and austere, this is a firm, medicinal and herbal wine that's still very young. Red berry fruits, along with drying tannins and spice from wood aging hint at its aging potential. It's best to wait until 2016.
title: Château d'Aiguilhe 2011  Castillon Côtes de Bordeaux

description: Lean and austere, this is a firm, medicinal and herbal wine that's still very young. Red berry fruits, along with drying tannins and spice from wood aging hint at its aging potential. It's best to wait until 2016.
title: Château d'Aiguilhe 2011  Castillon Côtes de Bordeaux

description: Dark in color, this is a bold, spicy wine. It has firm tannins that contrast well with the dense black fruits and acidity. The combination makes for a wine that promises to age well—rich and with a fine smoky aftertaste. Drink from 2019.
title: Château Peychaud 2012  Côtes de Bourg

description: Jean-Christophe Yung is driving this family property with a crisp and refreshing wine. The wine is light, bright and lively with plenty of citrus flavors topped by spice and zesty orange, this is a mineral textured wine. Its fruit is right up front, full of acidity and rich apple flavors. Drink from late 2016.
title: Château Les Hauts de Palette 2015 Château du Barail  (Bordeaux Blanc)

description: This Mottet family wine is a blend of 44% Sémillon, 46% Sauvignon Blanc and 10% Sauvignon Gris. Soft, rounded and perfumed, this is a full fragrant wine. Its acidity is just right for the smooth texture and green-plum flavored fruits. The background is more tightly coiled with minerality and zesty lemon flavors.
title: Château la France 2015  Bordeaux Blanc

description: Aging in wood for 18 months has brought out the richness of this generous wine. It has black-currant acidity that is balanced by the tarry tannins and smoky character. Rich and now in equilibrium, this wine is ready to drink.
title: Château Hourbanon 2009  Médoc

description: The wine shows the firmly tannic structure of the vintage. It is dense, packed with dark fruits and dry tannins that are slowly developing. That makes for a rich, black-fruited wine, concentrated and needing to age further. Drink from 2018.
title: Château Bardins 2010  Pessac-Léognan

description: A rounded wine, all comfortable fruits and texture. There is a nice bite of lime juice acidity to sharpen up the gentle character, as well as some toast to add spice. An attractive, already mature wine.
designation: Chartron et Trébuchet Cuvée La Chaume
title: Maison Jean-Baptiste Béjot 2007 Chartron et Trébuchet Cuvée La Chaume  (Rully)

description: There's not too much fruit going on here; the aromas and flavors tend more towards caramel, vanilla and cinnamon, with just a faint lemon tone as a backdrop. After a kiss of softness on the palate, this wine finishes with mouthwatering crispness. Though impressive, this wine is a bit disjointed and could use a few years to integrate.
title: Josmeyer 2005 Grand Cru Brand Pinot Gris (Alsace)

description: There's not too much fruit going on here; the aromas and flavors tend more towards caramel, vanilla and cinnamon, with just a faint lemon tone as a backdrop. After a kiss of softness on the palate, this wine finishes with mouthwatering crispness. Though impressive, this wine is a bit disjointed and could use a few years to integrate.
title: Josmeyer 2005 Grand Cru Brand Pinot Gris (Alsace)

description: Does the vineyard name mean “foggy” as its etymology suggests? The wine certainly has a cool character for normally generous Volnay. But it is finely structured, the delicate tannins offering a balance to the more forward black fruits. There is a fine fresh, dry aftertaste.
title: Domaine Jessiaume 2007 Brouillards Premier Cru  (Volnay)

description: Does the vineyard name mean “foggy” as its etymology suggests? The wine certainly has a cool character for normally generous Volnay. But it is finely structured, the delicate tannins offering a balance to the more forward black fruits. There is a fine fresh, dry aftertaste.
title: Domaine Jessiaume 2007 Brouillards Premier Cru  (Volnay)

description: A broad wine, its ripe flavors fashioned with yellow fruits, toast, vanilla and an opulent texture. This is rich, open and packed with full-in-the-mouth flavors. Ready to drink.
designation: Château de Rully Cuvée Comte R. de Ternay Premier Cru
title: Antonin Rodet 2007 Château de Rully Cuvée Comte R. de Ternay Premier Cru  (Rully)

description: A broad wine, its ripe flavors fashioned with yellow fruits, toast, vanilla and an opulent texture. This is rich, open and packed with full-in-the-mouth flavors. Ready to drink.
designation: Château de Rully Cuvée Comte R. de Ternay Premier Cru
title: Antonin Rodet 2007 Château de Rully Cuvée Comte R. de Ternay Premier Cru  (Rully)

description: There is good weight here. Its richness and fruits offer light red plum textures, a dry tannic character as well as some good power. Complexity and sweetness both promote a concentrated wine.
designation: Domaine du Pavillon Clos des Maréchaudes
title: Albert Bichot 2007 Domaine du Pavillon Clos des Maréchaudes  (Corton)

description: Firm and tannic, a wine that, at this stage, is putting structure before fruit. That will change over 4–5 years as the dry tannins soften into the ripe plum and cranberry juice fruits underneath. While not weighty, this is a delicious, well-crafted wine.
title: Roux Père et Fils 2006 Les Grands Epenots Premier Cru  (Pommard)

description: A big wine, with structure and fruit. The mild tannins are a counterpoint to the harmonious red berries, acidity and dense texture. Boasts a delicious, sensuous finale. For medium-term aging.
title: Manuel Olivier 2007 Les Damaudes  (Vosne-Romanée)

description: A big wine, with structure and fruit. The mild tannins are a counterpoint to the harmonious red berries, acidity and dense texture. Boasts a delicious, sensuous finale. For medium-term aging.
title: Manuel Olivier 2007 Les Damaudes  (Vosne-Romanée)

description: Smooth and rich, a wine that seems soft rather than focused. Hints of wood add to the attraction, while pear and lychee flavors give further ripeness. It probably needs several months, or a year, to come together.
title: Maison Jessiaume 2007 Charmes Premier Cru  (Meursault)

description: From parcels of old vines in the Côte des Blancs, this limited-edition wine is a beautiful Chardonnay. It is finely woven, tightly textured and crisp in apple skin and lemon notes. Concentration from the low-yielding vines gives great depth and the potential to still age well. Drink this exceptional wine from 2017.
designation: La Vigne aux Gamins Cuvée de 3435
title: Thiénot 2004 La Vigne aux Gamins Cuvée de 3435 Chardonnay (Champagne)

description: Extra Age in the name means just that. This wine has been given more time (5 years) in bottle before release. That results in a very fine wine, a blend of 2002, 2004 and 2005 that has more depth of flavor and richness as well as showing some bottle maturity. Like all Lanson wines, it is dry although this rosé also brings out crisp red currant fruits and tight acidity. It is ready to drink.
title: Lanson NV Extra Age Brut Rosé  (Champagne)

description: Veuve Clicquot's prestige cuvée is named after the widow Clicquot, the great lady who built up the house in the early 19th century. This latest incarnation is just showing signs of ripe toasty maturity. It is rich and soft with a high dosage, in the house style, with a full panoply of lime, red apple and apricot. Drink now and until 2022.
title: Veuve Clicquot Ponsardin 2006 La Grande Dame Brut  (Champagne)

description: Made from only Grand Cru vineyards, this ripe, full and wonderfully textured wine is rich and complex. It brings out tangy orange and lemon zest, a tightly mineral texture, fragrant fruit and acidity. Dense and concentrated, the wine would benefit from some bottle age to bring out all its flavors.
title: Taittinger NV Prélude Grands Crus Brut  (Champagne)

description: The top wine from Mailly, this is rich with a good balance between its fresh white fruits streaked with lemon and its tight texture. Together, these two aspects hold the wine poised and coiled, a tight wine that is now just at maturity. Drink now and until 2022.
title: Mailly Grand Cru 2006 Les Echansons Grand Cru Brut  (Champagne)

description: With 49% Chardonnay and 51% Pinot Noir from grand cru vineyards, this well-balanced wine is just coming into its best years. Crisp and dry, following the Lanson style of no malolactic fermentation, the wine is full of white fruits, citrus and hints of toast, based around a tangy, mineral texture. Drink now and until 2025.
title: Lanson 2005 Gold Label Brut Vintage  (Champagne)

description: With 49% Chardonnay and 51% Pinot Noir from grand cru vineyards, this well-balanced wine is just coming into its best years. Crisp and dry, following the Lanson style of no malolactic fermentation, the wine is full of white fruits, citrus and hints of toast, based around a tangy, mineral texture. Drink now and until 2025.
title: Lanson 2005 Gold Label Brut Vintage  (Champagne)

description: This is a dry style of wine, with great acidity and a tightly wrought texture. As with many Gosset Champagnes, this wine has had no malolactic fermentation, enhancing the freshness and crispness as well as the structure. Full of lemon zest, crisp grapefruit and delicious acidity, it will still age for many years. Drink from 2017.
title: Gosset 2006 Grand Millésime Brut  (Champagne)

description: This is a dry style of wine, with great acidity and a tightly wrought texture. As with many Gosset Champagnes, this wine has had no malolactic fermentation, enhancing the freshness and crispness as well as the structure. Full of lemon zest, crisp grapefruit and delicious acidity, it will still age for many years. Drink from 2017.
title: Gosset 2006 Grand Millésime Brut  (Champagne)

description: With some sweetness, this red-currant-flavored wine gets its ripe feel from a hint of honey. The wine is rich, its acidity lying easily with the warm, open fruit.
title: Domaine Ernest Burn 2010 Sylvaner (Alsace)

description: With some sweetness, this red-currant-flavored wine gets its ripe feel from a hint of honey. The wine is rich, its acidity lying easily with the warm, open fruit.
title: Domaine Ernest Burn 2010 Sylvaner (Alsace)

description: The light, elegant style of this Pinot Blanc brings out its apple character and fresh acidity. It has an attractive tang of fruitiness as well as some sweetness on the finish.
title: Jean-Baptiste Adam 2011 Réserve Pinot Blanc (Alsace)

description: This is an attractive, fruity wine, expressing the spice and ripe fruit character of Pinot Gris. It is rich and full bodied, its white fruit mingles with notes of mango and ginger.
title: Hugel 2009 Classic Pinot Gris (Alsace)

description: Warm and ripe, this is a soft, green-plum- and quince-flavored wine. It is fruity, with some concentration providing a rich tang of orange zest on the finish.
title: Boeckel 2011 Mittelbergheim Vieilles Vignes Sylvaner (Alsace)

description: Warm and ripe, this is a soft, green-plum- and quince-flavored wine. It is fruity, with some concentration providing a rich tang of orange zest on the finish.
title: Boeckel 2011 Mittelbergheim Vieilles Vignes Sylvaner (Alsace)

description: Notes of ripe Russet pear dominate nose and palate. The fresh body gives full rein to these ample lively fruit flavors. Zesty tangy freshness counters the full fruit and creates a lively, harmonious, moreish and refreshing wine. The finish is dry.
title: André Kientzler 2015 Pinot Gris (Alsace)

description: This is a bright, ripe wine. It has a sense of lightness, attractive acidity and black currant flavors. This delicious, juicy wine will be ready to drink in another few months.
title: Château Rauzan Despagne 2011  Bordeaux

description: This exotic, spicy wine's wood flavors give it a lively character. This is a medium-bodied wine, not heavy in any sense, its fruitiness and attractive acidity producing a wine that will soon be ready to drink.
title: Château Larose-Trintaudon 2011  Haut-Médoc

description: This exotic, spicy wine's wood flavors give it a lively character. This is a medium-bodied wine, not heavy in any sense, its fruitiness and attractive acidity producing a wine that will soon be ready to drink.
title: Château Larose-Trintaudon 2011  Haut-Médoc

description: Even Weinbach's simplest Rieslings are full of intense flavors. This wine is floral, with flavors of white fruits along with a racy, crisp acidity. It is complex, concentrated but essentially dry.
title: Domaine Weinbach 2001 Reserve Personelle Riesling (Alsace)

description: Even Weinbach's simplest Rieslings are full of intense flavors. This wine is floral, with flavors of white fruits along with a racy, crisp acidity. It is complex, concentrated but essentially dry.
title: Domaine Weinbach 2001 Reserve Personelle Riesling (Alsace)

description: A quarter of this nonvintage blend was vinified in wood. That adds some extra richness to the already ripe fruit. Based on the 2013 vintage, the wine is full of pear, crisp apple and hints of apricot. Drink now.
title: A.R. Lenoble  NV Intense Brut  (Champagne)

description: A quarter of this nonvintage blend was vinified in wood. That adds some extra richness to the already ripe fruit. Based on the 2013 vintage, the wine is full of pear, crisp apple and hints of apricot. Drink now.
title: A.R. Lenoble  NV Intense Brut  (Champagne)

description: This tight crisp wine delivers citrus and sliced apple fruits. There is a brisk mousse that gives the wine quite a bite of acidity. All the elements point in the direction of food for this Champagne. Like many bone-dry Champagnes, this bottling needs to age, so drink from 2018.
title: A.R. Lenoble  NV Dosage Zéro Brut Nature  (Champagne)

description: This tight crisp wine delivers citrus and sliced apple fruits. There is a brisk mousse that gives the wine quite a bite of acidity. All the elements point in the direction of food for this Champagne. Like many bone-dry Champagnes, this bottling needs to age, so drink from 2018.
title: A.R. Lenoble  NV Dosage Zéro Brut Nature  (Champagne)

description: This is a floral wine with a tight nervy texture and intense acidity. Citrus fruit and crispness drive this forward. While it has plenty of fruit, it is this mineral texture that dominates this dry wine. Drink now.
designation: Grand Cru Blanc de Blancs Extra Brut
title: Legras & Haas NV Grand Cru Blanc de Blancs Extra Brut Chardonnay (Champagne)

description: Ripe rounded aspects of ripe pear and yellow apple play on the nose. The palate has an earthy touch and frothy lively fizz that boosts the fruit notes of the nose. The body is light and dry with a mouth-watering, refreshing finish that echoes long with lovely apple notes.
title: Willm NV Blanc de Noirs Sparkling (Crémant d'Alsace)

description: Bright fresh notes of greengage and lemon play on the nose. The palate has the same zippy fruit flavors which are ripe but remain resolutely fresh. The mousse is frothy and lively, accentuating the lemony brightness even more against a more mellow autolytic background. A wonderfully balanced dry fresh apéritif.
title: René Muré NV Sparkling (Crémant d'Alsace)

description: There is plenty of ripe fruit here, the richness of 2005 evident. The flavors are of ripe blackberry jam, red plums and a strong structure of sweet tannins. There is a fresh, acidity-driven juicy lift on the finish.
title: Château Sainte Barbe 2005  Bordeaux

description: There is plenty of ripe fruit here, the richness of 2005 evident. The flavors are of ripe blackberry jam, red plums and a strong structure of sweet tannins. There is a fresh, acidity-driven juicy lift on the finish.
title: Château Sainte Barbe 2005  Bordeaux

description: High toast and burnt wood are initially off-putting. The tannins in the wine are also on the smoky side. However, there is fruit here, offering some balance in this powerful, dry wine, and giving some blackberry juiciness, which gives relief from the intensity of the wood.
title: Château Lagarosse 2006 Les Comtes  (Premieres Côtes de Bordeaux)

description: Produced from Grand Cru vineyards on the Côte des Blancs, this wine, now mature, is ripe and rich. While the initial fruit has diminished, it has not forgotten its tight, mineral texture and crisp acidity. The toast flavors, now dominant, are given a final lift by hints of honeyed almonds and steely acidity.
designation: Noble Cuvée Blanc de Blancs Brut
title: Lanson 2000 Noble Cuvée Blanc de Blancs Brut Chardonnay (Champagne)

description: From a single parcel that is above the emblematic windmill of Moulin-à-Vent, this wine shows its 16 months of wood aging in its smooth and perfumed character. Cherries and freshly ground spice mix with some firm tannins to give structure while leaving room for the fruit. Drink from 2017.
title: Château du Moulin-à-Vent 2012 La Rochelle  (Moulin-à-Vent)

description: From a single parcel that is above the emblematic windmill of Moulin-à-Vent, this wine shows its 16 months of wood aging in its smooth and perfumed character. Cherries and freshly ground spice mix with some firm tannins to give structure while leaving room for the fruit. Drink from 2017.
title: Château du Moulin-à-Vent 2012 La Rochelle  (Moulin-à-Vent)

description: With some maturity, this is a rich, full-bodied wine. Its crisp fruitiness has been tempered with a more toasty, yeasty character that adds complexity. The wine has good depth, with spice and a steely minerality coming together with the fruit. Drink now.
title: Bailly-Lapierre 2012 Egarade Brut  (Crémant de Bourgogne)

description: From a great Champagne vintage year, this mature rosé is at once stylish with its toasty character, and full of life, with red fruits and bright acidity still evident. This combination makes now the perfect moment to drink this rich, dry and elegant wine.
title: Boizel 2004 Joyau de France Brut Rosé  (Champagne)

description: Marie-Amélie is the daughter of the Henriets and her cuvée is a fine blend of ripe fruits from the difficult 2010 vintage. It has a crisp element as well as fresh acidity and delicious apple juice and ripe pear flavors. A crisper element gives a balanced wine that has soft acidity at the end.
designation: Marie-Amélie Fleur de Vigne Premier Cru Brut
title: Henriet-Bazin 2010 Marie-Amélie Fleur de Vigne Premier Cru Brut Chardonnay (Champagne)

description: Marie-Amélie is the daughter of the Henriets and her cuvée is a fine blend of ripe fruits from the difficult 2010 vintage. It has a crisp element as well as fresh acidity and delicious apple juice and ripe pear flavors. A crisper element gives a balanced wine that has soft acidity at the end.
designation: Marie-Amélie Fleur de Vigne Premier Cru Brut
title: Henriet-Bazin 2010 Marie-Amélie Fleur de Vigne Premier Cru Brut Chardonnay (Champagne)

description: The hot 2003 vintage makes an interesting choice for a Vintage Champagne. This wine, with its almond and toast flavors, is certainly ripe. However it has not lost its fresh background acidity and tense texture, making it a rich wine with a fresh aftertaste. It is ready to drink.
title: Vincent Couche 2003 Millésime Brut  (Champagne)

description: This is tight, with acidity that cuts through the red fruits and perfumed raspberry flavors. It is light and bright, with minimal tannin and just a hint of structure.
title: Louis Latour 2012  Rully

description: With its pale sunset color and light raspberry flavors, this is a fresh, crisp wine. The tang of lemon zest and acidity is part of the fruitiness without dominating. Drink now.
title: Gassier 2014 Sables d'Azur Rosé (Côtes de Provence)

description: This is very smoky, with flavors of bacon as well as a yeasty character. The fruit has migrated into a taut texture, spiced with parsley and bay leaf. It's mature yet still zesty.
title: Fournier Père et Fils 2007 Grand Fumé  (Pouilly-Fumé)

description: This is very smoky, with flavors of bacon as well as a yeasty character. The fruit has migrated into a taut texture, spiced with parsley and bay leaf. It's mature yet still zesty.
title: Fournier Père et Fils 2007 Grand Fumé  (Pouilly-Fumé)

description: Dominated by minerality, this is a flinty and steel textured wine. It has some richness while remaining straight and narrow. With its structured character, it will need to age for over several years.
title: Henri Bourgeois 2010 La Demoiselle de Bourgeois  (Pouilly-Fumé)

description: Redde's top wine, named after the winery, is rounded, rich and full in the mouth. Flavors of toast and ripe pear combine with tangy acidity, producing a complex, intensely fruity wine that should age for two years.
title: Michel Redde et Fils 2010 La Moynerie  (Pouilly-Fumé)

description: This Pouilly Fumé works well, balancing the ripe yellow and pineapple fruits with toast and spice notes to give a rounded, richly textured wine. It is now mature, while retaining a fruity character on the finish.
title: Joseph Mellot 2007 La Grande Cuvée des Edvins  (Pouilly-Fumé)

description: A food friendly wine, with its finely balanced herb and green tea flavors along with pear and red apple fruits. The wine is tangy, very Sauvignon in character, packed with a lime and pink grapefruit aftertaste.
title: Château Couhins 2009  Pessac-Léognan

description: Rounded and soft, this has currant and sweet apple flavors balanced with its acidity. It is concentrated and rich, and there's still some aging potential.
title: Veuve Doussot 2006 Millésime  (Champagne)

description: With considerable acidity, this has a taut line in citrus, the greenest apple and just a touch of spice. It is not for aging, drink now.
title: Dopff & Irion 2010 Sylvaner (Alsace)

description: A wine without great varietal character, although with an attractive, light feel to it. The acidity gives a final mineral edge.
title: Domaine Specht 2009 Riesling (Alsace)

description: Soft Champagne, with a white fruit character, tasting ripe. The acidity is there, although it is unbalanced against the high dosage. The general feel is heavy.
title: Château de Bligny NV Grande Réserve Brut  (Champagne)

description: Softly fruity wine, with a touch of toast, ripe pear and melon flavors. The wine is warm, approachable, fruity, ready to drink.
title: Kuentz-Bas 2009 Tradition Pinot Blanc (Alsace)

description: A concentrated wine, although with some of the delicacy of the 1998 vintage, showing structure, tannins and ripeness. The finish is full of chocolate and sweet coffee flavors. The acidity gives a sense of elegance and lightness which suggests this will develop relatively fast.
title: Delas Frères 1998 Marquise de la Tourette  (Hermitage)

description: A concentrated wine, although with some of the delicacy of the 1998 vintage, showing structure, tannins and ripeness. The finish is full of chocolate and sweet coffee flavors. The acidity gives a sense of elegance and lightness which suggests this will develop relatively fast.
title: Delas Frères 1998 Marquise de la Tourette  (Hermitage)

description: Chapoutier has crafted a beautiful Condrieu. It may have high levels of new wood flavors, but of greater importance is the ripe Viognier, with powerful spice flavors and concentration. There is a sense of elegance as well as power which gives the wine a fine presence.
title: M. Chapoutier 2000  Condrieu

description: Alain Graillot, chemical industry executive turned farmer, is showing how good Crozes-Hermitage really can be. The 1999 vintage of his special cuvée, La Guiraude, is a powerful, but bright wine, full of red fruits and firm tannins and balancing acidity. Raisins and rich fruit join the mixture that goes to make an immediately enticing wine, but one that should age over the next 10 years.
title: Alain Graillot 1999 La Guiraude  (Crozes-Hermitage)

description: Unlike so many Condrieus, this is a wine that needs to be aged. From a parcel of land in the south end of the Condrieu appellation, this vintage is currently dominated by new wood. But under that, there is elegant, spicy fruit with delicious flavors of ripe pears and peaches. Just a hint of acidity gives it structure and considerable potential for aging.
title: E. Guigal 2000 La Doriane  (Condrieu)

description: Unlike so many Condrieus, this is a wine that needs to be aged. From a parcel of land in the south end of the Condrieu appellation, this vintage is currently dominated by new wood. But under that, there is elegant, spicy fruit with delicious flavors of ripe pears and peaches. Just a hint of acidity gives it structure and considerable potential for aging.
title: E. Guigal 2000 La Doriane  (Condrieu)

description: According to Brigitte Roch, this was an exceptional year for the domaine. With such huge concentration, heavy black tannins, fine acidity and hugely ripe fruit, it is hard to disagree. This wine, made using an old-fashioned hand-operated basket press, is full of power, yet has an astonishing elegance.
title: Domaine Clusel-Roch 1999  Côte Rôtie

description: According to Brigitte Roch, this was an exceptional year for the domaine. With such huge concentration, heavy black tannins, fine acidity and hugely ripe fruit, it is hard to disagree. This wine, made using an old-fashioned hand-operated basket press, is full of power, yet has an astonishing elegance.
title: Domaine Clusel-Roch 1999  Côte Rôtie

description: A finely perfumed wine, with powerful tannins but also excellent flavors of dark plums and ripe black fruits, with well-judged acidity and a sweet jelly character. This will develop relatively quickly for a Cornas, but still has all the right power and intensity.
title: Éric & Jöel Durand 1999  Cornas

description: The name refers as much to the brilliant green-gold color of this wine as to its richness. A tiny production from selected parcels of old Marsanne vines, this is a beautifully rich, creamy wine with a touch of honey and flavors of ripe pears.
title: M. Chapoutier 1999 De l'Orée Ermitage White (Hermitage)

description: Jaboulet bought this 7.3-acre estate in 1998, and this is the first full vintage. It is a huge wine, with all the true inky blackness and density of a Cornas. Firm, dry and concentrated, it also has generous ripe black plums, a hint of sweet jelly. It makes an excellent mix of the traditional foursquare Cornas style, with modern sophistication.
title: Paul Jaboulet Aîné 1999 Domaine de Saint-Pierre  (Cornas)

description: Apart from the fact that this wine comes from a small parcel that is itself called Saint-Joseph, the other curiosity of this wine is its label, which is designed like a banknote, by the man who used to design French francs (now, of course, out of a job). The wine inside the bottle is powerful and concentrated, flavored heavily with new wood, vanilla and spicy fruits. Guigal believes it is possible to make great Saint-Joseph, and this wine certainly proves the point.
title: E. Guigal 1999 Lieu-dit Saint-Joseph  (Saint-Joseph)

description: Only 6,000 bottles and 300 magnums have been made of this wine, from a parcel in the famed La Landonne vineyard. This is a beautifully crafted wine, with vanilla and polished violet perfumes. To taste, the ripeness of the tannins and the richness of the fruit give both complexity and elegance. It should age for at least 15 years.
title: Delas Frères 1999 La Landonne  (Côte Rôtie)

description: Only 6,000 bottles and 300 magnums have been made of this wine, from a parcel in the famed La Landonne vineyard.
